Fact.Name: Knockout Due to Being Statutory Employee
Fact.Description:
NARROWED to the DATA COMPLETENESS RESIDUE: a W-2 with the box 13 "Statutory employee" box checked whose ROUTING WAS NEVER ANSWERED. It used to read "The TP requires statutory employee forms that we don't support" and to refuse every return carrying a checked box 13; that is no longer true of the tree.
WHAT IS NOW BUILT, so the refusal is scoped to what is not. The printed instruction routes a statutory employee's box 1 to the linked Schedule C's line 1: box 1 leaves Form 1040 line 1a (/wages subtracts /statutoryEmployeeWagesRoutedToScheduleC) and line 1z (the two per filer bases subtract the two per filer sums); it lands on the linked business's line 1 (scheduleC:/scheduleCs/*/statutoryEmployeeWagesFromLinkedW2s); that business's line 31 reaches Schedule 1 line 3 and NOT Schedule SE line 2 (scheduleC:/scheduleCs/*/primaryFilerNetProfit's gate); and every earned income surface that wants the wages back takes its own printed add back line - EIC Worksheet B Part 3 (eitc:/eitcEarnedIncomeBase), Schedule 8812 line 18a worksheet line 2a with its line 2b exclusion (income:/earnedIncomeWithAllCombatPay and scheduleSE:/selfEmploymentEarnedIncomeSubjectToUsTax), Form 2441 earned income item 3 and the cdcc gates and section 129 screen (income:/primaryFilerEarnedIncomeBaseWithStatutoryEmployeeWages and its twin), IRA Deduction Worksheet line 8 (iraDeduction:/primaryFilerIraCompensation and its twin) and the IRC 63(c)(5)(B) floor (standardDeduction:/minimumStandardDeduction).
WHAT STILL REFUSES, AND IT IS A DATA STATE RATHER THAN A MISSING RULE. A W-2 whose box 13 is checked but whose box 1 DID NOT MOVE: either no Schedule C was named, or one was named on a return that does not claim Schedule C income. For those wages there is no Schedule C to carry them, so they stay on line 1a as ordinary wages and the related expenses the instruction says to report land nowhere. That is a return we must not file, and it is the correct permanent residue.
THE KEY IS THE ROUTE GATE, NOT THE LINK'S COMPLETENESS, and the difference is a real population rather than a style preference. /formW2s/*/isStatutoryEmployeeRoutedToScheduleC is All(box 13 answered and checked, the link answered, scheduleC:/claimsScheduleCIncome) - it has a THIRD conjunct, so it can be FALSE with the link perfectly answered: a statutory W-2, linked, on a return where Schedule C income is not claimed. Nothing moves on that return and it must keep refusing, and a Not(IsComplete(/formW2s/*/writableStatutoryEmployeeScheduleC)) key would ADMIT it. Keying on the gate also makes this guard read the SAME single gate the two money legs read, which is the invariant the whole build rests on.
THE Count STAYS COMPLETE. /formW2s/*/statutoryEmployee is a bare Writable, so it is kept in HEAD position: AllOperator short circuits on a Complete false head and keeps Count out of Result.Incomplete on a W-2 whose box 13 is unanswered. The second element is Complete by construction. The pre existing body already counted the bare writable and was Complete today, so this is preserved rather than introduced.
BYTE IDENTICAL ON THE COMMITTED CORPUS: no committed scenario checks box 13 (measured, 1,538 occurrences of statutoryEmployee in scenarios/, none true), so the Count is 0 either way and this guard is false on every committed return exactly as before.

Fact.Name: The filer(s) lives in a state that requests Box 14 data
Fact.Description: Whether we ask about the contents of box 14 because the integrated state tool needs it.

Fact.Name: Ask this W-2 for its box-14 RRTA amounts
Fact.Description:
The question-flow gate for the five box-14 railroad retirement (RRTA) amounts on THIS W-2 — ../RRTA_COMPENSATION, ../TIER_1_TAX, ../TIER_2_TAX, ../MEDICARE_TAX and ../ADDITIONAL_MEDICARE_TAX. True when the integrated state tool already needs box 14 (/flowStateToolNeedsBox14), OR when the filer has answered ../hasRRTACodes true for this W-2 — that second disjunct is the whole point of the fact.
WHY THIS EXISTS: THE DICTIONARY SIDE OF AN INTAKE THAT WAS ONLY EVER ASKED IN THREE STATES. /flowStateToolNeedsBox14 is Any(livedInMd, livedInNj, livedInNy), so the per-code box-14 amount questions are asked only of a Maryland, New Jersey or New York filer, because they were built for the integrated state tool rather than for Form 8959. The boolean ../hasRRTACodes is a bare Writable with no Placeholder and is asked broadly. A railroad employee in, say, Florida can therefore say "yes, this W-2 has RRTA codes in box 14" and never be asked what the amounts ARE — which is why Form 8959 Part III line 14 and Part V line 23 are unreachable outside those three states even though both lines ship (form8959:/rrtaCompensationAndTips, /rrtaAdditionalMedicareTaxWithheld). This fact is the dictionary's declaration of when those amounts must be asked for. It is a flow gate, so it is exported and carries no consumer inside the graph — the same shape /flowStateToolNeedsBox14 itself had before this fact became its first consumer, and the shape filers:/livedInNy has. That a consumerless dictionary fact already drove a real intake is the whole argument that this one can too.
A STRICT SUPERSET, DELIBERATELY. /flowStateToolNeedsBox14 is kept as a disjunct rather than replaced, so this gate can never be false where the state gate is true. A gate that narrowed the state tool's existing intake would be a retreat hidden inside an additive change, and the NY superset case pins it.
WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO, stated because the neighbouring contract's history invites the mistake: it does NOT retire either box-14 RRTA submission knockout. /flowKnockoutHasRRTACodesInBox14NotInNY and /hasABox14NYRRTAValueWeKnockout are unchanged by this unit, and the returns they refuse are refused exactly as before. This gate makes the DATA askable; the retirement additionally needs the unmodelled RRTA credit surface , which is not built.
THE RESIDUAL THIS GATE MITIGATED BUT COULD NOT CLOSE — CLOSED ON THE GRAPH SIDE, and the paragraph is kept in its original terms because the finding is the record. AS FOUND, while pinning the firing witness: ../hasRRTACodesInBox14 is All(../hasRRTACodes, ../hasBox14Codes), and outside MD/NJ/NY ../hasBox14Codes can only become true from ../writableHasBox14Codes. So a Florida filer who answered ../hasRRTACodes TRUE but left ../writableHasBox14Codes false was refused by NEITHER knockout and filed with Form 8959 line 14 at 0 — an under-stated line 17, taxpayer-favourable, witnessed by tests/nodes/ty2025/formW2s/w2-box14-rrta-intake-non-ny-codes-asks-amounts. This gate is the intake-side half of the fix (the filer is now asked the amounts, and a positive answer trips /formW2s/*/hasBox14RRTAAmount and the refusal). THE GRAPH-SIDE HALF HAS SINCE LANDED, as its own unit exactly as this paragraph said it should: /formW2s/*/hasRRTACodesReported is the unanswered-safe form of ../hasRRTACodes alone, and /flowKnockoutHasRRTACodesInBox14NotInNY's first disjunct now counts it instead of ../hasRRTACodesInBox14. The witness test above was RE-PINNED with that widening — it now asserts the refusal FIRING — so this paragraph no longer describes a live hole, only the one this gate was written beside.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Boolean; no rounding. Unanswered-safe by the All(IsComplete, value) shape its neighbour /formW2s/*/hasBox14RRTAAmount already uses, so an unanswered ../hasRRTACodes resolves Complete false rather than Incomplete and cannot spread incompleteness into the flow.

Fact.Name: This W-2's filer answered "yes, box 14 has RRTA codes"
Fact.Description:
The filer's own ../hasRRTACodes answer for THIS W-2, made unanswered-safe: true exactly when ../hasRRTACodes is both answered and true. Nothing more. It exists because a refusal must be able to key on that answer ALONE, and until recently nothing could.
WHY THIS IS NOT ../hasRRTACodesInBox14, which is the fact whose name promises this. ../hasRRTACodesInBox14 is All(../hasRRTACodes, ../hasBox14Codes) — TWO booleans — and outside Maryland, New Jersey and New York ../hasBox14Codes can only become true from ../writableHasBox14Codes, because /formW2s/*/hasInputBox14Codes is a Switch on the filer's state whose DEFAULT arm is a bare False. So a Florida railroad employee who answers "yes, this W-2 has RRTA codes in box 14" and leaves the second question false tripped NEITHER box-14 RRTA knockout and filed with Form 8959 line 14 at $0. That residual was found and recorded by the intake-gate unit, which could only mitigate it (the filer is now ASKED the amounts, and a positive answer trips ../hasBox14RRTAAmount); this fact is the graph-side half, and it is a knockout WIDENING.
THE OLD CONJUNCT IS SUBSUMED, NOT MERELY REPLACED. ../hasRRTACodesInBox14 is true only where ../hasRRTACodes is true, so every return the first disjunct refused before is still refused. tests/nodes/ty2025/formW2s/w2-box14-rrta-intake-non-ny-codes-asks-amounts is the witness for the returns that are NEWLY refused, and its assertions were deliberately FLIPPED (that file pinned the refusal at false while the residual stood); its transcript re-derives the subsumption as max(min(codes, box14Codes), codes) = codes.
../hasRRTACodesInBox14 IS LEFT EXACTLY AS IT WAS and is now consumed by nothing. It is a ty2024-l0 inherited path, so it is not deleted here — a shipping upstream path is not this unit's to remove, and its Description is unchanged so that a reader diffing against upstream still sees upstream's fact.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Boolean; no rounding. The All(IsComplete, value) shape is copied from ../hasBox14RRTAAmount and ../flowShouldAskBox14RRTAAmounts deliberately, so an unanswered ../hasRRTACodes resolves Complete FALSE rather than Incomplete and cannot carry incompleteness into flow:/flowIsKnockedOut. ../hasRRTACodes is a bare Writable Boolean with no Placeholder, so a bare Dependency here would have done exactly that. tests/nodes/ty2025/formW2s/w2-box14-rrta-intake-unanswered-complete-safe pins it.

Fact.Name: This W-2 reports a positive box-14 RRTA amount
Fact.Description:
Whether this W-2 reports a POSITIVE amount in any of the five box-14 railroad retirement (RRTA) codes — ../RRTA_COMPENSATION, ../TIER_1_TAX, ../TIER_2_TAX, ../MEDICARE_TAX and ../ADDITIONAL_MEDICARE_TAX. Those five, and only those five, are the set carried by ALL THREE state box-14 enums (/box14NYCodeOptions, /box14MDCodeOptions, /box14NJCodeOptions), which differ only in New York's extra 414_H / retirement pile; they are the railroad employer's box-14 set rather than a state-specific one, which is the same argument /formW2s/*/rrtaAdditionalMedicareTaxWithholdingUnrounded makes at length.
WHY THIS FACT EXISTS: A REFUSAL MUST KEY ON WHAT THE COMPUTATION READS, and until this fact landed it did not. /formW2s/*/rrtaCompensationUnrounded and /formW2s/*/rrtaAdditionalMedicareTaxWithholdingUnrounded read the raw box-14 writables directly, under an IsComplete/Switch wrapper and under NO boolean gate, and they reach Form 8959 lines 14 and 23. The two box-14 RRTA submission knockouts, by contrast, keyed only on BOOLEANS: /flowKnockoutHasRRTACodesInBox14NotInNY read Count(/formW2s/*/hasRRTACodesInBox14), which is All(../hasRRTACodes, ../hasBox14Codes).
THE HOLE THAT LEFT, measured on this branch rather than assumed. /formW2s/*/hasInputBox14Codes is a Switch on the filer's state whose DEFAULT arm is a bare False, so for a filer outside Maryland, New Jersey and New York no answered box-14 amount can make ../hasBox14Codes true; and ../hasRRTACodes is a bare Writable Boolean with no Placeholder. A Florida railroad employee who reports box-14 ADDITIONAL_MEDICARE_TAX of 540 and answers neither boolean was therefore NOT refused, and took the whole 540 to Form 8959 line 23, line 24 and Form 1040 line 25c while Form 8959 line 14 stayed at 0 — the RRTA CREDIT WITHOUT THE RRTA TAX, an under-collection in the taxpayer's favour. Witnessed by tests/nodes/ty2025/formW2s/w2-box14-rrta-amount-without-codes-knockout-fires, whose transcript carries both halves.
WHY NEW YORK NEEDS NO COMPANION CHANGE. That contract says /hasABox14NYRRTAValueWeKnockout "also requires the boolean first". It does not, for a New York filer: the NY arm of /formW2s/*/hasInputBox14Codes is Any(IsComplete over every NY box-14 field), so ../hasBox14Codes is ALREADY true whenever any box-14 amount is answered, and the NY twin fires on the amounts by construction — including the stale-edit shape where the filer says ../writableHasBox14Codes is false, since hasInputBox14Codes never consults it. Maryland and New Jersey get that same auto-true, but their escape hatch is ../hasRRTACodes, so they were holed exactly like the other forty-six states and are closed here with them.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Boolean; no rounding. The comparison is a STRICT GreaterThan against Dollar 0 against the cents-carrying writables, each under its own IsComplete guard — the same shape /formW2s/*/knockoutBox14NYRRTACode already uses code by code, reused deliberately so the two refusals cannot drift apart on what counts as "a box-14 RRTA amount".
TWO READINGS REJECTED, named so a later reader does not have to re-derive them. (1) GATING THIS FACT ON ../hasBox14Codes, the way /formW2s/*/hasBox14NYRRTAKnockoutCode does. That guard exists for the edit case ("the user says they don't have box 14 codes") and it is the right guard THERE, but adopting it here would preserve the hole for every filer outside MD/NJ/NY — where hasBox14Codes cannot become true from an amount at all — which is the entire population this fact was written for. The consequence is deliberate and is stated rather than hidden: a filer with a stale box-14 amount and an edited-to-false box-14 answer is now REFUSED. That is the safe direction, and it is also the consistent one, because the stale amount is already moving dollars through the two Unrounded wrappers, which consult no such guard. (2) AN IsComplete-ONLY TEST, treating any ANSWERED box-14 RRTA field as evidence. Rejected: an answered 0.00 is not an RRTA return, and refusing a filer who typed a zero would turn a containment into a nuisance. The boundary pair pins it — w2-box14-rrta-amount-boundary-zero-allows against w2-box14-rrta-amount-boundary-one-cent-refuses.
ITS REFUSAL IS RETIRED AND THIS FACT IS NOW AN EXPORTED SIGNAL, which is a change of ROLE and not of meaning — the body below is untouched, and every claim in the paragraphs above about what it measures still holds. /flowKnockoutHasRRTACodesInBox14NotInNY was rebodied down to the one residual that survives a railroad return being computable (/formW2s/*/reportsRRTAWithoutCompensation), and that predicate deliberately does NOT read this fact: this one counts RRTA_COMPENSATION and TIER_2_TAX among its five codes, and neither belongs in an "RRTA activity that needs compensation to be right" test — a positive compensation is the very thing whose absence is being refused, and a Tier 2 amount reaches no 1040 line at all. So this fact lost its in-graph consumer rather than its point. It is EXPORTED instead of deleted, for two reasons stated so the choice is checkable: deleting it would remove 997 rows from the committed conformance corpus, which a delta store cannot absorb; and "this W-2 reports a positive box-14 RRTA amount" is a real question the application can ask, the same consumer-less-but-exported shape /flowStateToolNeedsBox14 and /formW2s/*/flowShouldAskBox14RRTAAmounts already have. That is also the disposition the missing-Export cluster took, all five rows.
WORLD-1 SAFETY: this fact WIDENED a refusal while it drove one, so its only effect then was to turn returns that filed wrongly into returns that cannot file. Additive on the committed corpus: measured on this branch, NO scenario (0 of 700 fact-bearing documents) answers any of the five box-14 RRTA amounts. Five node-test fixtures do, and all five answer BOTH booleans true, so all five were already refused — but not all by THIS fact: four are non-New-York and were already refused here, while tests/nodes/ty2025/formW2s/w2-box14-rrta-yonkers is a New York return refused by /hasABox14NYRRTAValueWeKnockout, and its assert file pins this fact at Complete false both before and after the widening.

Fact.Name: This W-2 reports box-14 RRTA activity a 1040 line computes from, without the RRTA compensation that sizes it
Fact.Description:
The one predicate that survives the RETIREMENT of both box-14 RRTA submission knockouts. TRUE when this W-2 reports railroad retirement activity that a Form 1040 line is computed from — the filer answered "yes, box 14 has RRTA codes" (../hasRRTACodesReported), or box 14 carries a POSITIVE Tier 1 tax, Medicare tax or Additional Medicare Tax — while ../RRTA_COMPENSATION is not a positive reported amount. Read by /flowKnockoutHasRRTACodesInBox14NotInNY, whose whole body it now is.
WHY A REFUSAL SURVIVES AT ALL, when the retirement's premise is that the railroad computation is complete. It is complete: Form 8959 Part III lines 14-17 and Part V lines 23-24 ship (form8959:/rrtaCompensationAndTips, /additionalMedicareTaxOnRrtaCompensation, /rrtaAdditionalMedicareTaxWithheld), Schedule 3 line 11 carries its tier-1 leg in both terms (schedule3:/excessSocialSecurityTaxWithheld) and the i1040s8 Additional Medicare Tax and RRTA Tax Worksheet's employee legs, lines 8-11, reach Schedule 8812 line 21 (ctcOdc:/sched8812Line21WorksheetLine11). What is NOT complete is the DATA. Every one of those lines is measured against box-14 RRTA COMPENSATION: line 14 is the base of lines 16 and 17, and box-14 compensation is also the wage term of Schedule 3 line 11's eligibility test (schedule3:/formW2s/*/oasdiAndTier1WagesForExcessEligibility), because the W-2 instructions say boxes 3 through 7 "are not to be used to report railroad retirement compensation and taxes" so a railroad employee's box 3 is empty by printed rule. A return that reports the TAXES and withholds the COMPENSATION therefore computes wrong in both directions at once: line 17 collapses to $0 (an under-collection) and the tier-1 excess credit collapses to $0 (an under-refund). That, and only that, is what is still refused.
THE ENUMERATION THIS PREDICATE IS THE RESIDUE OF. Every shape the two retired knockouts used to refuse was walked, and each either computes correctly today or lands here. (1) RRTA COMPENSATION reported, with any of the four taxes: Form 8959 Parts III and V compute, Schedule 3 line 11 computes, Schedule 8812 line 21 computes. FILES. (2) TIER 2 tax: not claimable on this return at all ("You can't claim a refund for excess tier 2 RRTA tax on Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR. Instead, use Form 843"), and the i1040s8 flush text above worksheet line 8 excludes it by name. It reaches NO 1040 line, so a return carrying it computes correctly by claiming nothing for it. FILES — and Tier 2 is deliberately NOT one of this fact's activity disjuncts, because a Tier 2 amount needs no compensation to be right. Witnessed by tests/nodes/ty2025/formW2s/w2-box14-rrta-tier2-not-claimable-files-anyway. (3) The Form CT-2 EMPLOYEE REPRESENTATIVE, whose line-14 and line-23 alternatives this dictionary does not model: there is no CT-2 intake anywhere, so no representative amount can enter the graph, and a representative's return computes correctly on the W-2 data it does have. That is a SCOPE gap, not a data gap, and a refusal cannot close it — it is recorded on form8959:/rrtaAdditionalMedicareTaxWithheld and inside the standing oos-form8959-part-iii-rrta ledger row. FILES. (4) RRTA activity WITHOUT the compensation. This fact. REFUSED.
WHY IT IS NOT KEYED ON THE QUESTION FLOW, which is the reading a reader is most likely to expect. ../flowShouldAskBox14RRTAAmounts declares WHEN the five amounts must be asked, and it is true whenever ../hasRRTACodes is true — so gating this refusal on it would add a conjunct that is implied by the first disjunct and false for nobody it would catch. The declaration is an intake instruction for the application; the refusal is a statement about the DATA that arrived. They are deliberately separate.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Boolean; no rounding. Complete-safe in the direction this predicate needs, which is the OPPOSITE of its neighbours': ../hasBox14RRTAAmount and ../hasRRTACodesReported use All(IsComplete, value) so that an unanswered field resolves Complete FALSE and cannot refuse anybody, while this fact must FIRE on a missing compensation. It gets there without ever leaking incompleteness by negating the same idiom — Not(All(IsComplete(../RRTA_COMPENSATION), ../RRTA_COMPENSATION > 0)) — so an unanswered compensation resolves Complete TRUE rather than Incomplete, and the activity disjuncts keep the All(IsComplete, GreaterThan) shape unchanged.
TWO READINGS REJECTED, named so a later reader does not re-derive them. (1) REFUSING ONLY THE CLAIMED-AND-WHOLLY-UNANSWERED SHAPE — ../hasRRTACodesReported true AND none of the five amounts answered. Rejected because it re-opens the hole the an earlier widening closed: a filer who reports box-14 ADDITIONAL_MEDICARE_TAX of 540.00 and answers neither intake boolean would file with Form 8959 line 23 crediting 540.00 against a line 14 of $0 — the RRTA credit without the RRTA tax. Keying the activity test on the AMOUNTS as well as the boolean is what keeps tests/nodes/ty2025/formW2s/w2-box14-rrta-amount-without-codes-knockout-fires and -amount-boundary-one-cent-refuses firing across the retirement, unchanged. (2) TREATING AN ANSWERED 0.00 COMPENSATION AS AN ANSWER, i.e. Not(IsComplete(...)) rather than Not(positive). Rejected, and it is the one place this fact deliberately departs from ../hasBox14RRTAAmount's "an answered zero is a real answer" stance. The departure is justified by the conjunct it sits under: this test is only reached when the W-2 ALREADY reports RRTA activity, and a positive Tier 1 tax beside a compensation of 0.00 is not a filer declaring zero, it is a filer contradicting themselves — and it computes wrong in both directions exactly as an unanswered compensation does. The nuisance objection that sank the IsComplete-only reading on ../hasBox14RRTAAmount does not apply here, because a return with no RRTA activity never reaches this conjunct.

Fact.Name: Knockout: this return reports box-14 RRTA activity without the RRTA compensation that sizes it (⚠ the path's "NotInNY" is now HISTORY — this fires in every state)
Fact.Description:
Submission refusal for a return that reports railroad retirement (RRTA) activity a Form 1040 line is computed from while withholding the box-14 RRTA COMPENSATION that every one of those lines is measured against. Read by flow:/flowIsKnockedOut with BlockSubmissionOnTrue. The whole predicate is /formW2s/*/reportsRRTAWithoutCompensation, counted over the W-2 collection; that fact carries the enumeration, the two rejected readings and the authorities.
RETIRED AND REBODIED, WITH ITS NY TWIN, which is the change this Description now exists to explain. Until that day this fact refused the ENTIRE non-New-York railroad population — any W-2 with RRTA codes reported or any positive box-14 RRTA amount — and formW2s:/hasABox14NYRRTAValueWeKnockout refused New York's. Both refusals existed because the return would otherwise have been computed WRONG, and that reason is spent: Form 8959 Parts III and V, Schedule 3 line 11's tier-1 leg and the Schedule 8812 line-21 worksheet's employee legs all ship. A railroad return now FILES.
⚠ THE PATH NAME IS STALE AND THE STALENESS IS DELIBERATE. "NotInNY" described the old body, which carried a Not(livedInNy) conjunct because New York's returns were refused by the twin instead. The twin is retired, and the residual this fact now carries — RRTA activity reported without RRTA compensation — has NO state dimension: it is a data-completeness defect, and the five box-14 RRTA codes are identical across all three state box-14 enums. Keeping the conjunct would have left New York the one state where such a return files with Form 8959 line 14 at $0, which is precisely the hole the earlier widenings were spent closing. The alternative — renaming the path — was measured and rejected: this path resolves on all 939 committed conformance cases, so a rename is 939 REMOVED rows plus 939 added ones, blocking the delta store and buying nothing but a spelling. The reachable NY shape is pinned by tests/nodes/ty2025/formW2s/w2-box14-rrta-ny-claimed-without-compensation-refused, which is the same fixture that used to be committed under the name w2-box14-rrta-codes-only-ny-non-ny-knockout-silent asserting the OPPOSITE — the rename and the assertion flip are the record that a live New York hole was closed here, not opened.
WHAT NO LONGER FIRES, stated as a list because a retirement is judged by what it stops refusing. A railroad employee who reports box-14 compensation with any combination of Tier 1 tax, Medicare tax, Additional Medicare Tax and Tier 2 tax now files, in every state, and every dollar of it computes: witnesses tests/nodes/ty2025/formW2s/w2-box14-rrta-claimed-with-compensation-files (non-NY), -ny-value-files-after-twin-retires (New York, the twin's own retirement), and -tier2-not-claimable-files-anyway (Tier 2 reaches no 1040 line and the return claims nothing for it, which is the correct outcome rather than a refusal), plus the four tests/nodes/ty2025/schedule3/excess-oasdi-tier1-* credit witnesses and tests/nodes/ty2025/ctcOdc/sched8812line21-rrta-tier1-legs-railroad-employee, all five of which were committed asserting this refusal FIRING beside the credit they computed and are re-pinned by this unit to assert it SILENT. The end-to-end proof is a scenario rather than a node test — scenarios/units/rrr/rrr-railroad-return-files.json, the corpus's first railroad return that files, with its own committed spine.
THE REFUSAL IS PER-W-2, NOT PER-RETURN, and that is load-bearing. The count is over W-2s whose OWN compensation is missing, so a return with two railroad employers where the first reports everything and the second reports only its codes is REFUSED — line 14 would otherwise be understated by the whole of the second employer's compensation. A per-return reading ("some W-2 claims codes and no W-2 answered any amount") would let exactly that return through. Pinned by tests/nodes/ty2025/formW2s/w2-box14-rrta-mixed-second-w2-without-compensation-refused.
NO COMMITTED ROW MOVES. Measured, not assumed: /formW2s/*/hasRRTACodesReported is Complete false on every W-2 in the corpus and no scenario answers any of the five box-14 RRTA amounts, so the old body and the new one both resolve Complete false on all 939 cases, and flow:/flowIsKnockedOut is unmoved by both the rebody and the twin's unwiring. The new per-W-2 predicate's rows are pure additions.
THE HISTORY THIS REPLACES is kept below because the corrections in it are what made the retirement legible, and a reader diffing against the earlier body needs them.
WIDENED TWICE, THEN RETIRED. The second disjunct — Count(/formW2s/*/hasBox14RRTAAmount) — is what makes this refusal cover the population Form 8959 Parts III and V actually compute for. The full derivation of the hole THAT closed, why New York needed no companion change, and the two readings rejected on the way is on /formW2s/*/hasBox14RRTAAmount; the short form is that the box-14 amounts reach Form 8959 lines 14 and 23 through wrappers that consult neither intake boolean, so a filer who reported the amount and skipped the questions filed with an RRTA credit and no RRTA tax.
THE SECOND WIDENING closes the OPPOSITE hole. The first disjunct used to be the original body, character for character: a count of the W-2s whose ../hasRRTACodesInBox14 is true, which is All(../hasRRTACodes, ../hasBox14Codes) — two booleans, the second of which cannot become true outside MD/NJ/NY except from ../writableHasBox14Codes. A Florida filer who answered ../hasRRTACodes TRUE and left that second question false therefore tripped NEITHER knockout and filed with Form 8959 line 14 at $0 — the RRTA TAX WITHOUT THE RRTA CREDIT, the mirror image of the earlier hole and taxpayer-favourable. The residual was recorded by the intake-gate unit (/formW2s/*/flowShouldAskBox14RRTAAmounts), which could only mitigate it from the intake side. The first disjunct now counts /formW2s/*/hasRRTACodesReported — the unanswered-safe form of ../hasRRTACodes ALONE — which SUBSUMES the old conjunct, so nothing that was refused stops being refused. ../hasRRTACodesInBox14 is left untouched and is now consumed by nothing (it is a ty2024-l0 inherited path; removing an upstream fact was not this unit's call). Witnessed by the deliberate assertion FLIP in tests/nodes/ty2025/formW2s/w2-box14-rrta-intake-non-ny-codes-asks-amounts, against what was then the NY negative control w2-box14-rrta-codes-only-ny-non-ny-knockout-silent (a New York filer answering ../hasRRTACodes true was still NOT refused here — the Not(livedInNy) conjunct survived that widening intact, and that is exactly the hole this retirement closed by dropping the conjunct; the fixture is now committed as w2-box14-rrta-ny-claimed-without-compensation-refused) and the two silent controls w2-box14-rrta-intake-non-ny-no-codes-does-not-ask and w2-box14-rrta-intake-unanswered-complete-safe.
TWO COMMITTED RESOLVED ROWS MOVED, IN COMPLETENESS ONLY. The VALUE is false on both sides and neither return's refusal decision changes. The cause is the design choice itself: ../hasRRTACodes is unanswered on those W-2s, so the old first disjunct reached an unanswered ../writableHasBox14Codes through ../hasBox14Codes and resolved PLACEHOLDER false, while /formW2s/*/hasRRTACodesReported's All(IsComplete, value) shape resolves COMPLETE false. A submission-blocking knockout that says "definitely not refused" is a stronger statement than one that says "probably not refused", so the direction is safe.
THE BLOCKER MOVED TWICE, AND IS NOW GONE. This paragraph first named a SERVICE-owned question-flow change (invariant #7) as what kept the retirement out of reach, because /flowStateToolNeedsBox14 is Any(livedInMd, livedInNj, livedInNy) so the per-code box-14 amount questions reached only a Maryland, New Jersey or New York filer. That half was DECLARED IN THIS MODULE the same day: /formW2s/*/flowShouldAskBox14RRTAAmounts says the five box-14 RRTA amounts must be asked of any W-2 whose ../hasRRTACodes is true, in every state, and the application builds its screens against what ships here. The paragraph then named unmodelled TAXPAYER-ADVERSE credit surface — Schedule 3 line 11's tier-1 leg and the Schedule 8812 line-21 worksheet's tier-1 legs. Both landed later that day and both are witnessed (tests/nodes/ty2025/schedule3/excess-oasdi-tier1-*, tests/nodes/ty2025/ctcOdc/sched8812line21-rrta-tier1-legs-railroad-employee), which is what made this retirement possible rather than merely desirable.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Boolean; no rounding. Complete-safe by construction — the count is a CollectionSize over a Filter, so it resolves Complete on every return including one with no W-2 section at all, and the per-item predicate is complete-safe in both directions (see /formW2s/*/reportsRRTAWithoutCompensation's own TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING). The New-York exclusion this paragraph used to describe is GONE; see the stale-name warning above.

Fact.Name: Wages
Fact.Description: Box 1 of Form W-2, wages, tips, and other compensation. This is the writable optional fact. Can be left incomplete. Please use the derived fact in downstream calculations.

Fact.Name: Wages (box 1), cents preserved
Fact.Description:
Box 1 of Form W-2, wages, tips, and other compensation, AS REPORTED — cents preserved, not rounded. Complete-safe (0 when the writable is left incomplete), exactly like /formW2s/*/wages, which is now this fact wrapped in Round. Floored at zero: box 1 reports wages paid, so a negative entry is a transcription error and counts as $0 rather than being subtracted from Form 1040 line 1a; an employer reduces a box 1 it overstated on Form W-2c, never with a negative amount on a Form W-2.
This is the ADDEND fact: it is what a multi-W-2 wage total must sum. Form 1040 line 1a is exactly the kind of line i1040gi page 23 governs — "Enter the total amount from Form(s) W-2, box 1. If a joint return, also include your spouse's income from Form(s) W-2, box 1" — so "include cents when adding the amounts and round off only the total" applies, and summing already-rounded per-W-2 items is what that sentence forbids. Do NOT use this fact as a stand-in for box 1 on a printed line or in an export — it deliberately carries cents; use /formW2s/*/wages for the per-W-2 entry, /wages for Form 1040 line 1a, and income:/employerIncomeSubtotal for line 1z.
The same shape as /formW2s/*/federalWithholdingUnrounded and /formW2s/*/medicareWithholdingUnrounded — the same cents-preserved-addend fix, carried to box 1, the one member of the class whose total reaches total income and AGI.

Fact.Name: Wages
Fact.Description:
Box 1 of Form W-2, wages, tips, and other compensation. Whole dollars: this is /formW2s/*/wagesUnrounded rounded at the per-W-2 entry.
UNCHANGED IN VALUE, deliberately — same rationale as /formW2s/*/federalWithholding: this fact is a MeF export surface standing for the box-1 entry on ONE W-2, so the per-W-2 export does not move. The aggregating facts (/wages for line 1a, /primaryFilerWages and /secondaryFilerWages for the line-1z chain) are repointed at the unrounded sibling instead.

Fact.Name: Part of box 1 excluded on Form 4563 line 7 (American Samoa)
Fact.Description: The part of this W-2's box 1 that you exclude as a bona fide resident of American Samoa for the whole year: wages for work you did in American Samoa. Form 4563 line 7 includes only wages earned while you were in American Samoa, and those wages are reported on Form 4563 instead of on Form 1040 line 1a. Enter all of box 1 if you did all the work there, part of it if you worked both there and elsewhere, and leave it blank if none of this W-2 qualifies. Wages paid to you as an employee of the U.S. Government do not qualify. The amount you enter here leaves Form 1040 line 1a and is carried to Form 4563 line 7 for you, so do not enter the same wages again as a separate Form 4563 amount. An amount above box 1 counts as box 1, and a negative amount counts as zero.

Fact.Name: Part of box 1 excluded as Puerto Rico source income (section 933)
Fact.Description: The part of this W-2's box 1 that you exclude as a bona fide resident of Puerto Rico for the whole year: wages for work you did in Puerto Rico. Those wages are not reported on Form 1040 line 1a; they are part of the Puerto Rico income you excluded on Schedule 8812 line 2a. Enter all of box 1 if you did all the work there, part of it if you worked both there and elsewhere, and leave it blank if none of this W-2 qualifies. Wages paid to you as an employee of the U.S. Government do not qualify. The amount you enter here leaves Form 1040 line 1a and counts toward Schedule 8812 line 2a for you. An amount above what is left of box 1 after the American Samoa part counts as that remainder, and a negative amount counts as zero.

Fact.Name: This W-2's wages excluded on Form 4563 line 7
Fact.Description: The part of this W-2's box 1 excluded under section 931 and carried to Form 4563 line 7: the answer to ../writableAmericanSamoaExcludedWages, floored at zero and capped at box 1 (../wagesUnrounded), with cents preserved. Zero when unanswered, and zero when this box 1 is routed to a Schedule C as statutory-employee income, because that box 1 already leaves Form 1040 line 1a by that route.

Fact.Name: This W-2's wages excluded under section 933
Fact.Description: The part of this W-2's box 1 excluded under section 933 and counted in Schedule 8812 line 2a: the answer to ../writablePuertoRicoExcludedWages, floored at zero and capped at what is left of box 1 after ../americanSamoaExcludedWages, with cents preserved, so the two exclusions together never exceed box 1. Zero when unanswered, and zero when this box 1 is routed to a Schedule C as statutory-employee income.

Fact.Name: This W-2's wages excluded under section 931 or 933

Enter the total on line 25a" — i.e. the literal trigger of i1040gi page 23: "If you have to add two or more amounts to figure the amount to enter on a line, include cents when adding the amounts and round off only the total." Summing already-rounded per-W-2 items is what that sentence forbids. This is the writable optional fact. Can be left incomplete. Please use the derived fact in downstream calculations.

Fact.Name: Social security wages (box 3), cents preserved
Fact.Description:
Box 3 of Form W-2, social security wages, AS REPORTED — cents preserved, not rounded. Complete-safe (0 when the writable is left incomplete), exactly like /formW2s/*/oasdiWages, which is this fact wrapped in Round.
WHY THIS EXISTS, with the Form 4137 fill. This is the ADDEND fact. Form 4137 line 8 is "Total social security wages and social security tips (total of your Form(s) W-2, boxes 3 and 7)", which is exactly the construction i1040gi page 23 legislates for — "If you have to add two or more amounts to figure the amount to enter on a line, include cents when adding the amounts and round off only the total." Summing already-rounded per-W-2 items is what that sentence forbids, and it is the same defect verbatim: two W-2s with box 3 = 100.40 each total 200.80, so the line is 201, but Sigma round(x_i) gives 200. The unrounded-addend twin is the same remedy applied to box 5, to box 4 and to box 1.
Do NOT use this fact as a stand-in for box 3 on a printed line or in an export — it deliberately carries cents. Use /formW2s/*/oasdiWages for the per-W-2 entry, whose MeF export is unchanged by this fact's arrival.

Fact.Name: Social security tips (box 7), cents preserved
Fact.Description:
Box 7 of Form W-2, social security tips, AS REPORTED — cents preserved, not rounded. The box-7 twin of /formW2s/*/oasdiWagesUnrounded and it exists for the same reason: Form 4137 line 8 adds boxes 3 and 7 across every W-2, so both are addends and neither may be pre-rounded. Complete-safe (0 when the writable is left incomplete).
Do NOT use as a stand-in for box 7 on a printed line or in an export; use /formW2s/*/oasdiTips, whose MeF export is unchanged.

Fact.Name: Social security wages
Fact.Description: Box 3 of Form W-2, social security wages. Includes non-taxable income, and excludes income that exceeds the wage cap.

PER-EMPLOYER OASDI BASE (box 3 + box 7), capped at maxOasdiWagesOnMultipleW2sForOnePerson per W-2. §3121(a)(1)'s contribution and benefit base applies to OASDI wages, and §3121(q) puts tips in that base, so box 3 alone understates the per-employer measure whenever a W-2 carries social security tips (box 7). This fact returns the lesser of (box 3 + box 7) or maxOasdiWagesOnMultipleW2sForOnePerson, so a single employer's excess over the cap cannot be double-counted into the multi-employer excess test below.
Sums the UNROUNDED box 3 and box 7 twins (../oasdiWagesUnrounded, ../oasdiTipsUnrounded) rather than the rounded per-item facts, so this per-employer measure is not built from two already-rounded addends; the per-filer aggregators below (/primaryFilerTotalOasdiWagesForKnockout, /secondaryFilerTotalOasdiWagesForKnockout) round once, after their CollectionSum — the same addend/total shape as /formW2s/*/allocatedTips's per-filer totals.
Nothing this fact feeds refuses a return: /anyFilerExceedsMaxOasdiWages is not a member of flow:/flowIsKnockedOut, and its one surviving reader, imported:/knockoutFormW2s, carries no BlockSubmissionOnTrue. Nothing downstream of this measure moves a dollar today; schedule3's excess-OASDI credit chain duplicates this measure (its own box 3 + RRTA computation) rather than reads it.

Fact.Description:
Box 5 of Form W-2, Medicare wages and tips, AS REPORTED — cents preserved, not rounded. Complete-safe (0 when the writable is left incomplete), exactly like /formW2s/*/medicareWages, which is now this fact wrapped in Round.
WHY THIS EXISTS. This is the ADDEND fact: it is what a multi-W-2 total must sum. Form 8959 line 1 is "Medicare wages and tips from Form W-2, box 5. If you have more than one Form W-2, enter the total of the amounts from box 5", which is precisely the construction i1040gi page 23 legislates for — "If you have to add two or more amounts to figure the amount to enter on a line, include cents when adding the amounts and round off only the total." Summing already-rounded per-W-2 items is what that sentence forbids: two W-2s with box 6 = 100.40 each total 200.80, so the line is 201, but Sigma round(x_i) gives 200. Do NOT use this fact as a stand-in for box 5 on a printed line or in an export — it deliberately carries cents; use /formW2s/*/medicareWages for the per-W-2 entry and /formW2totalMedicareWages for the total.

Fact.Name: Medicare wages
Fact.Description:
Box 5 of Form W-2, Medicare wages and tips. Includes non-taxable income. Whole dollars: this is /formW2s/*/medicareWagesUnrounded rounded at the per-W-2 entry.
UNCHANGED IN VALUE, deliberately. The fix landed on the multi-W-2 TOTAL (/formW2totalMedicareWages), which now sums the cents-bearing addend fact and rounds once. The item-level Round is RETAINED here because this fact is itself a MeF export surface standing for the box-5 entry on one W-2, and a single-W-2 return is unaffected either way (Round(x) = Round(Sigma x) when there is one addend). Retaining it also keeps the export byte-identical, so the blast radius is exactly the totals.

Fact.Name: This Form W-2's box 5 is over the $200,000 per-employee withholding trigger
Fact.Description:
True when THIS ONE Form W-2's box 5 (/formW2s/*/medicareWages) is greater than /maxIndividualMedicareWages ($200,000) — the per-employee point at which the employer must begin withholding Additional Medicare Tax under IRC 3102(f)(1).
PER W-2, NOT PER RETURN, which is the whole reason it exists. The filing-status thresholds ($250,000 MFJ / $125,000 MFS / $200,000 otherwise, /medicareWagesAdditionalTaxThreshhold) are measured against the RETURN's Medicare wages; this one is measured against a SINGLE employment, and the two answer different questions. The instructions' "Who Must File" first bullet is this fact, not that threshold: Form 8959 must be filed when box 5 on any single Form W-2 exceeds $200,000, even by an MFJ couple whose combined wages never reach $250,000 and who therefore owe no Additional Medicare Tax at all. Read by /anyW2MedicareWagesOverPerEmployeeWithholdingTrigger, whose Filter predicate it is.
COMPLETE-SAFE — but NOT because of the IsComplete conjunct, which is belt and braces and is measured to be INERT: box 5 was never Incomplete to begin with. ../medicareWages is Round(../medicareWagesUnrounded), and that Switch's LAST case is a bare True arm returning Dollar 0, so a W-2 whose ../writableMedicareWages is unanswered reads box 5 as Complete $0.00. The conjunct therefore cannot change this fact's value on any representable return, and deleting it is an EQUIVALENT MUTANT — measured, not assumed: the whole form8959 corpus stays green with the IsComplete line removed, so there is no test to write for it and its absence from the mutation kill list is not a gap. It is KEPT because the consumer is form8959:/form8959RequiredForReturn — a RENDER GATE that must answer on every return, including one whose W-2 intake has not started — and it is what would hold that answer at FALSE if the zero default upstream were ever removed.

Fact.Name: Some single Form W-2 on this return has box 5 over $200,000
Fact.Description:
True when at least one Form W-2 on the return satisfies /formW2s/*/medicareWagesOverPerEmployeeWithholdingTrigger. This is the 2025 Instructions for Form 8959 "Who Must File" first bullet, made testable, and form8959's render gate (/form8959RequiredForReturn) is its only consumer.
THE IsComplete(/formW2s) CONJUNCT IS LOAD-BEARING, and it is MEASURED rather than argued. IT IS NOT that "a CollectionSize or a Filter over an UNANSWERED collection does not resolve": a Filter over an unanswered collection resolves to a PLACEHOLDER empty collection, CollectionSize of that is a Placeholder 0, and the comparison is a Placeholder false. So without the conjunct this fact does not go Incomplete — it goes PLACEHOLDER false. What the conjunct buys is the upgrade to a COMPLETE false: IsComplete(/formW2s) is Complete false on an unanswered collection, and a Complete false is absorbing in the head position of an All. That matters because this fact is a leg of a RENDER GATE, and a Placeholder leg is an answer nobody has committed to. The shape is copied verbatim from /flowKnockoutHasRRTACodesInBox14NotInNY, which learned the same lesson. Without the conjunct this fact is a Placeholder false rather than a Complete one; form8959:/form8959RequiredForReturn is a Placeholder false either way.

Fact.Name: Total Medicare Wages
Fact.Description:
The sum of box 5 (Medicare wages and tips) across every Form W-2 — Form 8959 line 1 (and, through line 4, lines 5-7; and line 20 in Part V). Whole dollars: the addends are summed WITH CENTS and the total is rounded once, at this line.
This previously read CollectionSum(/formW2s/*/medicareWages), i.e. a sum of per-W-2 amounts each ALREADY rounded to whole dollars, with no Round on the total. That is the construction i1040gi page 23 forbids: "If you have to add two or more amounts to figure the amount to enter on a line, include cents when adding the amounts and round off only the total." Two W-2s with box 5 = 100.40 each total 200.80 -> 201, but Sigma round(x_i) gave 200. The fix sums /formW2s/*/medicareWagesUnrounded (cents preserved) and rounds here. A SINGLE-W-2 return is unaffected — Round(x) = Round(Sigma x) with one addend — so only multi-W-2 returns whose box-5 cents cross a .50 boundary in aggregate move, bounded at roughly $0.50 per extra W-2 and unsigned in direction (Sigma round(x_i) can sit either side of round(Sigma x_i)).
The per-W-2 item fact /formW2s/*/medicareWages keeps its own Round and its exported value is unchanged; see that fact for why.

Fact.Name: Total Medicare tax withheld (Form W-2 box 6)
Fact.Description:
Form 8959 line 19: the sum of all Medicare tax withheld (box 6) across Form W-2s, PLUS the qualifying box-12 code B and code N amounts (/form8959Line19Box12MedicareTerms). Twin of /formW2totalMedicareWages. Used by the Form 8959 Part V withholding reconciliation. Whole dollars: the addends are summed WITH CENTS and the total is rounded once, at this line.
THE BOX-12 LEG. Until then this fact summed box 6 ALONE, which is the printed line minus its second paragraph — "Also include any uncollected Medicare tax on tips from Form W-2, box 12, code B, and any uncollected Medicare tax on the taxable cost of group-term life insurance over $50,000 (for former employees) from Form W-2, box 12, code N ... However, don't include any amounts reported on Form W-2, box 12, codes B and N, for uncollected RRTA Medicare tax" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8959.pdf, page 4). The closing exclusion is what held the term back: box 12 uses the same code for a FICA amount and an RRTA one. The discriminator that settles it, its printed grounds and its rejected alternatives are on /formW2s/*/box12MedicareTaxIsRrta. The box-12 leg is an ADDEND of this line, so it arrives WITH CENTS and this fact's single Round is still the only one — the same reading as /formW2totalMedicareWages, unchanged, and its per-code Switches make it $0 rather than Incomplete on a W-2 carrying neither code, so every committed case is byte-identical.
Identical in shape and rationale to the box-5 twin above, which carries the full reading; the form says the same thing on line 19 ("If you have more than one Form W-2, enter the total of the amounts from box 6"). Previously a bare CollectionSum over the ALREADY- rounded /formW2s/*/medicareWithholding. Single-W-2 returns are unaffected.

Medicare Wages for the primary filer: the sum of /primaryFilerW2s/*/medicareWagesUnrounded (cents preserved), rounded once at the total — matching /formW2totalMedicareWages, and avoiding the sum-of-rounded-addends shape (two W-2s at 1,000.50 each would otherwise sum to 2,002 instead of the printed 2,001).
THE PRECISE STATE: this pair's ONLY reader is /maxMedicareWagesForAnyFilerOnReturn, whose own consumer /anyFilerRequiredToPayExtraMedicareTax has been deleted, so the whole three-fact chain is retained raw material rather than a computation any return reads. The chain is dead, not absent — it still RESOLVES in every scenario, so its rows are live snapshot rows, and tests/nodes/ty2025/form8959/i8959-kathleen-liam-mfj-example.assert.tsv asserts this fact directly. The twin /secondaryFilerMedicareWages carries the same shape.
Medicare wages for the secondary filer. Carries the same shape as /primaryFilerMedicareWages; see that fact for the reason and the dead-but-resolving reader chain.
The highest medicare wages a single person on the return recieved

Fact.Name: Medicare Tax Withheld

Complete-safe (0 when the writable is left incomplete), exactly like /formW2s/*/medicareWithholding, which is now this fact wrapped in Round. Twin of /formW2s/*/medicareWagesUnrounded; see that fact for the full rationale. The addend fact for Form 8959 line 19 ("Medicare tax withheld from Form W-2, box 6. If you have more than one Form W-2, enter the total of the amounts from box 6"). Do NOT use it as a stand-in for the box-6 entry or in an export — it deliberately carries cents.

Fact.Name: Medicare tax withheld
Fact.Description:
Box 6 of Form W-2, Medicare tax withheld. Whole dollars: this is /formW2s/*/medicareWithholdingUnrounded rounded at the per-W-2 entry.
UNCHANGED IN VALUE, deliberately — same reasoning as the box-5 twin /formW2s/*/medicareWages: the item-level Round is retained because this fact is a MeF export surface standing for one W-2's box-6 entry, and the fix belongs at the TOTAL (/formW2totalMedicareWithholding), which now sums the cents-bearing addend and rounds once. The one other consumer that summed this ROUNDED item — /socialSecurityTaxesWithheld (box 4 + box 6, Schedule 8812 Part II-B) — carried the same sum-of-rounded-addends shape and was deliberately left alone at first, so as not to union two value changes, and has since been FIXED: that total now sums /formW2s/*/medicareWithholdingUnrounded and the new box-4 twin /formW2s/*/oasdiWithholdingUnrounded, and rounds once. No consumer sums this rounded item today.

Fact.Name: Allocated Tips

Fact.Name: Allocated tips (box 8), cents preserved
Fact.Description:
Box 8 of Form W-2, allocated tips, AS REPORTED — cents preserved, not rounded. Complete-safe (0 when the writable is left incomplete), exactly like /formW2s/*/allocatedTips, which is now this fact wrapped in Round.
WHY THIS EXISTS. This is the ADDEND fact: it is what a multi-W-2 box-8 total must sum before /primaryFilerAllocatedTips and /secondaryFilerAllocatedTips feed Form 4137 line 4. i1040gi's own rounding rule applies to any multi-source total on this return — "If you have to add two or more amounts to figure the amount to enter on a line, include cents when adding the amounts and round off only the total" — and summing already- rounded per-W-2 items is what that sentence forbids. Do NOT use this fact as a stand-in for box 8 on a printed line or in an export — it deliberately carries cents; use /formW2s/*/allocatedTips for the per-W-2 entry (still the MeF export and the fact /formW2s/*/causesAllocatedTipsKO reads) and /primaryFilerAllocatedTips / /secondaryFilerAllocatedTips for the per-filer totals.
The same shape as /formW2s/*/wagesUnrounded and /formW2s/*/federalWithholdingUnrounded.

Fact.Name: Allocated tips
Fact.Description:
Box 8 of Form W-2, allocated tips. You may have an amount here if you receive tips at your job, but the amount of tips you reported falls below a certain percentage of food and drink sales (typically 8%). Allocated tips will need to be included as unreported tip income, unless you have adequate records to show that you received less than the allocated amount.
This fact is a MeF export surface standing for the box-8 entry on ONE W-2 (and /formW2s/*/causesAllocatedTipsKO reads it per item), so its own value is the per-W-2 entry, same rationale as /formW2s/*/wages and /formW2s/*/federalWithholding. The aggregating facts (/primaryFilerAllocatedTips, /secondaryFilerAllocatedTips) sum /formW2s/*/allocatedTipsUnrounded instead, so a multi-W-2 total never sums already- rounded addends.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's total allocated tips from Forms W-2 box 8
Fact.Description:
The primary filer's box-8 amounts summed across only that filer's Forms W-2. Form 4137 is prepared separately for each spouse, so a return-wide W-2 sum would assign one spouse's allocated tips to the other's Form 4137. Complete-safe zero when the W-2 collection has not been initialized.
Sums /formW2s/*/allocatedTipsUnrounded (cents preserved per item) and rounds ONCE on the total, rather than summing the already-rounded per-item /formW2s/*/allocatedTips — the same whole-dollar total rule /formW2s/*/wagesUnrounded's Description quotes.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's total allocated tips from Forms W-2 box 8
Fact.Description: The secondary filer's per-spouse twin of /primaryFilerAllocatedTips, on the same unrounded-addend shape.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's attested actual unreported tips for the box-8 comparison
Fact.Description: Form 4137 line 2 less line 3, floored at zero. The shipping line-2 and line-3 facts are complete-safe to zero independently, so a supplied total-tips amount remains effective when the reported-to-employer amount is correctly absent or zero. The adequate- records exception still requires its separate explicit attestation.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's attested actual unreported tips for the box-8 comparison
Fact.Description: The secondary-filer twin of /primaryFilerActualUnreportedTipsForAllocatedTipsComparison.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's Form 4137 line-4 amount after the box-8 rule
Fact.Description:
The primary filer's actual unreported tips when adequate records are attested and a line-2 amount has been stated; otherwise the greater of actual unreported tips and W-2 box 8. An unanswered attestation takes the box-8 minimum, because the printed exception requires adequate records.
THE EXCEPTION DOES NOT DEPEND ON LINE 3. The printed condition is records alone — "unless you have adequate records to show that your unreported tips are less than the amount in box 8" — and a blank line 3 is $0 on the paper form, which form4137:/primaryFilerForm4137Line3 already resolves. Requiring an ANSWERED line 3 would charge a filer with adequate records and no tips reported to any employer on the whole box-8 figure instead of on the tips they actually received. What the exception does still require is a stated LINE 2: with no line-2 amount the comparison amount is $0 on no basis, and the box-8 floor would vanish for a return that has said nothing at all.
"STATED" MEANS EITHER SOURCE LINE 2 HAS. form4137:/primaryFilerForm4137Line2 takes the attested writable when it is answered and otherwise adds the primary filer's own line-1 column (c) rows, so this conjunct admits both: the writable being ANSWERED, or the resulting line 2 being POSITIVE. A filer whose whole statement of line 2 is the employer table is a filer who has stated it, and gating on the attestation alone would re-create the over-charge this fact's line-3 correction removed.
THE SECOND DISJUNCT IS A POSITIVE LINE 2, NOT AN ANSWERED COLLECTION, and the difference is the whole guard. An intake collection is normally INITIALIZED EMPTY — every committed scenario ships /1095As, /dividendReports and their siblings as empty collections — so IsComplete(form4137:/form4137Employers) would be TRUE on every return the moment a screen exists, and adequate-records alone would then drop the box-8 floor for a filer who has stated nothing at all. That is the case the line-2 conjunct exists to refuse. A positive line 2 is a statement in either form; an empty table is nobody's. An ANSWERED line 2 of $0 still admits the exception through the first disjunct, because a filer who wrote $0 said something.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's Form 4137 line-4 amount after the box-8 rule

Box 11 of Form W-2, non-qualified plans.
This is the writable optional fact. Can be left incomplete. Please use the derived fact in downstream calculations.

Fact.Name: Non-qualified plans
Fact.Description:
Box 11 of Form W-2, non-qualified plans. These are DISTRIBUTIONS to the employee from a nonqualified deferred-compensation plan or a nongovernmental section 457(b) plan.
This Description used to read "This compensation is excluded from box 1, but it is included in FICA wages", which is the opposite of the printed rule and would have led any successor to ADD box 11 to income and tax the same money twice. The instruction is explicit: "Report distributions to an employee from a nonqualified plan or nongovernmental section 457(b) plan in box 11. Also report these distributions in box 1" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/iw2w3--2025.pdf, page 19). Box 11 is a RESTATEMENT of amounts already in box 1, not a separate income item, and its stated purpose is administrative: "The purpose of box 11 is for the SSA to determine if any part of the amount reported in box 1 or boxes 3 and/or 5 was earned in a prior year" (line 1306). Governmental section 457(b) distributions are not here at all - they go on Form 1099-R (line 1315-1317).
NOTHING ON THE 1040 READS THIS FACT, and that is correct rather than a gap. It is carried for the MeF surface only. /flowKnockoutNonQualifiedPlans, which used to refuse any return with a positive box 11, is RETIRED for the reason above; the section 409A additional-tax population reaches the return through box 12 code Z and is still refused there.

Fact.Name: Elective deferrals subject to the IRC 402(g) limit
Fact.Description: This W-2's box 12 amounts that are elective deferrals within the meaning of IRC 402(g)(3), plus the designated Roth contributions IRC 402A(a)(1) treats as elective deferrals: code D (401(k)), code E (403(b)), code F (408(k)(6) SARSEP), code S (408(p) SIMPLE), code H (501(c)(18)(D)), code AA (designated Roth 401(k)) and code BB (designated Roth 403(b)). It is NOT the Form 8880 line 2 total (../totalDeferralsAndContributions): that total also carries code G (457(b)) and code EE (designated Roth governmental 457(b)), whose underlying deferral is a 457 deferral. A 457(b) plan has its OWN ceiling under IRC 457(b)(2), which is a plan-level maximum and is not aggregated with 402(g). CODE H IS INCLUDED, on the ground that 501(c)(18)(D) is not in the closed four-item list at IRC 402(g)(3) but Pub. 525 states it counts toward the overall limit anyway: "Amounts you defer under a section 501(c)(18) plan count toward the overall limit ($23,500 in 2025) and may affect the amount you can defer under other elective deferral plans" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p525.pdf, page 9, RIGHT column). A W-2 carrying code H 7,000 beside code D 20,000 that excluded code H would file with line 1h at $0.00 where $3,500 is owed - an UNDER-inclusion. Code H is IN the total and is NOT part of the designated-Roth carve-out below: a code-H deferral is in box 1 as wages and leaves box 1 again as the Schedule 1 deduction, which IRC 219(b)(3) caps at the lesser of $7,000 or 25% of compensation and at nothing else, so an excess attributable to code H has not already been taxed. That is the opposite of the designated-Roth codes, which are in box 1 and stay there. Reported deferrals include the IRC 414(v) catch-up contributions, which the employer reports as a single sum in the same box 12 code, so the limit compared against this total is the base limit RAISED by the catch-up allowance rather than the base limit alone. Summed per filer and compared against that limit in income:/primaryFilerElectiveDeferralsLimit402g and its secondary twin. THREE GAPS THIS TOTAL LEAVES, named here rather than left to be re-found later, each with its direction of error. (1) A SECTION 457(b) DEFERRAL OVER ITS OWN CEILING NEVER REACHES FORM 1040 LINE 1h, and that is an UNDER-inclusion. Code G is correctly outside the 402(g) aggregate - 457(b)(2) is a plan-level maximum and not one of the 402(g)(3) paragraphs - but Pub. 525 states the 457 ceiling in its own right ("your limit can be the lesser of your includible compensation or $23,500", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p525.pdf, page 9) and routes ITS excess to the same printed line ("You must include the excess deferral in your income for the year of the deferral. File Form 1040 or 1040-SR to add the excess deferral amount to earned income on line 1h.", lines 966-969). Nothing here tests a 457 deferral against a 457 ceiling, so a filer who over-defers under a governmental 457(b) plan alone files with no inclusion. It is a separate limit and a separate unit, and its missing operand is includible compensation, which this dictionary does not hold. (2) CODES F AND S CARRY DESIGNATED-ROTH AMOUNTS THAT NO W-2 FIELD SEPARATES, and that is an OVER-inclusion of exactly the kind the designated-Roth carve-out exists to prevent. A Roth SEP or Roth SIMPLE contribution is reported inside the same box 12 code as the pre-tax deferral (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/iw2w3--2025.pdf, pages 20-21), so a Roth share inside a code-F or code-S amount is already in box 1 and is nevertheless carried into the carve-out's MINUEND with no way to reach its subtrahend. The error is bounded by the Roth share of the excess and needs a W-2 field that does not exist. (3) CODE Y IS NOT A CANDIDATE AND ITS ABSENCE IS NOT AN OMISSION: it reports a section 409A nonqualified deferred-compensation deferral (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/iw2w3--2025.pdf, page 21), which is not an elective deferral under 402(g)(3) and carries no 402(g) limit. Recorded because iw2w3's code table groups Y with the deferral letters and a later reader will ask.

Fact.Name: Designated Roth contributions inside the 402(g) elective-deferral total
Fact.Description: The part of ../electiveDeferralsSubjectTo402gLimit that is a designated Roth contribution: box 12 code AA (Roth 401(k)) and code BB (Roth 403(b)). IRC 402(g)(1)(A) subjects those amounts to the limit but then withholds the gross-income inclusion for so much of the excess as does not exceed them, because a designated Roth contribution is already in box 1. Code EE is NOT here: it is the Roth leg of a 457(b) deferral, which never entered the 402(g) total in the first place. Subtracted from the excess in income:/primaryFilerExcessElectiveDeferralsOnLine1h and its secondary twin.

Fact.Name: Elective deferrals under the 402(g) limit that are not SIMPLE contributions
Fact.Description: ../electiveDeferralsSubjectTo402gLimit less its box 12 code S leg. Summed per filer, this is the discriminator for the TY2025 Form 1040 instructions’ "only SIMPLE plans" condition (that phrase is reflowed across the two-column page: "(a) $16,500 if you have only SIMPLE" then "plans, and (b) $26,500 for section 403(b)"): the filer is on the SIMPLE-only limit exactly when the per-filer total of this fact is zero and the per-filer total of ../electiveDeferralsSubjectTo402gLimit is not. KNOWN UNDER-INCLUSION, named rather than modelled: a SIMPLE retirement account that is part of a section 401(k) arrangement is reported under code D, not code S, so a filer whose only plan is such a SIMPLE reads as non-SIMPLE here and is given the higher $23,500 limit. That direction UNDER-includes income; the W-2 carries no field that distinguishes the two, so closing it needs an intake question this unit does not mint. CODE H BELONGS ON THIS SIDE OF THE DISCRIMINATOR, and the point is a MEASUREMENT rather than a tidy-up: since code H joins ../electiveDeferralsSubjectTo402gLimit and also joins this fact, a return whose ONLY deferral is code H does NOT read as SIMPLE-only - this fact is not zero beside a positive total - and takes the $23,500 overall ceiling rather than the $16,500 SIMPLE one. A section 501(c)(18)(D) plan is not a SIMPLE plan, so code H belongs here.

Fact.Name: 457(b) is governmental plan
Fact.Description: The 457(b) plan to which the filer contributed is a governmental 457(b).

Fact.Name: Box 12 code G includes employer or nonelective contributions
Fact.Description: Screen question: "Does the amount in box 12 with code G include any contributions your employer made for you (employer or nonelective contributions), rather than only amounts you chose to defer from your pay?" Help text: "Code G reports both your own elective deferrals and your employer's contributions to a section 457(b) plan. Only your own elective deferrals count toward the Retirement Savings Contributions Credit (Form 8880). Your plan statement or employer can tell you whether the code G amount includes employer contributions." Asked on a Form W-2 with a box 12 code G amount when the plan is a governmental 457(b) plan (../457bIsGovernmentalPlan Yes). A Yes on a return that qualifies for the Retirement Savings Contributions Credit refuses the return, because the elective part cannot be separated. UNANSWERED IS TREATED AS NO: the whole code G amount counts toward Form 8880 line 2, which over-credits for a filer whose code G amount includes employer money, so the question must be asked on that population.

Fact.Name: This Form W-2's governmental 457(b) code G amount mixes employer contributions into Form 8880 line 2
Fact.Description: True when this Form W-2 carries a box 12 code G amount above $0, the plan is answered as a governmental 457(b) plan (the only case in which ../totalDeferralsAndContributions adds code G to Form 8880 line 2), and the filer answered Yes to ../writableBox12CodeGIncludesEmployerContributions. COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE: every completeness test comes first in the conjunction, so an unanswered question, a No, a nongovernmental or unanswered plan type and a Form W-2 without code G all read false.

Fact.Name: Knockout: a governmental 457(b) code G amount that includes employer contributions, on a return that qualifies for the saver's credit
Fact.Description: Blocks submission when the return qualifies for the Retirement Savings Contributions Credit (saversCredits:/eligibleForSaversCredit Complete true) and at least one Form W-2's governmental 457(b) box 12 code G amount is answered as including employer or nonelective contributions. Code G reports elective deferrals and employer contributions together, Form 8880 line 2 counts only the elective deferrals, and the return does not ask for the split, so it would credit the employer's money. SCREEN: "Your Form W-2 box 12 code G amount includes contributions your employer made for you. Only the part you chose to defer from your own pay counts toward the Retirement Savings Contributions Credit, and this return cannot separate that part yet, so it cannot be filed here." COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE on a return with no Form W-2 or with the Form W-2 list unanswered, on a return that does not qualify for the credit or whose qualification is not yet decided, and on every return where no Form W-2 is answered that way.

Fact.Name: Elective deferrals under a section 408(k)(6) salary reduction SEP
Fact.Description:
Box 12, code F - elective deferrals under a section 408(k)(6) salary reduction SEP (SARSEP). SCREEN SPEC: this dollar amount is asked directly; the code F arm is not a refusal trigger on /formW2s/*/knockoutBox12Code.
QUESTION TEXT: "Box 12, code F - elective deferrals under a section 408(k)(6) salary reduction SEP" as a dollar amount on the box 12 code list for this W-2.
ASKED WHEN the filer answers yes to "does this W-2 have box 12 codes" (../writableHasBox12Codes, :3508; the derived ../hasBox12Codes at :3532 is the Any that also covers an imported W-2 already carrying box 12 entries).
HELP TEXT: a SARSEP is a salary reduction simplified employee pension - an older SEP arrangement your employer set up so you could elect to have part of your pay contributed to an IRA instead of paid to you. The printed instruction defines the letter as "Elective deferrals under a section 408(k)(6)" salary reduction SEP, and for 2025 it adds the Roth flavour: this includes "deferrals made to a Roth SEP IRA)." (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/iw2w3--2025.pdf, page 31, the box 12 code table; the same sentence appears in the code paragraph at lines 1384-1386). Copy the figure printed beside the letter F; do not compute anything and do not add the two flavours together yourself - whatever the employer printed with code F is the whole entry. A traditional SARSEP deferral is NOT in your box 1 wages; a Roth SEP deferral IS ("These contributions are" "included on Form W-2 in boxes 1, 3, and 5 (or box 14 for" railroad retirement taxes, and are reported in box 12 using "code F (for a SEP) or code S (for a SIMPLE IRA)." https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/iw2w3--2025.pdf, page 13, RIGHT column). Either way the employer has already done that split, so you enter the box 12 figure exactly as printed and change nothing about box 1.
VALIDATION: Dollar, Min $0. No maximum, and NO SCREEN-LEVEL WARNING OF ANY KIND - do not cap this box at the IRC 402(g) elective deferral limit, do not cap it at the 25 percent SARSEP limit below, and do not reject or flag an amount above either. The 25 percent test is enforced at the RETURN level by /formW2s/*/knockoutBox12Code, which routes the filer to the box 12 knockout screen; duplicating it here would fire on a half-entered W-2 whose box 1 has not been typed yet. This return does not compute that limit (see the named gap below), and the box legitimately carries a larger figure for a filer whose employer reported prior-year USERRA make-up contributions on separate box 12 lines. Not an enum.
UNANSWERED POSTURE: blank on the return, and an unanswered amount is NEVER refused. Do not require an answer. Unanswered leaves ../normalizedRoundedSarsepDeferrals complete-safe at $0 and every printed line identical to an answered $0.
WHAT THE APPLICATION SHOULD KNOW: a positive amount here USED TO end the interview at the box 12 knockout screen ALWAYS, and now does so ONLY WHEN IT EXCEEDS 25 PERCENT OF BOX 1 (the next paragraph but one gives the rule and the authority). At or below that line the filer FILES and takes the Form 8880 line 2 credit this box feeds; above it the filer still reaches the knockout screen. The screen's downstream moved because the code F arm in /formW2s/*/knockoutBox12Code NARROWED, not because this question changed. /knockoutForBox12Value stands for the SEVEN arms that remain - one of which is still this box - so a W-2 carrying any of THOSE codes still reaches the knockout screen. This paragraph is written to be read ONCE, in its current form, because this is the one Description in the module whose audience reads it and then builds a screen from it; the fuller history is on /formW2s/*/knockoutBox12Code, which is where a later author looks for it.
WHAT THE ANSWER FEEDS, AND IT IS A PRINTED LINE: FORM 8880 LINE 2, the saver's credit. ../sarsepDeferralsRounded rounds it, ../normalizedRoundedSarsepDeferrals makes it complete-safe 0, ../totalDeferralsAndContributions adds it beside the code D, E, S, AA, BB and EE deferrals and the governmental code G leg, and saversCredits sums that per filer into /primaryFilersDeferralsAndContributions and /secondaryFilersDeferralsAndContributions - Form 8880 line 2 columns (a) and (b), bound to the printed template at dictionary/pdf/2025/IRS8880/en/configuration.yml (fields f1_5[0] and f1_6[0]), whose printed caption is "Elective deferrals to a 401(k) or other qualified employer plan, voluntary employee contributions, and 501(c)(18)(D) plan contributions for 2025" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8880.pdf, page 1). IRC 25B(d)(1)(B)(i) is the authority - "(i) any elective deferrals (as defined in section 402(g)(3)) of such individual, and" (26 U.S.C. 25B, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section25B&num=0&edition=2024) - read with IRC 402(g)(3)(B), "(B) any employer contribution to the extent not includible in gross income for the taxable year under subsection (h)(1)(B)" (26 U.S.C. 402, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section402&num=0&edition=2024). The amount also reaches the MeF W-2 record through ../sarsepDeferralsNeeded and ../sarsepDeferralsRounded (dictionary/manifest/spine-registry.tsv lines 340-341) and the presentational ../hasInputBox12Codes. For example, a single filer with $30,000 of wages and $2,000 here takes a $200 saver's credit, and the same return with the same amount at code D instead takes the identical $200. It also feeds /formW2s/*/knockoutBox12Code's narrowed 25 percent arm (see the second limit below); at $2,000 on $30,000 of wages that arm is silent, because $2,000 is 6.7 percent.
NAMED GAP THE SCREEN MUST NOT PRETEND TO CLOSE: this return does not test the IRC 402(g) limit, its IRC 414(v) catch-up or the age 60-63 super catch-up, and it does not add an excess deferral to Form 1040 line 1h. Do not ask the filer whether they exceeded the limit and do not warn them from this screen. The reason is not laziness: the TY2025 Form 1040 instructions put the test over ALL PLANS and all employers, with different limits for SIMPLE plans, for section 403(b) plans under the 15-year rule and for section 457(b) participants near retirement, and with a carve-out for the designated-Roth share (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, pages 24-25 - the RIGHT column, "2025 under all plans was more than" at line 1471) - none of which this screen can see from one W-2. The same gap applies to every other box 12 deferral code (D, E, G, S, AA, BB, EE) and belongs to a unit of its own.
THE SECOND LIMIT, WHICH THIS RETURN *CAN* SEE AND DOES ENFORCE, stated so an application reader does not read the gap above as exhaustive. A SARSEP deferral is also capped at 25 PERCENT OF COMPENSATION, and Pub. 560 states the pair together: the most a participant may defer for 2025 is "year 2025 is the lesser of the following amounts." "1. 25% of the participant's compensation (limited to" $350,000, or $23,500 (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p560.pdf, page 12), with the base excluding the deferral itself - "Figuring the elective deferral. For figuring the 25% limit" "on elective deferrals, compensation doesn't include SEP" "contributions, including elective deferrals or other" "amounts deferred in certain employee benefit plans." (same file, lines 869-872). That is box 1 as issued, so the test IS computable from this one W-2, and /formW2s/*/knockoutBox12Code enforces it: a W-2 whose code F amount exceeds 25 percent of its box 1 is REFUSED at the return level, because the excess is an employee-side gross income inclusion (IRC 402(h)(2), 26 U.S.C. 402, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section402&num=0&edition=2024) that this return does not compute. THE APPLICATION MUST NOT WARN FROM THIS SCREEN: the knockout screen is the place the filer is told, and a screen-level warning would fire while box 1 is still blank.
