Fact.Name: Substantiated employee business expense reimbursements
Fact.Description:
Box 12, code L - substantiated employee business expense reimbursements. SCREEN SPEC: this dollar amount is asked directly; the code L arm is not a refusal trigger on /formW2s/*/knockoutBox12Code.
QUESTION TEXT: "Box 12, code L - substantiated employee business expense reimbursements" as a dollar amount on the box 12 code list for this W-2.
ASKED WHEN the filer answers yes to "does this W-2 have box 12 codes" (../writableHasBox12Codes, :3508; the derived ../hasBox12Codes at :3532 is the Any that also covers an imported W-2 already carrying box 12 entries).
HELP TEXT: your employer paid you a per diem or mileage allowance for business expenses and the allowance was MORE than the federal rate. Box 12 code L is only the part treated as substantiated - the nontaxable part. The rest of the allowance is already included in your box 1 wages and you do not enter it again here. The payer's instruction is "Report in box 12 only the amount treated as substantiated (such as the nontaxable part). Include in boxes 1, 3 (up to the social security wage base), and 5 the part of the reimbursement that is more than the amount treated as substantiated." (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/iw2w3--2025.pdf, page 20). Copy the figure printed next to the letter L; do not compute anything.
IF YOU FILE FORM 2106 - and only Armed Forces reservists, qualified performing artists, fee-basis state or local government officials and employees with impairment-related work expenses may (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p463.pdf, page 45, whose printed text wraps with hyphens and uses typographic apostrophes, both normalised here per this module's convention) - THIS AMOUNT IS YOUR FORM 2106 LINE 7 ENTRY: "Enter on Form 2106, line 7, the amounts your employer (or third party) reimbursed you that weren't reported to you in box 1 of your Form W-2. This includes any amount reported under code L in box 12 of Form W-2." (same file, lines 3387-3391). The Schedule 1 line 12 figure you enter elsewhere in this return (income:/writableSchedule1Line12ReservistPerformingArtistExpenses) is the RESULT of Form 2106 and must ALREADY BE NET of this reimbursement. This return does not subtract it for you, and entering a Schedule 1 line 12 amount that has not been reduced by this box 12 figure overstates your adjustment to income.
IF INSTEAD YOU FILE FORM 2106 AS AN EMPLOYEE WITH IMPAIRMENT-RELATED WORK EXPENSES - the FOURTH of the four categories named above - YOUR FORM 2106 RESULT IS A SCHEDULE A LINE 16 WRITE-IN, NOT A SCHEDULE 1 LINE 12 ADJUSTMENT, and you enter it in this return at scheduleA:/writableOtherItemizedDeductions (scheduleA.xml:5374, "Other itemized deductions - general write-in (Schedule A line 16, non-gambling)", complete-safe-wrapped as scheduleA:/otherItemizedWriteIn and summed into /otherItemizedDeductions and on into /totalItemizedDeductions) - already net of this box 12 amount, for the same reason and by the same Form 2106 line 7 arithmetic. Pub. 463 routes the fourth category there in terms: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p463.pdf, page 51, RIGHT column ("from Form 2106, line 10, on Schedule A") - "After you complete Form 2106, enter your impairment-related work expenses from Form 2106, line 10, on Schedule A (Form 1040), line 16, and identify the type and amount of this expense on the line next to line 16." The Schedule A instruction's closed line 16 list carries it, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sca.pdf, page 12 ("Impairment-related work expenses of a disabled person."), and the Schedule 1 line 12 instruction covers only the OTHER THREE categories - National Guard and reserve members who traveled more than 100 miles from home, qualified performing artists, and fee-basis state or local government officials - closing https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 93 ("For more details, see Form 2106."). This return does not perform that netting either.
Everyone else has nothing to report: Pub. 463 says that where you fully accounted to your employer, were fully reimbursed, returned any excess, and "There is no amount shown with a code L in box 12 of your Form W-2", "there is no need to show the expenses or the reimbursements on your return" (same file, lines 92-102).
VALIDATION: Dollar, Min $0. No maximum. Not an enum.
UNANSWERED POSTURE: blank on the return, and NOTHING IS REFUSED - unanswered, $0 and a positive amount all leave every printed line identical, because no printed line reads this quantity (see below). Do not require an answer. WHAT THE APPLICATION SHOULD KNOW: a positive amount here used to end the interview at the box 12 knockout screen and no longer does. The screen's downstream moved because the code L arm left /formW2s/*/knockoutBox12Code, not because this question changed; /knockoutForBox12Value now stands for the seven arms that remain (code F narrowed to the 25-percent-of-box-1 cell rather than leaving, and code P has since left this Switch too), so a W-2 carrying one of THOSE seven codes still reaches the knockout screen.
WHAT THE ANSWER FEEDS: the MeF W-2 record ONLY, through ../expenseReimbursementsNeeded and ../expenseReimbursementsRounded (dictionary/manifest/spine-registry.tsv lines 305-306), plus the presentational ../hasInputBox12Codes. IT REACHES NO PRINTED FORM 1040 LINE AND NO PRINTED SCHEDULE LINE - not Schedule 1 line 12 and not Schedule A line 16 either, because both of those hold a DIFFERENT quantity, the already-finished Form 2106 result the filer enters themself; nothing in this dictionary reads THIS leaf into any computation. The substantiated part is the remainder the payer excludes from wages under the accountable-plan rule the IRS states in the same instruction, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/iw2w3--2025.pdf, page 9, RIGHT column ("are excluded from the employee's gross income and are") - "Generally, payments made under an accountable plan are excluded from the employee's gross income and are not reported on Form W-2." IRC 62(a)(2)(A) with the accountable-plan test of IRC 62(c) (26 U.S.C. 62, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section62&num=0&edition=2024) is why the substantiated part is a WASH rather than a disallowed itemized deduction - 62(a)(2)(A) is a DEDUCTION provision and 62(c) is the accountable-plan test, so neither is itself the exclusion. And the string "code L" does not occur once in https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1040s1.pdf, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p596.pdf, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sr.pdf or https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8919.pdf. This is a pure transcription question.

Fact.Name: Excludable moving expense reimbursements paid directly to members of the Armed Forces
Fact.Description:
Box 12, code P — excludable moving expense reimbursements paid directly to a member of the U.S. Armed Forces. This is the screen spec for that intake.
QUESTION TEXT: "Box 12, code P — excludable moving expense reimbursement" as a dollar amount on the box 12 code list for this W-2.
ASKED WHEN the filer answers yes to "does this W-2 have box 12 codes" (../writableHasBox12Codes; the derived ../hasBox12Codes also covers an imported W-2 already carrying box 12 entries).
HELP TEXT: your employer paid you directly for qualified moving expenses because you are a member of the U.S. Armed Forces on active duty who moved under military orders to a permanent change of station. "The exclusion for qualified moving expense reimbursements applies only to members of the U.S. Armed Forces on active duty who move pursuant to a military order and incident to a permanent change of station." (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/iw2w3--2025.pdf, page 21.) Copy the figure printed next to the letter P; do not compute anything.
WHAT THIS AMOUNT MEANS FOR YOUR RETURN: Form 3903 (the form3903 module) nets the code P reimbursement, entered there as its line 4 (form3903:/writableForm3903Line4CodePReimbursement), against your moving expenses on its line 3. If the expenses are MORE, the difference is the Schedule 1 line 14 deduction; if the reimbursement is at least as much, the excess is taxable on Form 1040 line 1h. Form 3903 line 4 is asked on its own screen; this box does not fill it.
VALIDATION: Dollar, Min $0. No maximum. Not an enum.
UNANSWERED POSTURE: blank on the return, and NOTHING IS REFUSED — unanswered, $0 and a positive amount all leave every printed line identical, because no printed line reads this quantity directly (see below).
WHAT THE ANSWER FEEDS: the MeF W-2 record, through ../armedForcesMovingExpensesNeeded and ../armedForcesMovingExpensesRounded, the presentational ../hasInputBox12Codes, and, as an export, other modules that need to know which filer's W-2 carries code P. No printed Form 1040 line reads this box directly.

Fact.Name: Knockout Box 12 Code
Fact.Description:
Which box 12 code on this W-2 refuses the return, named so the knockout screen can tell the filer which code it was. The Switch has no default case, so on a W-2 that carries no refused code this fact is INCOMPLETE; ../hasBox12KnockoutCode is IsComplete of this fact, and /knockoutForBox12Value counts the W-2s where it holds.
SEVEN ARMS, in Switch order. Each is a residue the computed return cannot yet handle, not a refusal of the code as such: - code N (uncollected Medicare tax on group-term life insurance over $50,000) and code B (uncollected Medicare tax on tips), positive, on a W-2 whose Medicare regime is undetermined (../box12MedicareRegimeUnknown). Form 8959 line 19 is box 6 plus these two codes, "However, don't include any amounts reported on Form W-2, box 12, codes B and N, for uncollected RRTA Medicare tax" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8959.pdf, page 4), and box 12 uses the SAME code for a FICA amount and an RRTA one. /formW2s/*/box12MedicareTaxIsRrta is the discriminator; it answers on any W-2 whose box-14 RRTA surface has been answered EITHER way. Only the W-2 where neither ../hasRRTACodes nor a box-14 RRTA amount was answered is refused, because there the line-19 term falls through to the FICA reading and could credit an amount the printed line excludes. A filer who answers "no RRTA codes" files and gets the term; a railroad filer files and does not. Witnessed by tests/nodes/ty2025/formW2s/w2-box12-code-b-medicare-tips-files-after-narrowing and w2-box12-line19-regime-unknown-still-refused. - code Z (IRC 409A nonqualified deferred compensation), positive, when /nqdcDeferralsBox12CodeZBelowSchedule2Line17hFloor holds: the Schedule 2 line 17h entry is below 20 percent of the return's code Z total, the flat component IRC 409A(a)(1)(B)(i) always adds. - code T (employer-provided adoption benefits), positive, when /adoptionBenefitsBox12CodeTNotOnForm8839 holds: the code T total exceeds Form 8839 line 23, so part of the benefit has no section 137 exclusion computation behind it. - code R (employer Archer MSA contributions), positive, on two data residues: (a) a W-2 attributed to the secondary filer whose amount does not reach that filer's Form 8853 line 1 (hsa ../filer/archerMsaForm8853Line1EmployerContributions differs from /secondaryFilerTotalArcherMsaContributionsFromW2s), so the printed line 1 would say less than the W-2; and (b) a return with an Archer MSA (hsa:/archerMsaOnThisReturn) whose filer's Form 8853 line 3 limitation is not above $0, where the whole employer contribution would be priced as an IRC 4973 excess against a limitation the line 3 chart never established. The computed case files: the code R amount is Form 8853 line 1, reduces the Form 8889 line 4 HSA limitation, bars the Archer deduction the instruction bars, and taxes any excess on Schedule 1 line 8z with the IRC 4973 excise on Schedule 2 line 8. Witnessed by w2-box12-code-r-secondary-filer-w2-on-an-unmarried-return-refused, w2-box12-code-r-orphan-w2-with-msa-answered-yes-refused and tests/nodes/ty2025/hsa/archer-msa-part-i-employer-only-unanswered-vector-refuses. - code F (SARSEP elective deferrals) when the deferral exceeds 25 percent of box 1 (../writableWages), complete-safe on both operands. That is the IRC 402(h)(2)(A) gross-income inclusion ("Contributions made by an employer to a simplified employee pension with respect to an employee for any year shall be treated as distributed or made available to such employee and as contributions made by the employee to the extent such contributions exceed the lesser of", 26 U.S.C. 402, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section402&num=0&edition=2024), decidable from one W-2 because its base is compensation from that employer; the threshold takes Pub. 560's base, under which compensation does not include SEP contributions (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p560.pdf, page 12), the reading that refuses a strict superset. Below the threshold code F is a Form 8880 line 2 addend through ../totalDeferralsAndContributions and files. - code W (employer HSA contributions), positive, on a W-2 answered to the secondary filer of a return that is not married: the code W twin of code R residue (a). It tests Not(filers:/isMarried) rather than Not(isFilingStatusMFJ), so the married-filing-separately community-property population is not swept in.
CODES WITH NO ARM. Codes A and M (uncollected social security tax on tips and on group-term life insurance) are charged on Schedule 2 line 13 through /schedule2Line13UncollectedBox12Tax, which also charges codes B and N once their regime is known; code K (the IRC 4999 golden parachute excise) is the Schedule 2 line 17k entry through /schedule2Line17kGoldenParachutePaymentsTax; codes J (nontaxable third-party sick pay) and L (substantiated accountable-plan reimbursement) have no Form 1040 consequence, because the payer has already kept them out of box 1; code P (armed forces moving expense reimbursement) has no arm either. The comment at each former Switch position names the reading. The IRC 402(g) elective deferral limit is measured over all plans and employers and so is undecidable from one W-2; no per-code arm is its guard, and it is computed per filer from /formW2s/*/electiveDeferralsSubjectTo402gLimit.

Fact.Name: This W-2's Schedule 2 line 13 addend (box 12 codes A, B, M and N)
Fact.Description:
The four box-12 uncollected-tax codes on THIS Form W-2, summed: code A (uncollected social security or RRTA tax on tips), code B (uncollected Medicare tax on tips, but not Additional Medicare Tax), code M (uncollected social security or RRTA tax on the taxable cost of group-term life insurance over $50,000, former employees only) and code N (the Medicare half of the same). These are exactly the four codes Schedule 2 line 13 names — "Uncollected social security and Medicare or RRTA tax on tips or group-term life insurance from Form W-2, box 12".
CENTS PRESERVED, DELIBERATELY. This is an ADDEND of a printed entry line, not the line itself, so the i1040gi page-23 rule applies: "include cents when adding the amounts and round off only the total". The single Round sits on /schedule2Line13UncollectedBox12Tax. Same shape, and for the same stated reason, as /formW2totalMedicareWages and /primaryFilerTotalOasdiWithholding.
COMPLETE-SAFE PER CODE, which is why each of the four sits behind its own IsComplete Switch rather than being a bare Dependency. All four writables are OPTIONAL — a W-2 with no code A leaves /formW2s/*/uncollectedOasdiTaxOnTips Incomplete — and a bare four-term Add would make this fact, /schedule2Line13UncollectedBox12Tax, Schedule 2 line 21 and therefore /totalTax Incomplete for every return in the corpus. The Switch resolves an unanswered code to $0, so a W-2 carrying none of the four contributes exactly 0.00 and every committed scenario's total tax is byte-identical.
THE RRTA HALF OF THE PRINTED LINE IS NOT SEPARATELY MODELED and rides the standing oos-form8959-part-iii-rrta gap. Codes A and M say "social security OR RRTA tax" — the W-2 does not distinguish which, so a railroad filer's uncollected tier-1 tax arrives in the same box and is charged here at the same amount. That is the printed line's own behavior, not an approximation; what the RRTA gap still owns is Form CT-2, which reports no box 12 at all.

Fact.Name: Schedule 2 line 13, uncollected social security and Medicare or RRTA tax from Form W-2 box 12
Fact.Description:
Schedule 2 line 13: the sum of every Form W-2's box-12 codes A, B, M and N, rounded once here at the printed entry line. Reaches Form 1040 line 23 through taxCalculations:/line21OfSchedule2, which computes the printed "Add lines 4, 7 through 16, 18, and 19" — line 13 falls inside that "7 through 16" span.
WHY THIS LIVES IN formW2s.xml. Every Part II term in this dictionary lives in its own SOURCE-FORM module and reaches /line21OfSchedule2 from there — scheduleSE line 4, form5329 line 8, scheduleH line 9, form8959 line 11, form8960 line 12, form8889 line 17c. dictionary/ty2025/schedule2.xml holds Schedule 2 PART I only. The source form for line 13 is Form W-2 box 12, so this module is the home. (The now-deleted /sched8812Line22ScheduleTwoTerms contract's paragraph (ii) originally sent this fact to schedule2.xml and a later re-derivation corrected that; this fill follows the correction. )
ADDITIVE ON THE COMMITTED CORPUS, on a ground NARROWER than this paragraph first stated: NO COMMITTED SCENARIO ANSWERS ANY OF THE FOUR CODES, so every scenario's value here is $0 by absence rather than by refusal; and the per-W-2 addend is complete-safe $0 when no code is answered, so this line resolves Complete 0.00 on every scenario rather than going Incomplete and dragging /totalTax with it. The retired claim was that "all four box-12 codes still reach /knockoutBox12Code, /knockoutForBox12Value and flow:/flowIsKnockedOut" — codes A and M LEFT that switch in this same arc, once this fact charged them, so only B and N still refuse. The knockout was never what makes the arithmetic correct; it is what made this landing additive, and for A and M the corpus census is now what does.
DIRECTION, PER CODE SINCE THE NARROWING. For codes B and N: taxpayer-ADVERSE and now REACHABLE — this clause used to end "unreachable, a filer with a positive box-12 B or N cannot file at all", and the second narrowing of /formW2s/*/knockoutBox12Code falsified it. Such a filer now files whenever the W-2's Medicare regime is answered, and pays this tax, with the matching Form 8959 line-19 credit landing in the same unit (/form8959Line19Box12MedicareTerms) — the two directions were built together on purpose. Only the undetermined-regime W-2 is still refused. For codes A and M: taxpayer-ADVERSE and REACHABLE — such a filer now files and pays this tax, which is exactly what the retirement was proven against. Landing the charge first was still the right order: the /socialSecurityOverEitc line-22 add-back the deleted contract sequenced after it is taxpayer-FAVOURABLE, and it landed with this fact already charging, so the false allowance paragraph (ii) named never existed on the tree.

Fact.Name: This W-2's box-12 code B and N amounts are RRTA Medicare tax, not FICA
Fact.Description:
THE DISCRIMINATOR Form 8959 line 19's closing sentence needs and box 12 does not supply. Line 19 ends "However, don't include any amounts reported on Form W-2, box 12, codes B and N, for uncollected RRTA Medicare tax" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8959.pdf, page 4), and box 12 uses the SAME code for a FICA amount and an RRTA one — iw2w3's own code B says "Show the employee Medicare tax or RRTA Medicare tax on tips that you could not collect" and code N says "the amount of uncollected Medicare tax or RRTA Medicare tax on the coverage" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/iw2w3--2025.pdf, pages 19, 21). So the code cannot answer the question and something else must.
THE READING, and it is an inference across two printed documents rather than one printed sentence, which is why it carries interpretation:provisional and its rejected alternatives below. The Medicare regime is a property of the EMPLOYEE AND THE W-2, not of the box-12 entry: the uncollected tax is whichever tax the employer would have withheld from that employee, and an employee is covered by FICA or by RRTA, not both on one Form W-2. Two printed passages make that partition and put it in box 14.
(i) The W-3 "Kind of Payer" instruction, which is where the partition is stated most plainly: "CT-1. Check this box if you are a railroad employer sending Forms W-2 for employees covered under the RRTA. Do not show employee RRTA tax in boxes 3 through 7. These boxes are only for social security and Medicare information. If you also have employees who are subject to social security and Medicare taxes, send that group's Forms W-2 with a separate Form W-3 and check the '941' checkbox on that Form W-3." (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/iw2w3--2025.pdf, page 24.) A single Form W-2 therefore belongs to exactly one of the two groups.
(ii) The reporting requirement that makes membership VISIBLE on the W-2 itself: "For employees covered by RRTA tax. ... Use Form W-2, box 14, to report total RRTA compensation, Tier 1, Tier 2, Medicare (excluding Additional Medicare Tax), and any Additional Medicare Tax withheld for each employee covered by RRTA tax. Label them 'RRTA compensation,' 'Tier 1 tax,' 'Tier 2 tax,' 'Medicare tax,' and 'Additional Medicare Tax.'" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/iw2w3--2025.pdf, page 12.) Form 8959's own line 14 instruction says the same thing from the return side: "The amount of RRTA compensation for a railroad employee is reported on Form W-2, box 14" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8959.pdf, page 4).
So: box 14 carrying RRTA is the printed mark of an RRTA-covered employee's W-2, and on such a W-2 the box-12 code B or N amount is uncollected RRTA Medicare tax, which line 19 excludes by name.
WHAT THIS FACT READS, and why it is a two-disjunct Any rather than one boolean. Both disjuncts already ship and both are complete-safe. ../hasRRTACodesReported is the filer's own "yes, box 14 on this W-2 has RRTA codes" answer, made unanswered-safe; it is the BROADLY asked half — ../hasRRTACodes is a bare Writable Boolean with no state gate, which is what makes this discriminator available on every return rather than only in Maryland, New Jersey and New York. ../hasBox14RRTAAmount is a positive amount in any of the five box-14 RRTA codes; it catches the filer who reports the amounts without ticking the boolean, the exact hole /formW2s/*/hasBox14RRTAAmount was built for.
THE REJECTED ALTERNATIVES, both of which this dictionary has actually shipped at some point. (1) NO DISCRIMINATOR, adding codes B and N unconditionally: that fixes the FICA filer and breaks the railroad one, sending a railroad filer's uncollected RRTA Medicare tax into line 19, line 22 and Form 1040 line 25c as a credit line 19 tells them not to take — a FALSE ALLOWANCE, the one direction this whole unit exists to avoid. (2) NO TERM AT ALL, the pre-fill state: line 19 is box 6 alone, short by the code B and N amounts, so line 22 is short and the filer is credited with less withholding than they had — taxpayer-ADVERSE, but wrong, and it is what kept codes B and N inside /formW2s/*/knockoutBox12Code. Between a wrong credit and a wrong refusal the printed rule is available, and this fact reads it.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Boolean; no rounding. Complete-safe by construction — both disjuncts are already All(IsComplete, value) shapes, so an unanswered box-14 surface resolves this fact Complete FALSE rather than Incomplete. FALSE THEREFORE MEANS TWO DIFFERENT THINGS, which is the whole reason /formW2s/*/box12MedicareRegimeUnknown exists beside it: the filer answered "not railroad", or nobody answered at all. Read that fact, not the negation of this one, when the question is whether the regime is KNOWN.

Fact.Name: Nothing on this W-2 says whether its box-12 B and N amounts are FICA or RRTA
Fact.Description:
True when this W-2 gives the graph NO signal either way about the Medicare regime: ../hasRRTACodes is unanswered AND no positive box-14 RRTA amount is reported. It is NOT the negation of ../box12MedicareTaxIsRrta — a filer who answered "no, box 14 has no RRTA codes" makes both facts false, and that filer's regime is known.
WHY IT EXISTS: IT IS THE FENCE ON THE ONE ARM THAT POINTS THE WRONG WAY. ../uncollectedMedicareTaxBox12FicaAddend falls through to INCLUDING the box-12 amounts when ../box12MedicareTaxIsRrta is false, because an all-zero fallthrough would make line 19 short for the ordinary FICA filer, who is the population the term exists for. On the unknown-regime W-2 that fallthrough runs in the FALSE-ALLOWANCE direction: line 19 high, line 22 high, an over-credit on Form 1040 line 25c. So that population is REFUSED at submission instead — /formW2s/*/knockoutBox12Code keeps its code B and code N cases and gates them on this fact, which is what narrows the refusal from "any positive B or N" to "a positive B or N whose regime nothing on the W-2 decides".
THE RESULT, stated as the coupling it is: on a SUBMITTABLE return every W-2 carrying a positive code B or N has an answered regime, so line 19 is exactly the printed line. The fallthrough's wrong direction survives only inside an unfinished return, where it keeps line 19 Complete instead of spreading incompleteness into Form 1040 line 25c.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Boolean; no rounding. Complete-safe: both conjuncts resolve without the writable being answered.

Fact.Name: This W-2's Form 8959 line 19 addend (box 12 codes B and N, FICA only)
Fact.Description:
THIS W-2's contribution to Form 8959 line 19 beyond box 6: code B (uncollected Medicare tax on tips) plus code N (uncollected Medicare tax on the taxable cost of group-term life insurance over $50,000 for former employees), and ZERO when ../box12MedicareTaxIsRrta says those amounts are uncollected RRTA Medicare tax, which line 19 excludes by name.
CENTS PRESERVED, DELIBERATELY, exactly as /formW2s/*/uncollectedBox12TaxAddend above: this is an ADDEND of a printed entry line, not the line itself, so the i1040gi page-23 rule applies and the single Round sits at line 19 on /formW2totalMedicareWithholding.
COMPLETE-SAFE PER CODE for the same reason the Schedule 2 line 13 addend is: both writables are optional, and a bare Add would make line 19, line 22, Form 1040 line 25c and the Schedule 8812 line-21 worksheet Incomplete on every return in the corpus.
DIRECTION OF EVERY ARM, because this fact is where the unit's whole risk sits. RRTA arm (../box12MedicareTaxIsRrta true) resolves 0: line 19 unchanged, which is the printed answer — no direction. FICA arm (regime answered, not RRTA) resolves B+N: line 19 UP, line 22 up, Form 1040 line 25c up. That is a bigger credit than before, and it is the CORRECTION of a taxpayer-adverse under-credit rather than a new allowance — the printed line says to include these amounts. UNKNOWN arm (nothing answered) also resolves B+N, because the fallthrough is the FICA one; that is the false-allowance direction, and it is fenced by /formW2s/*/box12MedicareRegimeUnknown, which keeps such a return refused at submission. See that fact for the argument.

Fact.Name: Form 8959 line 19, the box-12 code B and code N terms
Fact.Description:
The box-12 half of Form 8959 line 19: every W-2's qualifying code B and code N amounts, summed WITH CENTS. Added to the box-6 total inside /formW2totalMedicareWithholding, which is this dictionary's line 19 and carries the single Round at the printed entry line.
What the contract could not settle, and what this landing settles, is the FICA/RRTA discriminator its closing sentence needs — see /formW2s/*/box12MedicareTaxIsRrta for the reading, the four printed passages it rests on and the two rejected alternatives. The contract predicted the discriminator would be "an INTERPRETATION no vendored document states"; that is right as far as it goes, and the interpretation tag says so, but the four passages narrow it to an inference rather than an invention, which is why the term ships.
JOINT RETURNS NEED NO SEPARATE TERM. The printed line says "If you are filing a joint return, also include these amounts, if any, from your spouse's Form(s) W-2" — /formW2s is the whole return's collection, both filers' W-2s in it, so a CollectionSum already includes the spouse's.
SURFACE AT LANDING, measured rather than inherited: no committed scenario answers either writable (grep over scenarios/ for uncollectedMedicareTaxOnTips and uncollectedMedicareTaxOnLifeInsuranceOver50k returns nothing, and scripts/gen_layerb_inputs.py generates neither), and the per-W-2 addend is complete-safe $0 when neither code is answered, so this fact resolves Complete 0.00 on every committed case and /formW2totalMedicareWithholding is byte-identical everywhere.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, NON-NEGATIVE (uncollected tax amounts). NOT rounded here on purpose — see the CENTS PRESERVED paragraph on the per-W-2 addend.

Fact.Name: Box 12 code W on a dependent's W-2, still refused because the filer's OWN contributions are never answered
Fact.Description:
This W-2 carries a positive box 12 code W amount and belongs to a filer who can be claimed as another taxpayer's dependent AND who has not stated that their own (non-employer) HSA contributions are $0.
NARROWED by the fourth conjunct, matching the twin hsa:/flowKnockoutFilerIsDependentAndContributesToHsa. The employer-only dependent - the population the old Name and Description described whole - now files: IRC 106(d)(1) excludes the employer's contribution for any employee who is an eligible individual under IRC 223(c)(1), which dependency does not disturb, so the amount is not an IRC 4973(g)(1) excess contribution and no 6% excise tax is owed. What survives is the dependent's OWN contribution, which IS a 4973(g)(1) excess.
NARROWED AGAIN, on the same shared conjunct as the hsa twin: the fourth conjunct is now Not(hsa:../filer/hsaDependentOwnContributionsAnswered) rather than Not(...AnsweredZero). The own-contribution excess is no longer unmodeled - it computes at hsa:/filers/*/hsaDependentOwnContributionExcess and is taxed at 6% on that filer's Form 5329 line 47 - so a dependent who ANSWERS line 2 with a positive amount files, with the tax on it. What survives on this guard is the same residual as on the twin: a line 2 that is never answered at all, which the two optional and complete-safe-to-$0.00 writables make indistinguishable from a stated zero unless answeredness itself is tested.

Fact.Name: Knockout when a dependent's box 12 code W W-2 comes with unanswered own contributions
Fact.Description: Some W-2 with a positive box 12 code W belongs to a filer who can be claimed as a dependent and who has not answered their own (non-employer) HSA contributions at all. NARROWED TWICE through its leg, ../hasBox12HsaContributionsAndDependent, whose Description carries both arguments - first freeing the employer-only dependent, then the dependent who answers line 2 with a positive amount and pays the 6% excise tax on it.

Fact.Name: Has a Box 14 NY RRTA Value We Knockout (RETIRED as a refusal 2026-08-04 — still computed, no longer read by flow:/flowIsKnockedOut)
Fact.Description:
Has the filer entered a W2 with any of the Box 14 codes we knockout.
RETIRED AS A SUBMISSION REFUSAL, by OUTRIGHT REMOVAL of its flow:/flowIsKnockedOut dependency rather than by a rebody — the coupled half of the retirement of /flowKnockoutHasRRTACodesInBox14NotInNY, because a NY-only retirement would make railroad returns filable in exactly one state. The BODY BELOW IS UNCHANGED and this fact still resolves; only the wiring is gone. Same treatment formW2s:/anyFilerExceedsMaxOasdiWages and /formW2s/*/hasRRTACodesInBox14 got: a ty2024-l0 inherited path is not deleted by a ty2025 unit, and deleting it would in any case be 939 REMOVED conformance rows for a spelling.
⚠ THIS REFUSAL WAS NEVER NEW-YORK-ONLY, and that was measured on this branch rather than inferred. /formW2s/*/knockoutBox14NYRRTACode is a Switch over the five box-14 RRTA amounts with NO state test anywhere in it, and /formW2s/*/hasBox14Codes is Any(../hasInputBox14Codes, ../writableHasBox14Codes) — the first arm is state-switched, the second is a bare Writable asked of everybody. So ANY filer, in any state, who answered "yes, this W-2 has box 14 codes" and reported a positive RRTA amount tripped this refusal, not just a New Yorker. tests/nodes/ty2025/formW2s/w2-box14-rrta-claimed-with-compensation-files is a FLORIDA return and this fact resolves Complete TRUE on it; so does -tier2-not-claimable-files-anyway, and so do the two-employer schedule3 tier-1 fixtures. That makes the successor contract's "one unit, both knockouts" coupling stronger than the contract knew when it wrote it: the argument there was that a NY-only retirement leaves the other forty-nine states refused, and the truth is worse — retiring only /flowKnockoutHasRRTACodesInBox14NotInNY would have left THIS fact still refusing Florida railroad returns, and the retirement would have moved nobody. The name is the only New York thing about it, and it is a ty2024-l0 inherited name.
WHY DELETION RATHER THAN A REBODY, which is the choice the contract reserved for this fill. This fact fires through /formW2s/*/hasBox14NYRRTAKnockoutCode, which requires IsComplete(../knockoutBox14NYRRTACode), and that Switch is Complete only on a POSITIVE box-14 amount. So this refusal's entire range is "a New York return REPORTED a box-14 RRTA amount" — precisely the data that now computes end to end (Form 8959 Parts III and V, Schedule 3 line 11's tier-1 leg, the Schedule 8812 line-21 worksheet's employee legs). There is no shape inside its range that still computes wrong, and in particular the residual that DOES survive — RRTA activity reported WITHOUT the compensation that sizes it — is by construction outside it, because an unanswered amount leaves the Switch Incomplete and this fact false. A rebody would therefore have had to invent a new predicate for it to carry, duplicating /formW2s/*/reportsRRTAWithoutCompensation behind a livedInNy split that does no work; the residual has no state dimension, so it is carried once, by /flowKnockoutHasRRTACodesInBox14NotInNY, for all fifty states. Witnesses: tests/nodes/ty2025/formW2s/w2-box14-rrta-ny-value-files-after-twin-retires (a New York railroad return that FILES with this fact still resolving Complete TRUE beside /flowIsKnockedOut false — the pair is what makes the unwiring legible) and w2-box14-rrta-ny-claimed-without-compensation-refused (New York's surviving refusal, which this fact does NOT fire on). tests/nodes/ty2025/formW2s/w2-box14-rrta-yonkers is unchanged and is deliberately not the witness: that return is also refused by /knockoutYonkersPartYear, so its /flowIsKnockedOut would have stayed true either way.
NO COMMITTED ROW MOVES: this fact is Complete false on all 939 conformance cases before and after, because no scenario answers a box-14 RRTA field, and flow:/flowIsKnockedOut's Any loses a disjunct that was Complete false everywhere.

DO NOT use this fact as a stand-in for the printed box-14 entry or in an export — it deliberately carries cents.

Fact.Name: Box 14 RRTA compensation and tips (Form 8959 line 14 addend), cents preserved
Fact.Description:
Box 14 railroad retirement (RRTA) compensation and tips AS REPORTED on this W-2 — cents preserved, not rounded, and complete-safe (0 when ../RRTA_COMPENSATION is left incomplete). The ADDEND fact form8959:/rrtaCompensationAndTips sums: Form 8959 line 14 is "Railroad retirement (RRTA) compensation and tips from Form(s) W-2, box 14" — plural Form(s) — so the same i1040gi page-23 rule that governs the box-5 and box-6 totals governs this one ("include cents when adding the amounts and round off only the total"), and this fact exists for exactly the reason /formW2s/*/medicareWagesUnrounded does.
WHY THIS WRAPPER RATHER THAN THE EXISTING ../RRTA_COMPENSATIONRounded. That fact is Round(bare Dependency) and is therefore INCOMPLETE on every W-2 that does not answer the box-14 field — which is nearly all of them, since ../RRTA_COMPENSATION is an optional Writable with no default. Summing it would make Form 8959 line 18 Incomplete on ordinary returns and propagate that through Schedule 2 line 11 into total tax. The IsComplete/Switch shape here is the module's own established answer to that (see /formW2s/*/oasdiWages and /formW2s/*/medicareWagesUnrounded); a bare Placeholder would be the completeness-contagion trap. ../RRTA_COMPENSATIONRounded keeps its MeF export role and is untouched.
DO NOT use this fact as a stand-in for the printed box-14 entry or in an export — it deliberately carries cents; use ../RRTA_COMPENSATIONRounded for the per-W-2 entry and form8959:/rrtaCompensationAndTips for the line-14 total.

Fact.Name: Box 14 Additional Medicare Tax withheld on RRTA compensation (Form 8959 line 23 addend), cents preserved
Fact.Description:
Box 14 Additional Medicare Tax WITHHELD on railroad retirement (RRTA) compensation AS REPORTED on this W-2 — cents preserved, complete-safe (0 when ../ADDITIONAL_MEDICARE_TAX is left incomplete). The addend fact form8959:/rrtaAdditionalMedicareTaxWithheld sums, for Form 8959 line 23.
WHY ../ADDITIONAL_MEDICARE_TAX IS THE RIGHT BOX-14 FIELD, argued rather than assumed because that fact's own inherited Description says only "used by New York State or City" and that prose is not evidence of what the field MEANS. All three state box-14 enums (/box14NYCodeOptions, /box14MDCodeOptions, /box14NJCodeOptions) carry the SAME five codes — RRTA_COMPENSATION, TIER_1_TAX, TIER_2_TAX, MEDICARE_TAX, ADDITIONAL_MEDICARE_TAX — and only New York adds the 414_H / retirement-system pile on top. Those five are the railroad employer's box-14 set, not a state-specific one; a state tool collects them because box 14 is where RRTA amounts live, which is the same reason Form 8959 lines 14 and 23 both point at box 14. ADDITIONAL_MEDICARE_TAX is the 0.9% withheld, which is precisely line 23's "Additional Medicare Tax withholding on railroad retirement (RRTA) compensation from Form W-2, box 14".
WHERE THE BOX-12 CODES B AND N ACTUALLY BELONG, corrected against the source rather than inherited: an earlier reading said "the instruction for line 23 also warns that box 12 codes B and N (UNCOLLECTED RRTA Medicare tax) must NOT be included here". THAT ATTRIBUTION IS WRONG. i8959 is a two-column extraction and the B/N passage is the tail of the LINE 19 instruction, not line 23's: line 19 says to include uncollected Medicare tax on tips (code B) and on group-term life insurance over $50,000 (code N) IN ADDITION to box 6, "However, don't include any amounts reported on Form W-2, box 12, codes B and N, for uncollected RRTA Medicare tax" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8959.pdf, page 4). Line 23's own instruction (lines 226-236) says only "Enter the amount of Additional Medicare Tax withheld, if any, reported on Form W-2, box 14 ... If you are filing a joint return, include your spouse's Additional Medicare Tax withheld", plus the Form CT-2 alternative for an employee representative. So this fact needs no B/N guard at all: the codes are simply not line 23's inputs.
A REAL GAP THAT PASSAGE EXPOSED, AND IS NOW CLOSED; the paragraph is kept because the disclosure is the record. AS FOUND: Form 8959 LINE 19 is supposed to be box 6 PLUS box-12 codes B and N (less the RRTA ones), and /formW2totalMedicareWithholding summed box 6 only. That UNDER-stated line 19 and so UNDER-stated line 22 — an under-credit, taxpayer-ADVERSE — for a filer with a positive box-12 B or N, and it was unreachable because those two codes were still submission knockouts. BOTH HALVES MOVED IN ONE UNIT: /form8959Line19Box12MedicareTerms adds the box-12 leg with the RRTA amounts excluded per W-2 (/formW2s/*/box12MedicareTaxIsRrta carries the discriminator's printed grounds), and /formW2s/*/knockoutBox12Code's code B and code N cases narrowed to the W-2 whose regime nothing answers. This sentence used to read "all four box-12 uncollected codes reach /knockoutForBox12Value and BlockSubmissionOnTrue"; codes A and M left /knockoutBox12Code first, and codes B and N followed for every answered-regime W-2. The same four amounts are also Schedule 2 line 13, and the clause that used to say this dictionary "does not compute at all" is history: line 13 ships as /schedule2Line13UncollectedBox12Tax and reaches taxCalculations:/line21OfSchedule2.

Fact.Name: Box 14 Tier 1 RRTA tax withheld, cents preserved
Fact.Description:
Box 14 Tier 1 railroad retirement (RRTA) tax withheld AS REPORTED on this W-2 — cents preserved, not rounded, and complete-safe (0 when ../TIER_1_TAX is left incomplete). The per-W-2 addend for Schedule 3 line 11's tier-1 leg (schedule3:/formW2s/*/oasdiWithholdingForExcessCalculation) and for the Schedule 8812 line-21 worksheet's line 8 (ctcOdc:/sched8812Line21WorksheetLine8).
WHY BOX 14 AND NOT BOX 4, which is the whole reason this fact has to exist. The W-2 instructions send a railroad employer's Tier 1 tax to box 14 — "Use Form W-2, box 14, to report total RRTA compensation, Tier 1, Tier 2, Medicare (excluding Additional Medicare Tax), and any Additional Medicare Tax withheld for each employee covered by RRTA tax" — and then say of boxes 3 through 7 that "These boxes are not to be used to report railroad retirement compensation and taxes". So a railroad employee's W-2 has an EMPTY box 4, and every computation that reads box 4 alone sees none of their tier-1 tax.
WHY THIS WRAPPER RATHER THAN ../TIER_1_TAXRounded, which is the same argument ../rrtaCompensationUnrounded makes at length: that fact is Round(bare Dependency) and is therefore INCOMPLETE on every W-2 that leaves the box-14 field blank — nearly all of them, since ../TIER_1_TAX is an optional Writable with no default. Summing it would carry incompleteness into Schedule 3 line 15, Form 1040 line 31 and Schedule 8812 line 21. The IsComplete/Switch shape here is this module's established answer (see ../oasdiWages, ../medicareWagesUnrounded, ../rrtaCompensationUnrounded); ../TIER_1_TAXRounded keeps its MeF export role and is untouched.
DO NOT use this fact as a stand-in for the printed box-14 entry or in an export — it deliberately carries cents.
TIER 2 HAS NO SUCH WRAPPER AND MUST NOT GET ONE from this reasoning. ../TIER_2_TAX is a different tax with a different refund route ("You can't claim a refund for excess tier 2 RRTA tax on Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR. Instead, use Form 843"), so its absence from every consumer is correct rather than a gap. Pinned by tests/nodes/ty2025/schedule3/excess-oasdi-tier1-tier2-excluded, whose fixture reports 9,800.00 of Tier 2 and moves line 11 by nothing.

Fact.Name: Employer contributions to an Archer MSA
Fact.Description:
Box 12, code R - employer contributions to an Archer MSA. SCREEN SPEC: ask "Box 12, code R - employer contributions to your Archer MSA" as a dollar amount on the box 12 code list for this W-2, asked when the filer answers yes to "does this W-2 have box 12 codes" (../writableHasBox12Codes at :3508; the derived ../hasBox12Codes at :3532 is the Any that also covers an imported W-2 already carrying box 12 entries). Help text: this is what the EMPLOYER put into an Archer medical savings account for the employee or the employee's spouse; it is not what the taxpayer put in themselves, which is asked separately as Form 8853 line 2 (hsa:/filers/*/writableArcherMsaOwnContributions). Copy the figure from the W-2 exactly, cents included - "Employer contributions include any amount an employer contributes to any Archer MSA for you or your spouse for 2025. These contributions should be shown in box 12 of Form W-2 with code R" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8853.pdf, page 3, RIGHT column). Validation: Dollar, Min $0, no maximum (the annual limitation is applied downstream on Form 8853 line 3, not here). UNANSWERED POSTURE: blank on the return and nothing is refused by THIS fact - ../archerMsaContributionsUnrounded folds an unanswered entry to a complete-safe $0. WHAT THE ANSWER FEEDS, and it is a whole form: the per-filer sums /primaryFilerTotalArcherMsaContributionsFromW2s and /secondaryFilerTotalArcherMsaContributionsFromW2s, which are FORM 8853 LINE 1 (hsa:/filers/*/archerMsaForm8853Line1EmployerContributions) and from there the printed Form 8853 line 1 total, Form 8889 line 4 (the HSA limitation reduction), the Form 8853 line 5 deduction bar, Schedule 1 line 8z where the contribution exceeds the limit, and the Form 5329 Part VI 6 percent excise; plus the MeF W-2 record through ../archerMsaContributionsNeeded and ../archerMsaContributionsRounded. A POSITIVE ANSWER HERE MAKES THE ARCHER MSA QUESTION MANDATORY: hsa:/flowKnockoutArcherMsaEmployerContributionWithoutMsaAnswer refuses a return that reports a code R amount and does not answer YES to hsa:/hasHsaMedicalSavingsAccountType, so the application should ask or prefill that question whenever this field is positive. NARROWED in /formW2s/*/knockoutBox12Code (see the NARROWED comment there): a positive answer no longer knocks the return out by itself, and the arm survives only on two DATA residues - the amount reaching no filer's Form 8853 line 1, and a filer's Form 8853 line 3 limitation of $0.
CENTS, AND THE MeF CONSEQUENCE THIS NARROWING UNLOCKS. The figure entered here carries cents and NOTHING ROUNDS IT ON THE WAY TO FORM 8853 LINE 1: ../archerMsaContributionsUnrounded preserves them, the per-filer sums preserve them, and hsa:/archerMsaControllingForm8853Line1Total is an Export mef="true" with no Round on it by deliberate decision (its own "CENTS ARE KEPT AND THERE IS NO Round HERE" paragraph), because Form 8889 line 4 adds Form 8853 lines 1 and 2 before printing and i1040gi page 23 puts the single Round at the printed total. Every code R return used to be knocked out, so THIS UNIT IS WHAT FIRST MAKES A CENTS-BEARING FORM 8853 LINE 1 FILABLE: the committed archer-msa-controlling-form-totals-keep-cents now files with a controlling line 1 of 120.15 and a line 2 of 600.29 going to MeF, while the rounded pair ../archerMsaContributionsRounded and hsa:/filers/*/hsaLine4ArcherMsaContributions carry the whole-dollar figures. The application must therefore accept and transmit cents in this field. Whether the MeF schema wants cents on that element is an OPERATOR question this unit names rather than answers; nothing here rounds it away in the meantime.

One W-2's box 12 code Z income under a section 409A-failing plan, cents preserved, $0 when the box was never answered. Same shape as ../adoptionBenefitsOrZero and ../goldenParachuteExciseTaxAddend.
WHAT THIS AMOUNT IS FOR. It is the addend of /nqdcDeferralsBox12CodeZ, the return-level total the code Z data-completeness residue is measured against. It is NOT an addend of any income line: the payer's own instruction already puts a code Z amount in box 1 ("The amount reported in box 12 using code Z is also reported in box 1", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/iw2w3--2025.pdf, page 21), so adding it again here would double count wages already on line 1a.

Fact.Name: Return-level box 12 code Z income under a failed section 409A plan, whole dollars
Fact.Description:
Round(CollectionSum(/formW2s/*/nqdcDeferralsOrZero)) — every W-2 on the return, whichever filer it belongs to. This is the return-level whole-dollar box 12 code Z total. Complete-safe $0 — no per-filer split, unlike /adoptionBenefitsBox12CodeT: nothing needs one, because Schedule 2 line 17h is a single return-level entry, not per spouse.
THIS IS NOT THE OPERAND /nqdcDeferralsBox12CodeZBelowSchedule2Line17hFloor multiplies by 20 percent. That residue reads the cents-preserving CollectionSum directly and rounds once, at the end of the 20 percent multiplication, rather than taking 20 percent of THIS already-rounded whole-dollar total. Rounding twice would compound error and, because 20 percent of a whole-dollar integer can never itself land on an exact half-cent, would make this fact's own Round boundary unreachable by any fixture — no whole-dollar Z ever makes 0.2 times Z end in exactly .50. This fact is kept as the plain whole-dollar return-level total for its own sake (the code T aggregate shape) even though nothing else in the tree consumes it today.

Fact.Name: The return's box 12 code Z total exceeds the 20 percent statutory floor of Schedule 2 line 17h
Fact.Description:
True when Round(20 percent of the cents-preserving box 12 code Z total) is GREATER than schedule2:/schedule2Line17hSection409ANonqualifiedDeferredCompensation. This is the data-completeness residue /formW2s/*/knockoutBox12Code keeps refusing for code Z, once the federal consequence of code Z was confirmed already built (schedule2:/line18OfSchedule2 already carries the line 17h addend, wired into taxCalculations:/line21OfSchedule2 — see dictionary/ty2025/taxCalculations.xml:3147).
THE RIGHT OPERAND WAS A DUPLICATE AND IS RETIRED. The first landing minted its own complete-safe wrapper, /schedule2Line17hSection409ATaxOrZero, on the false premise that "the schedule2 writable itself is a bare Writable and this module has no grant to add an OrZero wrapper where it lives." schedule2.xml already carried exactly that wrapper — unexported — at /schedule2Line17hSection409ANonqualifiedDeferredCompensation (schedule2.xml:263, the very addend /line18OfSchedule2 itself reads). The duplicate is gone; this fact now reads that fact directly, exported for this one cross-module read.
WHY A FLOOR AND NOT A BARE COMPLETENESS CHECK. IRC 409A(a)(1)(B)(i) prices the additional tax as interest PLUS 20 percent of the includible amount; the interest component depends on the year the "deferred compensation" was first no longer subject to a substantial risk of forfeiture, a fact no W-2 box carries and this dictionary does not compute (Form 2210's underpayment-interest shape is the same kind of self-attested residue elsewhere in this tree). But the 20 percent term has NO such dependency — it is a flat rate on a number this W-2 collection already totals — so it is a computable LOWER BOUND on line 17h whenever any W-2 reports a positive code Z amount. A line 17h entry strictly below that floor is therefore never merely "a smaller correct tax"; it is either an unanswered question (the wrapper defaulted to $0) or an entry that omits the flat 20 percent component the statute always adds, and either state is the "unanswered or contradictory intake" a narrowing is required to keep refusing. This is the code T shape (/adoptionBenefitsBox12CodeTNotOnForm8839) applied to a rate instead of a 1:1 cross-check, chosen over a bare Not(IsComplete(...)) precisely because IsComplete alone would ADMIT an answered $0.00 against a positive code Z total — a contradictory intake this fact must not let through.
ONE-DIRECTIONAL, DELIBERATELY. Line 17h GREATER than the floor is not refused: it correctly includes the interest component 409A(a)(1)(B)(i)(I) adds, or a Form 1099-MISC box 15 amount this dictionary does not total (the printed line also reaches that source).
"WHOLE DOLLARS ON BOTH SIDES ... a cents difference can never trip this refusal" WAS WRONG AND IS WITHDRAWN. Schedule 2 line 17h is a bare Dollar writable with no forced rounding — the filer can and does enter cents — and this module's own boundary-below-floor fixture proves a one-CENT difference trips the refusal ($199.99 against a $200.00 floor refuses; $200.00 does not). The LEFT operand is the one that mostly lands on whole or tenths-of-a-dollar values (20 percent of a whole-dollar per-W-2 sum), but even that is not guaranteed once cents-bearing per-W-2 amounts are summed before the one Round — see w2-box12-code-z-boundary-half-dollar-rounds, which pins the engine's actual behavior at an exact $.50 pre-round value rather than assuming a rounding mode.
COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE: both operands are complete-safe $0, so this is Complete false on every return that reports no code Z — which is every committed scenario (zero occurrences of nqdcDeferrals in scenarios/, verified with an untruncated grep, corrections #1 and #8) — and why no committed return's knockout state moves.

Fact.Name: Statutory employee
Fact.Description: Whether statutory employee is checked in box 13. Form W-2 box 13 (Statutory employee, retirement plan, third-party sick pay checkboxes).

Fact.Name: Which Schedule C this statutory employee W-2's box 1 is reported on
Fact.Description:
The /scheduleCs item that reports THIS W-2's box 1 as its Schedule C line 1, on a W-2 whose box 13 "Statutory employee" checkbox is set. The per W-2 half of the routing the Schedule C instructions print: enter the box 1 amount on line 1 of Schedule C and check the box on that line.
OPTIONAL AND DELIBERATELY UN PLACEHOLDERED, the same call qbi:/qualifiedBusinesses/*/linkedScheduleC makes and for the same reason: nearly every W-2 is an ordinary W-2 with no Schedule C behind it, so an unanswered link is the common and legitimate state, and a default would INVENT a routing rather than record one. Every consumer gates on IsComplete of this link before comparing it (../isStatutoryEmployeeRoutedToScheduleC below is that gate), so an unanswered link supplies nothing rather than a plausible zero.
WHY A CollectionItem AND NOT A BOOLEAN: the two Schedules C rule. A filer with both self employment income and statutory employee income must file TWO Schedules C and may not combine them, so the successor to the guard cannot be a flag that says only THAT the wages are statutory; it has to say WHICH business they land on. That is what this holds, and scheduleC:/scheduleCs/*/statutoryEmployeeWagesFromLinkedW2s reads it back per business.
NO CONSISTENCY GUARD ON THE TARGET'S OWNER. Nothing here checks that the linked Schedule C belongs to the same filer as the W-2. Schedule SE is where that would matter and a statutory employee Schedule C reaches no Schedule SE at all (scheduleC:/scheduleCs/*/primaryFilerNetProfit and its secondary twin zero it), so a cross owner link cannot move self employment tax to the wrong spouse. It is named here so a later unit does not read the silence as an oversight.

Fact.Name: This W-2's box 1 is routed to a Schedule C as statutory employee income
Fact.Description:
True when box 13 is answered CHECKED, ../writableStatutoryEmployeeScheduleC names a Schedule C, and the return actually claims Schedule C income. The gate every other fact in this route reads, and the reason the route can never take money off Form 1040 line 1a without putting it somewhere: all three must hold before a dollar moves.
THE THIRD CONJUNCT IS NOT BELT AND BRACES. scheduleC:/scheduleCs/*/scheduleCGrossIncome is a Switch on scheduleC:/claimsScheduleCIncome whose false arm is a Complete $0, so on a return that carries /scheduleCs items while /hasScheduleCIncome is unanswered the Schedule C leg would be $0 while /wages still subtracted the same wages, and the box 1 amount would land on no line at all. Both sides read THIS fact, so they can only move together.
TYPE: Boolean, ALWAYS Complete, and that is load bearing rather than tidy. It is read in HEAD position of the All inside scheduleC's Count and CollectionSum over /formW2s, and both aggregates return Incomplete outright on ANY Incomplete element; ../statutoryEmployee is a bare Writable and ../writableStatutoryEmployeeScheduleC is deliberately un Placeholdered, so a bare read of either inside those aggregates would go Incomplete on every ordinary return. AllOperator short circuits on a Complete false head, so the two IsComplete conjuncts collapse the term before anything unanswered is forced. Same construction, and the same engine argument, as qbi:/scheduleCs/*/qbiIsDuplicatedAttributionTarget's derivation gate.
UNANSWERED BOX 13 MEANS NOT ROUTED, which is the pre existing behaviour exactly: no committed scenario checks box 13, so this resolves Complete false on every one of them and no committed figure moves.

Fact.Name: This W-2's box 1, when it is routed to a Schedule C (the amount that moves)
Fact.Description:
THE DOLLAR THE CONTRACT NAMES: one statutory employee W-2's box 1, cents preserved, when ../isStatutoryEmployeeRoutedToScheduleC and $0 otherwise. It is the amount that leaves Form 1040 line 1a (/wages subtracts the return level sum below) and arrives on the linked business's Schedule C line 1 (scheduleC:/scheduleCs/*/statutoryEmployeeWagesFromLinkedW2s adds it there). ONE QUANTITY, ONE FACT: the two consumers read the SAME per W-2 figure through the SAME gate, so no arithmetic can put this box 1 on both lines or on neither.
CENTS PRESERVED, deliberately: it is subtracted inside the sum that /wages rounds once, so it must be on the same footing as its minuend /formW2s/*/wagesUnrounded. See the footing note above /wages for why the whole line 1 chain adds with cents and rounds at the printed line.
COMPLETE SAFE $0: ../wagesUnrounded is itself complete safe, so an unanswered box 1 on a routed W-2 contributes 0 rather than an Incomplete, and every committed return, none of which checks box 13, resolves this to $0.

RETIRED AS A SUBMISSION REFUSAL. The BODY BELOW IS UNCHANGED and this fact still resolves; its one wiring - membership in flow:/flowIsKnockedOut - is gone. It never carried a BlockSubmissionOnTrue.
WHY THE REFUSAL HAD NO FEDERAL BASIS. The federal return's only interest in W-2 boxes 15 through 17 is box 17, which is deductible under section 164(a)(3) on Schedule A line 5a; box 17 is now transcribed and totalled by /box17StateIncomeTaxWithheldTotal. WHICH state box 15 names is a datum no federal fact derives from - enumerated over the whole tree, box 15 reaches only this guard, the alias /formW2s/*/state (also a stateSystems export), the MeF export /formW2s/*/xmlStateCd, and the intra-W-2 consistency check /formW2s/*/hasStateWagesWithoutStateCode. No PDF configuration.yml ever referenced a "PDF export" for box 15; the printed box uses ../writableStateAbbreviation directly. A FUTURE EDIT MUST NOT "RESTORE" THE MEMBERSHIP.

Fact.Name: Total state income tax withheld across Forms W-2 (box 17)
Fact.Description:
The total of Form W-2 box 17 across the filer's Forms W-2.
A DISCLOSURE, NOT A SCHEDULE A LEG. This total deliberately does not feed scheduleA:/writableStateLocalTaxes, and no consumer reads it today. Schedule A line 5a is reached in this dictionary only through that taxpayer-entered aggregate, and the decision about whether a payer-reported withholding box may feed it is recorded with the fact that owns it. Wiring it here would double-count against a total the filer has already typed by hand.
ADDENDS ARE ALREADY ROUNDED, because /formW2s/*/stateWithholding is the module's whole-dollar per-document image and no unrounded sibling exists. That is tolerable only while this total has no printed destination. A consumer that ever puts it on a printed line owes the /formW2s/*/federalWithholdingUnrounded treatment (an unrounded per-document addend, one Round at the line) FIRST - summing already-rounded addends is the defect.
COMPLETE-SAFE: /formW2s/*/stateWithholding is itself complete-safe ($0 when box 17 is unanswered), so this total is $0 on a return with no Forms W-2 and on a return whose W-2s leave box 17 blank.
A NEW YORK RETURN DUPLICATES THIS TOTAL ON PURPOSE, and this side says so because the duplication is invisible from here (an owner ruling). state/NY/ty2025 collects the same money again as a writable, /ny/it201/it2NewYorkStateTaxWithheld, feeding IT-201 line 72; it does not read this fact and must not. The New York intake has to be STANDALONE-CAPABLE - a filer may prepare the federal return elsewhere and come to this repo only for the New York return, and then the Forms W-2 collection behind this total is empty. Prefill from this disclosure, and any consistency prompt when the two figures disagree, belong to the application, not to the dictionary. NO CONSISTENCY KNOCKOUT COUPLES THE TWO GRAPHS, by the same ruling, and none exists (measured directly). NOTHING IN THIS FEDERAL FACT CHANGED for the note: the ruling asks the two sides to be documented, not wired. The reasoning in full lives with the New York writable, dictionary/states/NY/ty2025/nyIt201.xml.
NOW SUMS BOTH PRINTED ROWS. iw2w3:1593 says boxes 15-20 report "wages and taxes for two states and two localities"; this total previously summed row 1's /formW2s/*/stateWithholding only. It now adds row 2's /stateWithholding2, itself 0-defaulted the same way row 1 is, so a W-2 that leaves row 2 blank (nearly all of them) still resolves this total instead of going Incomplete.

Fact.Name: A W-2 shows Yonkers tax and the filer is a part-year resident - RETIRED AS A REFUSAL 2026-08-18
Fact.Description:
True when the taxpayer paid taxes in Yonkers on some Form W-2 and said that they are a part-year resident of Yonkers.
RETIRED AS A SUBMISSION REFUSAL. The BODY BELOW IS UNCHANGED and this fact still resolves; its one wiring - membership in flow:/flowIsKnockedOut - is gone. It never carried a BlockSubmissionOnTrue.
THE REFUSAL RESTED ON A CATEGORY ERROR, and it named the wrong obligation: it said part-year Yonkers residency "requires proration of the Yonkers resident/nonresident tax the engine does not compute". THE FEDERAL 1040 DOES NOT COMPUTE YONKERS TAX AT ALL, prorated or otherwise, and this repo does not owe one. The federal return's entire interest in box 19 is that a local income tax actually withheld is deductible under section 164(a)(3), and the deduction takes the amount PAID, which no proration changes; that amount is now transcribed and totalled by /box19LocalIncomeTaxWithheldTotal. Box 18 and box 20 reach no federal computation either - enumerated over the whole tree, box 20 reaches only /formW2s/*/locality and /formW2s/*/box20HasYonkers, whose sole consumer is this guard's own /formW2s/*/paidYonkersTaxes, and box 18 reaches nothing at all. A FUTURE EDIT MUST NOT "RESTORE" THE MEMBERSHIP.

Fact.Name: W2 belongs to secondary filer

A return with no secondary filer has none of the secondary filer's W-2s, so this is false there rather than undecided: the roster's secondary-filer lookup does not resolve on a one-filer return, and an undecided owner test would leave every per-filer W-2 total Placeholder.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer has W2s when primary filer is not filing jointly
Fact.Description:
Whether secondary filer has W2s when primary filer is not filing jointly. The community-property lift is per ITEM and conjoined with the character: it does not refuse a spouse's W-2 that Form 8958 line 1 gives this return half of, and it does refuse a spouse's W-2 that is separate property or whose character is unanswered.
COMPLETENESS SHAPE. The Derived All carries two conjuncts at the top - IsComplete(filingStatus:/isFilingStatusMFJ) and IsComplete(filers:/secondaryFiler) - ahead of every pre-existing operand, left byte-for-byte in its existing order. WHY: /formW2s/*/belongsToSecondaryFiler compares ../filer with filers:/secondaryFiler, and on a SINGLE-FILER return /secondaryFiler is a Find that resolves to nothing, so this guard, the collection guard's Count(...) > 0 and everything reading them would be Incomplete without the two conjuncts - the fact would never RESOLVE, so the knockout could not be shown false and the return could not be proved clean. NO REFUSAL MOVES: All short-circuits on a Complete-false operand, so the only transition the two conjuncts cause is Incomplete -> Complete false. LEFT ALONE ON PURPOSE: an unanswered ../filer on a TWO-FILER non-MFJ return keeps the base's value byte-for-byte (Incomplete), because filers:/secondaryFiler is Complete there - which is why the conjunct is IsComplete(filers:/secondaryFiler) and not IsComplete(../belongsToSecondaryFiler).

Fact.Name: Secondary filer has W2s when primary filer is not filing jointly
Fact.Description: Whether secondary filer has W2s when primary filer is not filing jointly, aggregated with ANY (Count(...) > 0) over every W-2 on the return: this is the collection-level fact that actually carries the submission block. True the moment any one item is true, because the harm is per return, not per document — one mis-attributed W-2 is enough to overstate Form 1040 line 1a. The community-property lift matches the item-level fact (/formW2s/*/secondaryFilerUsedWithoutMFJ) and is conjoined with the character there: this collection-level fact does not refuse a return whose only otherwise-unreportable spouse's W-2 items are ones Form 8958 line 1 gives this return half of, and it does refuse the moment any spouse's W-2 is separate property or its character is unanswered.

Fact.Name: Has Railroad Retirement Tax Act (RRTA) Codes
Fact.Description: Do any Railroad Retirement Tax Act (RRTA) codes show up in box 14 on this W2?

W-2 has a Box 17 (State income tax) value that is greater than the Box 16 (State wages, tips, etc) value.
Used to power a W-2 validation: State income tax cannot exceed state income amount.
Uses the writeable facts for these boxes and explicitly checks for completion, as the derived box values default to 0. Filling out a value for box 17 but not box 16 would then erroneously trigger this validation, for example, if using the derived facts for these boxes.
We only want to show this validation if the taxpayer entered a value for both boxes.

True if W2 has a value for Box 19 (Local income tax) and Box 18 (Local wages, tips, etc), and the value of Box 19 is greater than Box 18.
Derived box values default to 0, so this fact explicitly checks for completion; it's false if either box is incomplete.
Used to power a W-2 validation: Local income tax cannot exceed local income amount.

True if this W-2 reports social security tax withheld (box 4) but reports NO social security wages (box 3) and NO social security tips (box 7) — a combination that cannot occur on a correctly-prepared W-2.
Used to power a W-2 validation: social security tax cannot be withheld on a base of zero.
Box 3 is an optional writable (/formW2s/*/writableOasdiWages) whose derived fact silently defaults to 0 when it is left incomplete, and /formW2s/*/isComplete requires neither box 3 nor box 4. Nothing validated one against the other, so a filer could submit a return whose box 4 asserts social security tax was withheld while every box-3 consumer read zero. Two dollar consequences, in OPPOSITE directions, both from this one root cause:
(a) OVER-CLAIM. /primaryFilerTotalOasdiWagesForKnockout (and its secondary twin) is the sum of the per-W-2 min(oasdiWages, /maxOasdiWagesOnMultipleW2sForOnePerson), so it reads 0 and /anyFilerExceedsMaxOasdiWages cannot fire. A two-employer filer over the wage base escapes the knockout entirely, while formW2s:/socialSecurityTaxesWithheld sums box 4 unconditionally into ctcOdc:/sched8812Line21 — inflating Schedule 8812 line 23 while line 24's omitted Schedule 3 line 11 term understates the subtrahend. Both push /socialSecurityOverEitc up: the false-allowance direction. (b) UNDER-CLAIM. scheduleSE:/primaryFilerSePriorSocialSecurityWages (Schedule SE line 8d; its line-8a term used to read this module's knockout total until a rebuild replaced it with scheduleSE:/primaryFilerScheduleSeLine8a, the uncapped boxes 3+7+RRTA sum) reads a box-3-less W-2 as contributing only its tips/RRTA terms, so a self-employed filer whose W-2 answers none of them has line 8a = 0, keeps a full /seSocialSecurityWageBase on line 9, and is charged SE tax on earnings that the W-2 already used up. Taxpayer-adverse.
WHY THE PREDICATE IS SHAPED THIS WAY. Box 4 is tax on wages AND tips, so box 7 must be in the guard or a tips-only W-2 would be falsely refused. This fact also reads the DERIVED complete-safe box facts rather than IsComplete on the writables — deliberately UNLIKE the box17GreaterThanBox16 / box19GreaterThanBox18 validations above, which require both boxes complete precisely so a missing wage box cannot trigger them. Here a missing wage box IS the defect, so completeness-gating would defeat the check; reading the derived facts also catches an explicitly-entered zero box 3, which is the same impossible return.
An RRTA W-2 does not trip this: a railroad employer reports Tier 1/Tier 2 in box 14 and leaves boxes 3-6 blank, so box 4 is 0 and the first conjunct is false.

True if this W-2 reports Medicare tax withheld (box 6) but reports NO Medicare wages and tips (box 5) — a combination that cannot occur on a correctly-prepared W-2.
Used to power a W-2 validation: Medicare tax cannot be withheld on a base of zero.
The Medicare sibling of the box-3/box-4 check above, same root cause. Box 5 (/formW2s/*/writableMedicareWages) is an optional writable whose derived fact silently defaults to 0 when it is left incomplete, /formW2s/*/isComplete requires neither box 5 nor box 6, and nothing validated one against the other.
WHY THE PREDICATE IS SIMPLER THAN THAT CHECK, and this is the substantive difference between the two siblings. Box 4's guard needs a box-7 term because box 4 is tax on wages AND tips while box 3 deliberately EXCLUDES tips. Box 5 has no such gap: the instructions define it as "the wages and tips subject to Medicare tax ... the same as those subject to social security tax (boxes 3 and 7) except that there is no wage base limit", i.e. box 5 already SUBSUMES the tips that box 7 reports separately for social security. A tips-only W-2 therefore reports those tips IN box 5, so no tips term is needed and none is written. Adding one would have been harmless but false to the form.
THE LIVE FORM 8959 EXPOSURE IS ZERO, and that was MEASURED, not assumed before choosing a remedy. Both Form 8959 consumers of box 5 read the COMBINED box-5 total, and a zeroed box 5 pushes that total DOWN: - Part V (/additionalMedicareTaxWithheld, the line-22 withholding credit) is gated on the box-5 total exceeding /maxIndividualMedicareWages ($200,000). A zeroed box 5 CLOSES that gate, so the defect cannot manufacture a credit; - Part I (the 0.9% tax) measures its threshold against the same understated total, so it cannot manufacture a liability either. Across all 998 W-2 collection items in scenarios/upstream, scenarios/units, tests/nodes and syndoc, 16 items carry box 6 with no box 5, and the box-5 total is 0 on every one of the 16 affected scenarios — so the Part V gate is closed on all of them today and no Form 8959 dollar moves. The remedy is therefore the validation, and the delta is boolean-only.
THE DATA IS IMPOSSIBLE, NOT MERELY INCOMPLETE — which is the affirmative case for refusing it. Dividing box 6 by the statutory 1.45% recovers the Medicare wages the box-6 entry asserts were paid. On 13 of the 16 that implied base is a plausible-but-unreported wage figure. On the other three (scenarios/upstream/single-46k and the two node-test scenarios that reuse the same W-2) box 6 is 12,312.00, implying $849,103 of Medicare wages on a W-2 whose box 1 and box 3 both read 45,631.00 — and 12,312 is visibly a transcription of the same W-2's own writableStateEmployerId, 12312321. That is not a filer's wages under-reported; it is an entry no employer could have issued. A cross-box consistency check is the right instrument for it.
WHAT THIS FIX DOES NOT CLOSE, stated so the fix is not read as bigger than it is. /hasW2ValidationErrors has NO consumer anywhere in this dictionary (its downstream cone is itself — scripts/factdag.py down), so this fact makes the impossible W-2 REFUSABLE at the intake/validation layer but changes no computed value. In particular it does not close the over-claim path ctcOdc:/sched8812Line21 discloses as its scope gap (3) — the one where a closed Part V gate leaves an Additional-Medicare-Tax component in Schedule 8812 worksheet line 6 that the worksheet says to remove — because THIS fact only sees a box 6 against a ZERO box 5, which was 14 of that gap's 40 antecedent scenarios.
THE GAP IS NOW CLOSED AT ITS ANTECEDENT, by a sibling arm rather than by this one, and the paragraph above is left standing because it remains true OF THIS FACT. The clause that has NOT survived is the deferral that used to end it — that closing gap (3) "means revisiting form8959's $200,000 gate for its two opposite-signed consumers, which is a form8959 unit". That was adjudicated and refuted at form8959:/additionalMedicareTaxWithholdingOnWages: no fix at the gate improves world #1, and removing the gate was measured to relocate and multiply the phantom. The remedy landed here instead, as /formW2s/*/hasMedicareWithholdingAboveRateOnMedicareWages, which SUBSUMES this fact and covers the other 26 antecedent scenarios as well. This fact is kept for its own authority and its own witnesses; see the sibling for the two-tier bound and the per-W-2 shape.
An RRTA W-2 does not trip this: a railroad employer reports Tier 1/Tier 2 compensation in box 14 and leaves boxes 3-6 blank, so box 6 is 0 and the first conjunct is false. Confirmed against tests/nodes/ty2025/formW2s/w2-box14-rrta-yonkers.

True if this W-2 reports MORE social security tax withheld (box 4) than 6.2% of the social security wage and tip base it reports (boxes 3 + 7, capped at the annual wage base) — an amount no correctly-prepared W-2 can carry.
Used to power a W-2 validation: social security tax withheld cannot exceed the tax on the wages and tips the same W-2 reports.
A THIRD MEMBER OF A FAMILY of box-consistency validations, and the one that closes a dollar hole rather than an impossible-input hole: /formW2s/*/hasOasdiWithholdingWithoutOasdiWages catches box 4 against a ZERO base and /formW2s/*/hasMedicareWithholdingWithoutMedicareWages catches box 6 against a zero box 5; both leave untouched the case where the base is nonzero but too small for the withholding reported. This fact is the residual (a) that schedule3:/primaryFilerExcessOasdiWithheld disclosed in as many words: "an employer that over-withholds box 4 (or box-14 Tier 1) by LESS than the annual maximum, on a filer who also passes the wage gate, still inflates this leg dollar for dollar — the false-allowance direction. Closing it needs a per-W-2 withholding-against-6.2%-of-wages validation, which is the shape of its siblings and belongs in formW2s, not here." It is that validation. The direction is what earns it priority: Schedule 3 line 11 is a refundable credit and its per-employer cap only bites at $10,918.20, so every phantom dollar of box 4 below that ceiling reaches Form 1040 line 31 unchallenged.
THE CEILING IS DERIVED, NEVER TYPED. The instructions print the identity themselves — box 4 "should not exceed $10,918.20 ($176,100 x 6.2%)" — so this fact applies the 6.2% rate to LesserOf(box 3 + box 7, /maxOasdiWagesOnMultipleW2sForOnePerson) rather than carrying 10,918.20 as a second literal. The two forms are the same number by construction: below the wage base the cap is inert and the bound is 6.2% of the reported base; at or above it the cap binds and the bound is 6.2% x 176,100 = 10,918.20 exactly, in integer cents. One indexed parameter, and the ceiling moves with the SSA announcement without a second edit. The 6.2% is the section 3101(a) employee rate, statutory and not indexed, so it is a Rational exactly as schedule3:/maxOasdiTaxWithheldByOneEmployer spells it.
WHY BOX 7 IS IN THE BASE. Box 4 is tax on wages AND tips while box 3 deliberately EXCLUDES tips, so a base without box 7 would falsely refuse every tipped employee. This is the same term, for the same printed reason, that makes the box-4 sibling's predicate wider than the box-6 sibling's, and tests/nodes/ty2025/formW2s/w2-box4-rate-consistency-worked-example pins it as a quantity: a W-2 with box 3 = 10,000, box 7 = 5,000 and box 4 = 930 passes at a bound of 930 and would be refused at the box-3-only bound of 620.
THE COMPARISON IS ONE-SIDED ON PURPOSE. Box 4 BELOW 6.2% of the base is a reported return, not a defect: an employer that could not collect the tax on an employee's tips reports the shortfall as box 12 code A and is instructed "do not include this amount in box 4". Only the excess direction is impossible, and only the excess direction is tested.
THERE IS NO PRINTED TOLERANCE, and that was re-derived rather than assumed. Neither the box-4 instruction nor the common-errors list that supplied its siblings their own bullets states one; the worked example fixes the relationship exactly ("Box 4— 806.00 (6.2% of the amount in box 3)") and the ceiling sentence is an exact figure. So the only slack in this comparison is the WHOLE-DOLLAR RESOLUTION both sides are taken at, and that is a consequence of the operands rather than a tolerance anyone chose. This fact reads /formW2s/*/oasdiWithholding, ../oasdiWages and ../oasdiTips — the module's rounded per-W-2 box facts, the same three the box-4 sibling reads — and rounds its own bound to match. Comparing a HALF_UP-rounded box 4 against an unrounded cent-scale bound would manufacture up to $0.50 of pure rounding artefact on every W-2 whose box 4 carries cents, which is a false refusal with no basis in any printed rule. MEASURED, not argued: across the 1,005 W-2 collection items in scenarios/ and tests/nodes/, the cent-scale comparison refuses 159 items and the whole-dollar comparison refuses 64; the 95-item difference is entirely sub-dollar residue on W-2s whose box 4 was typed to the dollar.
IT SUBSUMES THE BOX-4 SIBLING EXACTLY, which is stated rather than left to be discovered. With box 3 and box 7 both zero the bound is 6.2% of zero, so this fact fires on precisely the population that sibling fires on, plus the nonzero-base excess. That sibling is kept: it is separately authorized, separately witnessed, and names a distinct defect to a filer reading the validation, and deleting it would change no verdict while losing that. An RRTA W-2 trips neither — a railroad employer reports Tier 1/Tier 2 in box 14 and leaves boxes 3-6 blank, so box 4 is 0 and 0 > 0 is false.
WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLOSE. Like its two siblings it makes the impossible W-2 REFUSABLE, not recomputed: /hasW2ValidationErrors still has no dictionary consumer, so no dollar moves on any return that is not refused, and residual (a) is closed in the sense that the bad input can no longer be submitted rather than in the sense that a corrected box 4 is inferred. Inferring one is expressly rejected below. The box-14 Tier 1 half of residual (a) is NOT closed here: no tier-1 tax base is reported on Form W-2, so the same 6.2% test cannot be written against box 14, and residual (b) on /formW2s/*/oasdiAndTier1WagesForExcessEligibility already states why.

True if this W-2 reports MORE Medicare tax withheld (box 6) plus uncollected Medicare tax (box 12 codes B and N, FICA only) than the two-tier Medicare rate applied to the Medicare wage and tip base it reports (box 5) — an amount no correctly-prepared W-2 can carry.
Used to power a W-2 validation: Medicare tax withheld cannot exceed the tax on the wages and tips the same W-2 reports.
A FOURTH MEMBER OF THE box-consistency FAMILY, and the one that closes ctcOdc:/sched8812Line21's scope gap (3) at its antecedent. /formW2s/*/hasOasdiWithholdingWithoutOasdiWages catches box 4 against a zero base, /formW2s/*/hasMedicareWithholdingWithoutMedicareWages catches box 6 against a zero box 5, /formW2s/*/hasOasdiWithholdingAboveRateOnOasdiWagesAndTips catches box 4 above 6.2% of a nonzero base; this one catches box 6 above the Medicare rate on a nonzero box 5, which is exactly the population gap (3) enumerated and could not close from the Form 8959 side. That gap's own adjudication (form8959:/additionalMedicareTaxWithholdingOnWages) found NO available fix at the $200,000 Part V gate — removing the gate was MEASURED to relocate and multiply the phantom, adding line-25c credits to 25 submittable returns totalling $110,309 — and named a formW2s intake validation as the remedy instead. This is it.
