THE BOUND HAS TWO TIERS BECAUSE MEDICARE HAS NO WAGE CAP, and that is the structural difference from the box-4 sibling rather than a variation on it. Box 4's ceiling is one rate on a CAPPED base (6.2% of boxes 3 + 7, capped at $176,100). Box 5 has no cap at all — "There is no limit on the amount reported in box 5" — so a capped-base shape has nothing to cap. What the printed rule supplies in its place is a SECOND RATE above a threshold: an employer withholds 1.45% on all Medicare wages and an additional 0.9% on what it pays one employee in excess of $200,000 in the calendar year. The bound is therefore 1.45% x box 5 + 0.9% x max(box 5 - 200,000, 0), rounded once. Both figures are read from the instructions, never from memory, and the $200,000 is the module's existing /maxIndividualMedicareWages — the per-employee withholding trigger, which is the right one: its own Description distinguishes it from the filing-status liability threshold, and it is the employer's obligation that is at issue here, not the taxpayer's.
THE SHAPE IS PER-W-2, AND THE PRINTED RULE DECIDES IT rather than the family precedent. The instructions for Form 8959 state the employer's duty employer by employer: "Your employer must withhold Additional Medicare Tax on wages it pays to you in excess of $200,000 for the calendar year, regardless of your filing status and regardless of wages or compensation paid by another employer." A RETURN-LEVEL predicate cannot express that. gap (3)'s successor note proposed one — Sigma box 6 greater than Round(0.0145 x Round(Sigma box 5)) — and it is WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, which is why the shape was re-derived rather than inherited. It is FALSE-REFUSING: a single filer with one employer paying $250,000 has a box 6 of 4,075.00 that section 3102(f)(1) REQUIRED, and 4,075 exceeds 1.45% of 250,000 = 3,625, so that lawful W-2 would be refused. The corpus already contains the witness — tests/nodes/ty2025/formW2s/w2-box5-present-medicare-part-v-fires reports box 5 = 250,000.00 and box 6 = 4,075.00, asserts /hasW2ValidationErrors false and is green today. It is also OVER-PERMISSIVE: the two-tier function is convex, so the sum of the per-W-2 bounds is never more than the bound on the sum, and an MFJ return with two $150,000 W-2s (neither employer withholding any additional tax) would be allowed 5,250 of box 6 where 4,350 is the most the two employers could lawfully have withheld.
THE COMPARISON IS ONE-SIDED ON PURPOSE. Box 6 BELOW the rate is a reported return, not a defect: an employer that could not collect the Medicare tax on an employee's tips reports the shortfall as box 12 code B and is instructed "Do not show any uncollected Additional Medicare Tax. Do not include this amount in box 6", and the uncollected Medicare tax on group-term life insurance for a former employee goes to box 12 code N on the same terms. Only the excess direction is impossible, and only the excess direction is tested.
THE COMPARISON IS TAKEN AT WHOLE DOLLARS, and that was re-measured here rather than inherited from the box-4 sibling. This fact reads ../medicareWithholding and ../medicareWages — the module's per-W-2 box facts, each already Round-wrapped at its own printed entry — and rounds its own bound to match. The argument transfers because the operands are the same class, but the MAGNITUDE does not: across 1,000 W-2s in a corpus of test returns the whole-dollar comparison refuses 41 and the cent-scale comparison refuses 109, a 68-W-2 difference that is entirely W-2s whose box 6 was typed to the dollar. The clearest is scenarios/upstream/mfj-cdcc-combat-pay-2024-verified, box 5 = 75,000.00 with box 6 = 1,088.00 where 1.45% is 1,087.50 exactly: at cent scale that HALF-UP-rounded entry reads as a fifty-cent over-withholding and the filer is refused, which no printed rule supports. There is no printed tolerance to appeal to instead — neither the box-6 instruction nor the Additional Medicare Tax paragraph states one — so the whole-dollar resolution is a consequence of the operands, not a tolerance anyone chose. The Round sits ONCE around the summed bound rather than on each tier, which is a choice and not a formality: with box 5 = 200,030 the tiers are 2,900.435 and 0.27, so rounding once gives 2,901 while rounding each tier gives 2,900. Rounding once is the more PERMISSIVE of the two by up to a dollar, which is the right direction for a refusal, and it matches the printed structure — the two rates compose one box-6 entry, and it is the entry that rounds.
IT SUBSUMES THE BOX-6 SIBLING EXACTLY, stated rather than left to be discovered. With box 5 zero the bound is zero, so this fact fires on precisely the population that sibling fires on, plus the nonzero-base excess. That sibling is kept: it is separately authorized, separately witnessed, and names a distinct defect to a filer reading the validation. An RRTA W-2 trips neither — a railroad employer reports Tier 1/Tier 2 compensation in box 14 and leaves boxes 3-6 blank, so box 6 is 0 and 0 > 0 is false when its box 12 codes B and N are answered as RRTA (they then add nothing); confirmed against tests/nodes/ty2025/formW2s/w2-box14-rrta-yonkers. An RRTA W-2 with code B or N whose regime is unanswered can trip it, and that return is already refused by ../box12MedicareRegimeUnknown.
WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT DO. Like its three siblings it makes the impossible W-2 REFUSABLE, not recomputed: /hasW2ValidationErrors still has no dictionary consumer, so no dollar moves on any return that is not refused. What CHANGES relative to the prior state of the module is which returns are refusable — gap (3)'s antecedent is no longer submittable, so the over-claim it describes can no longer be filed. Inferring a corrected box 6 is expressly rejected below. TWO RESIDUALS SURVIVE AND ARE NAMED. (i) A W-2 whose box 5 and box 6 are BOTH understated in the same proportion stays undetectable — a consistency check cannot see a consistent lie. (ii) The left side is box 6 PLUS the FICA share of box-12 codes B and N (../uncollectedMedicareTaxBox12FicaAddend), rounded once. Codes B and N are Medicare tax on the same box 5 wages and tips that the employer could not collect, so withheld and uncollected together cannot exceed the tax on box 5; Form 8959 line 19 adds them to box 6, so an inflated code B or N would otherwise raise the line 22 credit. Uncollected RRTA Medicare tax is excluded, as line 19 excludes it, because RRTA compensation is not in box 5.

Fact.Name: Form W-2 withholding
Fact.Description:
Federal income tax withheld from wages, as reported on line 25a of Form 1040. Whole dollars: the addends are summed WITH CENTS and the total is rounded once, at this line.
This previously read Round(CollectionSum(/formW2s/*/federalWithholding)), i.e. a sum of per-W-2 amounts each ALREADY rounded to whole dollars. The outer Round was present but inert — rounding an already-whole sum changes nothing — so the defect was the same sum-of-rounded-addends shape fixed on Form 8959 line 19, not a missing Round. Line 25a's instruction is the most explicit in the class: "Add the amounts shown as federal income tax withheld on your Form(s) W-2. Enter the total on line 25a." The fix sums /formW2s/*/federalWithholdingUnrounded (cents preserved) and rounds here. A SINGLE-W-2 return is unaffected — Round(x) = Round(Sigma x) with one addend — so only multi-W-2 returns whose box-2 cents cross a .50 boundary in aggregate move, bounded at roughly $0.50 per extra W-2 and unsigned in direction.
The per-W-2 item fact /formW2s/*/federalWithholding keeps its own Round and its exported value is unchanged; see that fact for why.

Fact.Name: (Writable) Are this employer's wages community income?
Fact.Description:
THE PER-ITEM CHARACTER INPUT for Form 8958 line 1, and the wage twin of interest:/interestReports/*/writableIsCommunityIncome. Form 8958 states the SPLIT with no state-law qualifier — "A spouse’s or RDP’s wages and self-employment income from a" / "sole proprietorship are community income and must be evenly split." (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8958.pdf, page 3, LEFT column of a two column extraction) — but that sentence settles how community wages are divided, not WHICH wages are community. Publication 555 answers the second question and names two populations whose wages are separate or may be: only pay for services earned "while domiciled in a community" property state is community (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p555.pdf, page 4, LEFT column, whose Table 1 right-hand column lists separate property income opposite it), and pay earned after separation and before a divorce decree "continues to be community in" / "come. In other states, it is separate income." (same file, lines 333 to 335, LEFT column). A filer who changed domicile mid-year, or who separated mid-year in a state that cuts the community off at separation, has a W-2 the gate cannot characterise. This question is the one the form itself puts to the filer, and it is asked per W-2 because domicile and separation both move within a year.
SCREEN SPEC. Implement the screen from this paragraph; no IRS document has to be opened. QUESTION: "Were the wages from {../employerName} community income?" HELP TEXT: "In a community property state, the pay you or your spouse earned while you were married and domiciled in that state is usually community income, and each of you reports half of it. Pay earned while either of you was domiciled somewhere else is separate income, and so is pay one of you earned after you separated if your state ends the community at separation. Answer No if any of that describes this W-2. If you are not sure, check your state's rules — the answer follows your state's law, not federal law." Cite for the help text: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p555.pdf, pages 4-5, LEFT column of a two column extraction. ASKED WHEN: filers:/isCommunityPropertyAllocationReturn is true — a married filer filing separately who is domiciled in a community property state and is not relieved by IRC 66(a). It is asked once per item of /formW2s, on every W-2 the return carries, including the spouse's. On every other return it is never asked and never read. UNANSWERED POSTURE: REFUSED, not defaulted. An unanswered character makes ../isCommunityIncome FALSE, so nothing is allocated and the whole W-2 stays on this return; and it makes /formW2s/communityPropertyCharacterisationIncomplete TRUE, which makes filers:/communityPropertyAllocationInputsComplete FALSE and leaves filers:/knockoutSubjectToCommunityPropertyLaws refusing the return. Silence therefore never allocates and never files: this dictionary does not assume community. VALIDATION: Boolean. Yes / No, no third option and no default. Nothing else to check. WHAT IT FEEDS: ../isCommunityIncome, hence ../communityPropertyAllocatedWagesUnrounded (Form 8958 line 1 column B and, through /communityPropertyWagesAllocationAdjustmentUnrounded, Form 1040 line 1a and line 1z), ../communityPropertyAllocatedFederalWithholdingUnrounded (Form 8958 line 11 and Form 1040 line 25a), the printed line 1 columns B and C, and the collection guard ../secondaryFilerUsedWithoutMFJ, which keeps refusing a SPOUSE's W-2 that is not characterised community.

Fact.Name: This employer's wages are community income
Fact.Description:
../writableIsCommunityIncome read complete safe. IsComplete FIRST, so an unanswered character resolves FALSE rather than Incomplete: nothing downstream may be dragged Incomplete by a question nobody has been asked yet, and FALSE is the fail closed direction — no allocation, refusal left standing.
AN ANSWERED FALSE AND AN UNANSWERED CHARACTER ARE THE SAME HERE AND DIFFERENT AT THE ROLLUP. Both leave the W-2 unallocated and both leave ../secondaryFilerUsedWithoutMFJ refusing when the W-2 is the spouse's. They part company at ../communityPropertyCharacterisationMissing, which is true only for silence, so an answered-separate return can still reach filers:/communityPropertyAllocationInputsComplete while an unanswered one cannot.

Fact.Name: This W-2's community-property character question is unanswered
Fact.Description: Not(IsComplete(../writableIsCommunityIncome)) and nothing else: TRUE while the per-item character question has no answer, FALSE the moment the filer answers it either way. An unanswered character must be VISIBLE at the return level rather than silently defaulted, because filers:/communityPropertyAllocationInputsComplete lifts the allocation-gate arm of filers:/knockoutSubjectToCommunityPropertyLaws only on a return whose every present item is characterised. This fact changes no figure on its own: an unanswered character already allocates nothing. Read only by /formW2s/communityPropertyCharacterisationIncomplete.

Fact.Name: Some W-2 community-property character is unanswered
Fact.Description: GreaterThan(Count of per-item unanswered characters, 0), the same return-level shape as /formW2s/secondaryFilerUsedWithoutMFJ. Read by filers:/communityPropertyAllocationInputsComplete, whose IsComplete-first wrapper is what keeps filers:/knockoutSubjectToCommunityPropertyLaws complete-safe when this collection is absent: an absent root is Placeholder on the JVM, the wrapper reads that as NOT complete, and the refusal stands. Fail closed.

Fact.Name: Form 8958 line 1 row is an allocated community income row
Fact.Description: True when this W-2 sits on a return that must allocate community income AND the filer has characterised this employer's wages as community income. It is the condition the allocation facts switch on, lifted to a fact of its own so the line 1 column B and column C facts and the collection guard select on the same test rather than restating it. False on an ordinary return and false on a separate-property row, which is why silence about the character of a W-2 never allocates it.

Fact.Name: Form 8958 line 1 — the community half of this employer's wages that this unit moves
Fact.Description:
The taxpayer's allocated share of ONE W-2's box 1, on a return that must allocate community income AND on a W-2 the filer has characterised as community income. $0 on every other W-2 and on every other return. NOT rounded to whole dollars: this is an addend of Form 1040 line 1a and line 1z, and both of those round once at their own printed line.
THE CHARACTER IS ASKED, NOT ASSUMED. Form 8958 splits wages with no state-law qualifier, but that sentence is about the SPLIT and not about which wages are community wages: Publication 555 makes pay community only when earned "while domiciled in a community" property state (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p555.pdf, page 4, LEFT column of a two column extraction) and leaves post-separation, pre-decree pay to state law (same file, lines 333 to 335). So the halving is switched on ../form8958Line1RowIsAllocatedCommunityIncome, and an unanswered character allocates nothing and leaves the return refused by filers:/communityPropertyAllocationInputsComplete.
THE HALF IS ROUNDED TO THE CENT. TWO BOUNDED CONSEQUENCES, disclosed here rather than only in the records file. (i) On an odd-cent W-2 the two spouses' halves total one cent more or less than box 1, which is a miss against the form's own instruction "amounts in columns B and C. Together, columns B and C should" / "equal column A." (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8958.pdf, page 4, LEFT column of a two column extraction, read DOWN the left column). It is the unavoidable cost of a per-payer allocation printed in cents and nothing in this dictionary can remove it. (ii) The return-level Round(CollectionSum(these)) can differ from Round(half of the whole collection) only once the per-employer residuals sum past half a dollar — roughly a hundred odd-cent W-2s. On the measured two-W-2 case they cancelled exactly (20,000.26 + 15,000.12 = 35,000.38, which is half of 70,000.76).
$0 when filers:/isCommunityPropertyAllocationReturn is false, which is every ordinary return. That gate is complete safe false by construction, and ../isCommunityIncome is complete safe false in the same way, so an unanswered domicile or an unanswered character leaves this fact Complete at $0 rather than Incomplete.
THIS IS NOT COLUMN B ON EVERY ROW. On a SEPARATE-property W-2 of this taxpayer's own, column A is the whole box 1 and column B is the whole box 1, with column C zero, while this fact is $0. The printed columns are ../form8958Line1ColumnBThisReturnShareUnrounded and ../form8958Line1ColumnCOtherSpouseShareUnrounded.

Fact.Name: Form 8958 line 11 — the community half of this employer's box 2 that this unit moves
Fact.Description:
The taxpayer's allocated share of ONE W-2's box 2, on a return that must allocate community income AND on a W-2 the filer has characterised as community income. NOT rounded to whole dollars; Form 1040 line 25a rounds once, at its own line.
IT SWITCHES ON THE SAME CHARACTER AS THE WAGES, because the printed rule is about community wages and nothing else: "each of you is entitled to credit for half the income tax withheld on" community wages (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8958.pdf, page 4). Withholding on a SEPARATE W-2 is not halved; it stays whole with the wages it was withheld from.
THE HALF IS ROUNDED TO THE CENT, exactly as on the wages twin above, and for the same reason — Multiply(Rational 1/2, Dollar) is cent-scaled, HALF EVEN. The same two bounded consequences follow — the two spouses' halves of one odd-cent box 2 can total a cent away from column A against "amounts in columns B and C. Together, columns B and C should" / "equal column A." (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8958.pdf, page 4, LEFT column of a two column extraction), and the line-25a total can differ from half the whole only once the per-employer residuals sum past half a dollar.
It moves on exactly the same halves as ../communityPropertyAllocatedWagesUnrounded, because the credit follows the wages it was withheld from. $0 on every non-allocation return and on every W-2 that is not characterised community.

Fact.Name: Form 8958 line 1 column B, this return's share of this employer's wages
Fact.Description:
The share of ONE W-2's box 1 that belongs on THIS separate return, which Form 8958 line 1 column B prints. On an allocated community row it is the community half ../communityPropertyAllocatedWagesUnrounded already computes; on every other row it is the whole box 1, because a separate-property W-2 that reaches a filable separate return is this taxpayer's own (/formW2s/secondaryFilerUsedWithoutMFJ blocks submission otherwise). The register prints this return's taxpayer in column B and the spouse or RDP in column C, matching the order of the page 1 identity block. Off gate the whole W-2 is this return's, which is the ordinary separate return answer. Column A is ../wagesUnrounded, so B and C foot to A by construction.
ON A SPOUSE'S SEPARATE-PROPERTY W-2 THE PREMISE FAILS AND THIS CELL PRINTS WRONG. The "is this taxpayer's own" premise above holds only for submission, not for computation: this fact does not itself read whose W-2 it is, so on a W-2 that belongsToSecondaryFiler and is characterised separate, this cell still resolves to the whole box 1 (right answer: column B should be $0, column C the whole). The return carrying that item is REFUSED — /formW2s/secondaryFilerUsedWithoutMFJ blocks its submission — so the wrong figure is never on a filed return; whether it can reach a rendered draft/preview is a product-flow question this dictionary does not answer. Inherited by interest:/interestReports/*/form8958Line2ColumnBThisReturnShareUnrounded, which ships the identical fallback and the identical exposure.

Fact.Name: Form 8958 line 1 column C, the other spouse or RDP share of this employer's wages
Fact.Description: The share of ONE W-2's box 1 that belongs to the other spouse or RDP, which Form 8958 line 1 column C prints. It is column A minus column B by construction, which is how the form's own instruction "Together, columns B and C should equal column A" is made to hold exactly. On an odd-cent community row the half rounds to the even cent and column B takes it, so the residual cent lands here rather than breaking the footing; that is a disclosed consequence of a per-employer allocation printed in cents. $0 on a separate-property row, where column A and column B are both the whole box 1, and $0 off gate.

Fact.Name: Community-property allocated wages (Form 8958 line 1)
Fact.Description:
The taxpayer's own half of the COMMUNITY rows of Form 8958 line 1, totalled over every employer where that row is community income — the outgoing half that leaves this return for the spouse's separate return in a community property state. Whole dollars — the per-employer halves are summed WITH CENTS and the total is rounded once here.
NOT THE PRINTED COLUMN B TOTAL OVER THE WHOLE COLLECTION. A separate-property row's column B is the row's WHOLE box 1 (../form8958Line1ColumnBThisReturnShareUnrounded), while this fact is $0 on that row — it only sums the per-employer COMMUNITY halves (/formW2s/*/communityPropertyAllocatedWagesUnrounded, itself $0 on a separate row). THE SPLIT RUNS BOTH WAYS ON A COMMUNITY ROW ONLY: half the taxpayer's OWN community wages leave this return as well as half the spouse's community wages arriving, which is why this is a sum of per-employer community halves and not the collection's printed column B nor a half of the whole collection. $0 on every return the gate reads false on, and $0 on every separate-property row even on a gate-true return.
This fact is the DISCLOSURE figure. The number Form 1040 line 1a actually carries moves through /communityPropertyWagesAllocationAdjustmentUnrounded, which is an addend of both the line 1a and the line 1z chain so the two agree by construction ; that adjustment's own Description names the residual this disclosure figure does not need to close.

Fact.Name: Community-property allocated federal withholding (Form 8958 line 11)
Fact.Description:
The taxpayer's own half of the WITHHOLDING on the COMMUNITY rows of Form 8958 line 11, totalled over every employer where that row is community income: half the federal income tax withheld on the community wages this return reports half of. Whole dollars, rounded once here over cents-bearing addends.
NOT THE PRINTED COLUMN B/C TOTAL OVER THE WHOLE COLLECTION, the same way its wages sibling /communityPropertyAllocatedWages is not: a separate-property row's withholding stays whole with the wages it was withheld from and is $0 on this fact, so this total is a sum of per-employer community halves, not a half of the whole collection.
It exists because the contract said it must: "Form 8958 line 11 allocates the withheld tax on the same halves ... so formW2s:/formW2Withholding moves with this fact or the return is internally inconsistent." $0 on every return the gate reads false on, and $0 on every separate-property row even on a gate-true return.

Fact.Name: The wage half that leaves this return under Form 8958
Fact.Description:
A NEGATIVE, cents-bearing addend: MINUS the sum of the per-employer community halves, which is the half of the community wages that belongs on the spouse's separate return.
WHY THE NEGATION AND NOT ALLOCATED MINUS UNSCOPED. Allocated MINUS the unscoped W-2 total is right only while EVERY W-2 is community income, and /formW2s/*/writableIsCommunityIncome makes the collection MIXED: on a $40,000 community W-2 plus a $10,000 separate W-2 of the taxpayer's own that shape gives 20,000 minus 50,000 equals minus 30,000 and prints $20,000, silently deleting the filer's OWN separate wages from Form 1040 line 1a. The negation gives minus 20,000 and prints $30,000, which is "half of all community income and all of your" separate income (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8958.pdf, page 3, LEFT column of a two column extraction). This is the same correction interest:/communityPropertyInterestAllocationAdjustmentUnrounded carries for the same reason.
THE RESIDUAL THIS SHAPE DOES NOT CLOSE, named rather than claimed away. This addend subtracts column B (this return's share, /formW2s/*/communityPropertyAllocatedWagesUnrounded) on every community row, but the exact addend that makes line 1a foot to the printed column B BY CONSTRUCTION — the same standard /formW2s/*/form8958Line1ColumnCOtherSpouseShareUnrounded sets two facts earlier — is MINUS that column-C fact, not this one. So line 1a actually resolves to Σ_community columnC + Σ_separate columnB rather than Σ columnB over every row: the two agree only where the HALF-EVEN split of an odd-cent box 1 is exact, and differ by up to one cent per odd-cent community W-2 otherwise. It does NOT "degenerate to the old shape exactly when every W-2 is community" — the old shape is Σ round½(A) and this one is ΣA − Σ round½(A), which differ on odd-cent A too. Measured on the committed cents fixture : the two per-W-2 residuals are −0.01 and +0.01, they cancel, and /wages stays 35,000.00 with no committed value moved — real but sub-cent, and it does not survive the whole-dollar Round in this case. This fact, its withholding twin below, and interest:/communityPropertyInterestAllocationAdjustmentUnrounded (which ships this same shape over an operand with the same "this return's share" meaning) all want repointing to the exact column-C addend in one two-module unit, so the wages and interest chains stay consistent with each other until then; the withholding twin has no column-B/C facts to repoint to, because line 11 (leg (b)) is untouched. Not built here.
WHY AN ADDEND AND NOT A REPLACEMENT, and it is the footing note made mechanical. Form 1040 line 1a (/wages) and line 1z (income:/employerIncomeSubtotal) are computed by two different chains and may never be moved separately. Switching either one to the allocated total alone would break the footing. This single fact is an addend of BOTH, so 1a and 1z carry the same allocation by construction, exactly as they carry the same cents. A THIRD chain takes the identical addend: income:/employerIncomeSubtotalDisregardingSection137, the Form 8839 MAGI worksheet line 1 and a §86(b)(2)(A) / §219(g)(3)(A)(ii) modified-AGI base. It moves in the same direction and by the same amount as line 1z, so the allocation is correct there; it is named here because it is not obvious from the fact's Name.
$0 whenever filers:/isCommunityPropertyAllocationReturn is false, so every ordinary return keeps the value it had. The gate is complete safe false, so an unanswered domicile changes nothing.
THE PER-FILER EARNED-INCOME CHAINS ARE DELIBERATELY NOT TOUCHED — /primaryFilerWages, /secondaryFilerWages and the two income:/*EmployerIncomeSubtotalBase facts. Publication 555 says so in terms for the EIC: "Your earned income includes the entire amount you" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p555.pdf, page 8, LEFT column) "earned, even if part of it is treated as belonging to your" (line 488) "spouse under your state's community property laws. The" (line 489), while its CAUTION puts the allocated figure in AGI, which is the line-1z path this addend does move.
THE EARNED-INCOME FIREWALL. Leaving /primaryFilerWages and /secondaryFilerWages alone is NOT enough to keep earned income unallocated, because eitc:/eitcEarnedIncomeBase reads Form 1040 LINE 1z (income:/employerIncomeSubtotal), which this addend moves. Measured, not reasoned: with the EITC base pointed at the allocated line it read 35,000.00 where this filer's earned income is 40,001.00. IRC 32(c)(2)(B)(i) forbids exactly that — the earned income of an individual "be computed without regard to any commu-" / "nity property laws," — so income:/employerIncomeSubtotalWithoutCommunityPropertyAllocation carries the unallocated base and the FOUR earned-income readers point at it (the EITC base, both /earnedIncomeWithAllCombatPay facts, and standardDeduction:/minimumStandardDeduction). The AGI chain keeps the allocation. THAT SIBLING FACT IS ALSO FILER-SCOPED: summing the primary AND secondary bases would report the HOUSEHOLD's wages as this filer's earned income — 70,001.00 where the filer earned 40,001.00 — on the one population this unit creates, a non-joint return that may now carry the spouse's W-2. Neither §32(c)(2)(B)(i) nor Pub. 555's "Your earned income includes the entire amount you" earned licenses ADDING the spouse's whole wages, and the error would run taxpayer-FAVOURABLE through the ACTC's 15% of earned income over $2,500. It switches on the gate and drops the secondary base on an allocation return.

Fact.Name: The withholding half that leaves this return under Form 8958
Fact.Description:
The line 25a twin of /communityPropertyWagesAllocationAdjustmentUnrounded: a negative, cents-bearing addend equal to MINUS the sum of the per-employer allocated withholding. Line 25a has no second chain to foot against, but the shape is kept identical so the two adjustments are read and audited together, and it is the negation for the same reason: on a mixed collection the withholding on a SEPARATE W-2 stays whole on this return.
$0 whenever filers:/isCommunityPropertyAllocationReturn is false.

Fact.Name: Statutory employee box 1 wages routed off line 1a onto a Schedule C
Fact.Description:
The return's total statutory employee wages that /wages must NOT carry: the sum of /formW2s/*/statutoryEmployeeWagesToScheduleC over every W-2, cents preserved. This is the return-level half of the /statutoryEmployeeWagesToScheduleC contract.
WHY IT EXISTS: the printed instruction routes this box 1 to Schedule C line 1, and Schedule C's own line 31 then reaches Schedule 1 line 3. Left on Form 1040 line 1a as well, the same wages would reach /totalIncome twice. This fact is the subtrahend that keeps the box 1 amount on exactly one line, and it is the SAME per W-2 figure the Schedule C leg adds, gated the same way, so the two sides cannot disagree.
$0 ON EVERY COMMITTED RETURN: no committed scenario checks box 13, every term is complete safe $0, and the sum is therefore Complete $0 there, which is what keeps line 1a byte identical. It is Complete rather than Placeholder on a return with no W-2 collection only because CollectionSum over an absent collection is not reached here: /formW2s is a Placeholder backed collection that every supported return carries, exactly as /wages above already assumes by summing it unguarded.
Form 1040 line 1z (income:/employerIncomeSubtotal) is a SECOND chain over the same box 1 amounts and needs the same subtrahend, but PER FILER rather than at income:/employerIncomeSubtotal itself: the two per-filer bases below each subtract their own filer-scoped sum, because those bases are also the per-filer earned income figures Form 2441 and the section 219 ceiling read. Line 1a and line 1z foot. /flowKnockoutStatutoryEmployee is narrowed to the data-completeness residue, a checked box 13 whose routing was never answered.

Fact.Name: The primary filer's own statutory employee box 1 wages routed to a Schedule C
Fact.Description:
The PRIMARY filer's half of /statutoryEmployeeWagesRoutedToScheduleC: the sum of /primaryFilerW2s/*/statutoryEmployeeWagesToScheduleC, cents preserved. This is the per-filer subtrahend the Form 1040 line 1z chain needs.
WHY A PER FILER SUM AND NOT JUST THE RETURN LEVEL ONE. Line 1a (/wages) is computed from the unscoped /formW2s collection and subtracts the return level total. Line 1z is computed by a COMPLETELY SEPARATE per filer chain - /primaryFilerWages and /secondaryFilerWages into income:/primaryFilerEmployerIncomeSubtotalBase and its twin - so the same subtraction has to be made filer by filer there or the two printed lines disagree. See the footing note above /wages for why the two chains may never be moved separately. Subtracting the RETURN level total inside ONE filer's base would mis attribute a routed W-2 that belongs to the other filer, which matters because those bases are also the per filer earned income figures Form 2441 lines 4 and 5 read.
SHAPED EXACTLY LIKE /primaryFilerWages: a bare CollectionSum over the same /primaryFilerW2s filtered collection, cents preserved, no Round of its own, because it is subtracted inside a sum that income:/employerIncomeSubtotal rounds once at the printed line.
COMPLETE SAFE $0. Every term is /formW2s/*/statutoryEmployeeWagesToScheduleC, which is complete safe $0, and no committed scenario checks box 13, so this is Complete $0 on every committed return and no committed line 1z moves.

Fact.Name: The secondary filer's own statutory employee box 1 wages routed to a Schedule C
Fact.Description:
The secondary filer mirror of /primaryFilerStatutoryEmployeeWagesRoutedToScheduleC; see that fact for the full statement of why the line 1z chain needs a per filer subtrahend and why no Round belongs here. Sums /secondaryFilerW2s/*/statutoryEmployeeWagesToScheduleC, cents preserved, complete safe $0.
THE TWO PER FILER SUMS ADD TO THE RETURN LEVEL /statutoryEmployeeWagesRoutedToScheduleC exactly as /primaryFilerWages and /secondaryFilerWages add to the unscoped box 1 total, because /primaryFilerW2s and /secondaryFilerW2s split /formW2s on which filer the statement names (/formW2s/*/belongsToPrimaryFiler and /formW2s/*/belongsToSecondaryFiler, one Equal against each filer). That is the EXACT posture the raw wage chain already relies on for line 1a and line 1z to foot: /primaryFilerWages plus /secondaryFilerWages is the box 1 total /wages sums unscoped. This pair inherits that posture rather than adding a guard of its own, deliberately, so the statutory subtraction can never be on a different footing from the wages it is subtracted from.

Fact.Name: The primary filer's own box 12 code T employer-provided adoption benefits
Fact.Description: The sum of /primaryFilerW2s/*/adoptionBenefitsOrZero, cents preserved, shaped exactly like /primaryFilerStatutoryEmployeeWagesRoutedToScheduleC: a bare CollectionSum over the same filer-scoped filtered collection, no Round of its own, complete-safe $0 on every return that reports no code T.

Fact.Name: The secondary filer's own box 12 code T employer-provided adoption benefits
Fact.Description: The secondary filer mirror of /primaryFilerAdoptionBenefitsBox12CodeT. The two add to /adoptionBenefitsBox12CodeT for the same reason /primaryFilerWages plus /secondaryFilerWages is the unscoped box 1 total: /primaryFilerW2s and /secondaryFilerW2s partition /formW2s on which filer the statement names.

Fact.Name: Return-level box 12 code T employer-provided adoption benefits, whole dollars
Fact.Description: Round(CollectionSum(/formW2s/*/adoptionBenefitsOrZero)) — every W-2 on the return, whichever filer it belongs to. Whole dollars because its ONE use is the comparison against form8839:/adoptionLine23TotalEmployerBenefits, which is itself a rounded printed line; comparing a cents-bearing sum against a rounded line would report a mismatch that is only a rounding difference. Complete-safe $0.

Fact.Name: Box 12 code T reports more adoption assistance than Form 8839 line 23 accounts for
Fact.Description:
True when the return's total box 12 code T amount EXCEEDS form8839:/adoptionLine23TotalEmployerBenefits. This is the data-completeness residue that /formW2s/*/knockoutBox12Code keeps refusing for code T, once the federal consequence of code T was built.
WHY THIS IS THE RESIDUE AND NOT SOMETHING NARROWER. Form 8839 line 22 is a PER-CHILD intake and its printed instruction is "Employer-provided adoption benefits you received in 2025. This amount should be shown in box 12 of your 2025 Form(s) W-2 with code T". The W-2 supplies the TOTAL; only the taxpayer can say which child each dollar belongs to, because the W-2 carries no child. So the per-child intake is not replaced by the W-2 sum and is not fed by it — the W-2 sum CROSS-CHECKS it. A code T total the Form 8839 lines 22 do not reach is an unanswered intake: the section 137 exclusion cannot be figured for the missing part, and the benefit would leave income with no exclusion computation behind it. That is exactly the "unanswered or contradictory intake" residue a narrowing is required to keep refusing.
ONE-DIRECTIONAL, DELIBERATELY. Line 23 GREATER than the code T total is legitimate and is not refused: i8839's foreign-child rule puts benefits received BEFORE 2025 on line 22 for an adoption that became final in 2025, and no 2025 Form W-2 reports those.
WHOLE DOLLARS ON BOTH SIDES: /adoptionBenefitsBox12CodeT rounds, and line 23 is a rounded printed line, so a cents difference can never trip this refusal.
COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE: both operands are complete-safe $0, so this is Complete false on every return that reports no code T — which is every committed scenario, and why no committed return's knockout state moves.

Fact.Name: W-2 wages carried to Form 4563 line 7
Fact.Description: The total, over every W-2 on the return, of the box 1 wages keyed to Form 4563 line 7 (/formW2s/*/americanSamoaExcludedWages), cents preserved. Form 4563 line 7 is never smaller than this. Zero when the return has no W-2s.

Fact.Name: W-2 wages counted in Schedule 8812 line 2a
Fact.Description: The total, over every W-2 on the return, of the box 1 wages excluded under section 933 (/formW2s/*/puertoRicoExcludedWages), cents preserved. Schedule 8812 line 2a is never smaller than this. Zero when the return has no W-2s.

Fact.Name: W-2 box 1 wages that stay on Form 1040 line 1a
Fact.Description:
The total, over every W-2 on the return, of box 1 (/formW2s/*/wagesUnrounded, cents preserved) less the part keyed as possession-source wages (/possessionExcludedWagesOnW2s) and less the statutory-employee wages routed to a Schedule C (/statutoryEmployeeWagesRoutedToScheduleC): the W-2 wages Form 1040 line 1a still carries. Zero on a return with no W-2s.
WHY IT EXISTS. ctcOdc:/possessionTypedWagesMayBeOnAnEnteredW2 reads it: Form 4563 line 7 wages that were typed on the form rather than keyed on a W-2 are counted twice when the same wages are also in the box 1 this fact still counts (once in adjusted gross income, and again when every MAGI adds the exclusion back). A positive figure here is what makes that possible.

Fact.Name: W-2 wages excluded from Form 1040 line 1a as possession income
Fact.Description: The total, over every W-2 on the return, of the box 1 wages excluded under section 931 or 933 (/formW2s/*/possessionExcludedWages), cents preserved: the amount that leaves Form 1040 line 1a. Zero when the return has no W-2s.

Fact.Name: Wages, salaries, tips, etc.
Fact.Description:
Wage income to report on line 1a of Form 1040. Whole dollars: the addends are summed WITH CENTS and the total is rounded once, at this line. Box 1 wages excluded under section 931 (Form 4563 line 7) or section 933 (Schedule 8812 line 2a) are not reported here: /possessionExcludedWagesOnW2s is subtracted alongside the statutory-employee routing.
This previously read Round(CollectionSum(/formW2s/*/wages)), i.e. a sum of per-W-2 amounts each ALREADY rounded to whole dollars — the same sum-of-rounded-addends shape fixed on Form 8959 line 1 and on Form 1040 line 25a. The outer Round was present but inert, so the defect was never a missing Round. Line 1a's instruction is explicit that it is a line you add to: "Enter the total amount from Form(s) W-2, box 1. If a joint return, also include your spouse's income from Form(s) W-2, box 1." The fix sums /formW2s/*/wagesUnrounded (cents preserved) and rounds here. A SINGLE-W-2 return is unaffected — Round(x) = Round(Sigma x) with one addend — so only multi-W-2 returns whose box-1 cents cross a .50 boundary in aggregate move, bounded at roughly $0.50 per extra W-2 and unsigned in direction.
Line 1z (income:/employerIncomeSubtotal) was repointed at the same addend in the same unit, so 1a and 1z agree; see the footing note immediately above for why they cannot be moved separately.
STATUTORY EMPLOYEE ROUTING: this line SUBTRACTS /statutoryEmployeeWagesRoutedToScheduleC. Box 1 of a W-2 whose box 13 "Statutory employee" box is checked, and which names the Schedule C it is reported on, belongs on that Schedule C's line 1 and not here. The subtrahend is complete safe $0 and resolves to $0 on every committed scenario, none of which checks box 13, so every committed line 1a is byte identical.
LINE 1z's matching subtrahend is NOT at income:/employerIncomeSubtotal: the subtraction is made PER FILER, on income:/primaryFilerEmployerIncomeSubtotalBase and its twin, reading the two filer-scoped sums below rather than this return-level one, because those bases are also the per-filer earned income figures. A second subtrahend at /employerIncomeSubtotal would double subtract and must not be added. /flowKnockoutStatutoryEmployee is narrowed to the data-completeness residue, a checked box 13 whose routing was never answered: a routed statutory employee return is filable. California TY2025 reads this fact through its stateSystems export (FTB 3514, Schedule CA (540), Schedule CA (540NR)).

Fact.Name: Primary Filer wages, salaries, tips, etc.
Fact.Description:
The primary filer's own W-2 box-1 total, less the box 1 wages he excludes under section 931 or 933 (/primaryFilerW2s/*/possessionExcludedWages), which are not includible in gross income: an ADDEND of the Form 1040 line-1 chain and the wage term of his Form 2441 and EIC earned income. Cents preserved, NOT rounded — this is not a printed line.
This previously summed /primaryFilerW2s/*/wages, i.e. per-W-2 amounts each already rounded to whole dollars, and was whole-dollar only as an accident of its pre-rounded addends. It now sums /primaryFilerW2s/*/wagesUnrounded, which puts it on exactly the footing its six sibling addends in income:/primaryFilerEmployerIncomeSubtotalBase already had (every one of them rounding=none). The rounding for Form 1040 line 1z happens once, at income:/employerIncomeSubtotal, which already wraps its Add in Round; no Round belongs here.
This is the chain that actually carries W-2 wages into line 1z, total income and AGI — see the footing note on /wages above for why line 1a could not be fixed without it.

Fact.Name: Primary filer has W2 Wages greater than 0
Fact.Description: Whether primary filer has wages greater than 0

The primary filer's total HSA contributions reported on their W-2s (box 12, code W): an ADDEND of Form 8889 line 9. Cents preserved, NOT rounded — this is not a printed line.
This is the row the audit table never named, found by re-deriving that audit mechanically with the per-filer collection ALIASES resolved back to their declaring item fact. What shipped here until this unit was the class defect written as literally as it can be written: CollectionSum(Round(x)) — Sigma round(x_i) with the Round INSIDE the sum — and it was a DOUBLE round, because /formW2s/*/employerHsaContributionsRounded was already /formW2s/*/employerHsaContributions wrapped in Round. i1040gi page 23 governs verbatim: include cents when adding, round off only the total.
THE ROUND NOW HAPPENS EXACTLY ONCE, AND NOT HERE. hsa:/filers/*/hsaContributionsW2sTotal is Form 8889 line 9 and already wrapped this fact in its own Round, so the fix is this total summing the cents-bearing addend /formW2s/*/employerHsaContributionsUnrounded with NO Round of its own — the /primaryFilerWages shape — and NO hsa.xml edit.
THE SECOND, SEPARATE DEFECT IN THIS PAIR IS CLOSED IN THE SAME COMMIT, as its own annotation demanded: the twin /secondaryFilerTotalHsaContributionsFromW2s had NO inner Round, so the two per-filer aggregates computed one quantity by two different expressions, agreeing only because the item fact was pre-rounded and the primary's inner Round was therefore inert. Both filers now read the same expression over the same addend.
Corpus exposure, measured directly and not inherited: ZERO. No committed scenario carries cents in box 12 code W (32 files, 38 W-2 entries, all whole dollars), and the six files with two reporting W-2s put one on each spouse. The fix is byte-identical on today's corpus — no resolved value moves, and the only snapshot movement is the addend fact's own added rows.

Whether the primary filer has HSA contributions reported on their W-2s — that is, whether HIS Form 8889 line 9 is nonzero.
FLOW-GATE BRANCH, STATED RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE FOUND. Moving cents into /primaryFilerTotalHsaContributionsFromW2s moves the quantity this GreaterThan-zero gate tests, and this gate fans out across seventeen read sites in hsa.xml — so leaving it untouched would have shipped a FLOW change disguised as a rounding change — the same trap refused on interest:/interestReports/*/taxWithheld for the same reason.
THE CONSERVATIVE BRANCH WAS TAKEN: the gate is wrapped in Round, so it keeps testing the WHOLE-DOLLAR quantity it has always tested, which is exactly Form 8889 line 9 (hsa:/filers/*/hsaContributionsW2sTotal). The rejected branch — reading the cents-bearing subtotal directly — would open a Form 8889 whose line 9 reads 0 for a lone $0.40 box-12 code-W entry.
The branch is conservative, not inert, and the residue is deliberate: the gate now reads Round(Sigma x) where it read Sigma round(x). Those differ only when every contribution is under half a dollar AND they add to half a dollar or more, in which case line 9 genuinely is 1 and the gate genuinely should fire. The gate tracks the printed line in every case, which is a stronger invariant than it carried before. Pinned in both directions by tests/nodes/ty2025/formW2s/w2-hsa-box12w-single-w2-subdollar-gate-tracks-line9.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer wages, salaries, tips, etc.
Fact.Description:
The secondary filer's own W-2 box-1 total, less the box 1 wages she excludes under section 931 or 933 (/secondaryFilerW2s/*/possessionExcludedWages): an ADDEND of the Form 1040 line-1 chain and the wage term of her Form 2441 and EIC earned income. Cents preserved, NOT rounded — this is not a printed line.
This is the secondary-filer mirror of /primaryFilerWages; see that fact for the full statement of the reading and for why no Round belongs here.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer has W2 wages greater than 0
Fact.Description: Whether secondary filer has wages greater than 0

Fact.Name: Primary filer's box 12 code R total — Form 8853 line 1, cents preserved
Fact.Description:
The primary filer's employer contributions to Archer MSAs, summed across that filer's W-2s with the cents intact. This is Form 8853 line 1 for that filer, which Form 8889 line 4 then reads.
THE PER-FILER SPLIT IS THE RIGHT ADDEND BOUNDARY and it is the same boundary /primaryFilerTotalHsaContributionsFromW2s draws for box 12 code W: Form 8853 Part I is completed per spouse ("If you are filing jointly and both you and your spouse have high deductible health plans with self-only coverage, complete a separate Part I for each spouse"), so each filer's code-R amounts belong to that filer's own line 1. The joint-return fold-in that Form 8889 line 4 prescribes — "If you or your spouse had family coverage under an HDHP at any time during 2025, also include any amount contributed to your spouse's Archer MSAs" — is applied downstream in hsa.xml, not here, so this fact stays one filer's own figure.
NO ROUND HERE, on purpose: the addends carry cents and the single Round happens at the printed line 4 (hsa:/filers/*/hsaLine4ArcherMsaContributions), per i1040gi page 23. Complete-safe 0 on every W-2 that never answered box 12 code R, which is every W-2 committed to this repo today — so this fact resolves 0 for every existing scenario and moves nothing.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's box 12 code R total — Form 8853 line 1, cents preserved
Fact.Description:
The secondary filer's employer contributions to Archer MSAs, summed across that filer's W-2s with the cents intact. This is Form 8853 line 1 for that filer, which Form 8889 line 4 then reads.
THE PER-FILER SPLIT IS THE RIGHT ADDEND BOUNDARY and it is the same boundary /secondaryFilerTotalHsaContributionsFromW2s draws for box 12 code W: Form 8853 Part I is completed per spouse ("If you are filing jointly and both you and your spouse have high deductible health plans with self-only coverage, complete a separate Part I for each spouse"), so each filer's code-R amounts belong to that filer's own line 1. The joint-return fold-in that Form 8889 line 4 prescribes — "If you or your spouse had family coverage under an HDHP at any time during 2025, also include any amount contributed to your spouse's Archer MSAs" — is applied downstream in hsa.xml, not here, so this fact stays one filer's own figure.
NO ROUND HERE, on purpose: the addends carry cents and the single Round happens at the printed line 4 (hsa:/filers/*/hsaLine4ArcherMsaContributions), per i1040gi page 23. Complete-safe 0 on every W-2 that never answered box 12 code R, which is every W-2 committed to this repo today — so this fact resolves 0 for every existing scenario and moves nothing.

The SECONDARY filer's total HSA contributions reported on their W-2s (box 12, code W): the spouse twin of /primaryFilerTotalHsaContributionsFromW2s, and the addend of HER Form 8889 line 9 — each spouse files their own Form 8889. The name said "Primary filers" until its audit pass read it; the body has always summed /secondaryFilerW2s.
See /primaryFilerTotalHsaContributionsFromW2s for the class defect, the reading, the authority and the measured corpus exposure. This half also carried the pair's SECOND defect: it had no inner Round where the primary did, so one quantity was computed by two expressions. Landed together, as that annotation required.

Whether the secondary filer has HSA contributions reported on their W-2s — that is, whether HER Form 8889 line 9 is nonzero. Carries the same flow-gate branch as /hasPrimaryFilerHsaContributionsFromW2s; see that fact for the reading, the rejected alternative and the residue.

The total amount of HSA contributions reported on the TPs W2s.
Both operands are PRINTED LINES, so this adds them as printed. Each spouse files their own Form 8889, so an MFJ return has TWO line 9s, and the printed-operand model says a printed operand chain adds printed operands — hence Round on each per-filer subtotal here rather than one Round over the pair. Whole dollars out, which is what keeps the /hasHsaContributionsOnW2 gate below testing the same kind of quantity it always tested (see /hasPrimaryFilerHsaContributionsFromW2s for the flow-gate branch this follows).
Whether we already know the TP has HSA contributions reported on their W2

Fact.Name: Social Security taxes withheld
Fact.Description:
W-2 box 4 (OASDI) plus box 6 (Medicare) tax withheld, summed across all W-2s. NOTE: this is only the employee-FICA-withholding leg of the §24(d)(2) "social security taxes" definition used by the Schedule 8812 Part II-B (3-or-more-qualifying-children) ACTC method — it does NOT include the one-half self-employment-tax and Additional Medicare Tax components that §24(d)(2) also adds. The one-half SE-tax component (Schedule 8812 line 22 / Schedule 1 line 15) is NOT missing from the Part II-B computation: the consumer ctcOdc:/socialSecurityOverEitc adds scheduleSE:/selfEmploymentTaxDeduction to this fact itself . The Additional Medicare Tax leg of line 21 is ALSO no longer uncovered : this fact is now consumed by ctcOdc:/sched8812Line21, which is the i1040s8 "Additional Medicare Tax and RRTA Tax Worksheet" — this fact supplies only its lines 1 and 2 (boxes 4 and 6), and that fact adds Form 8959 line 7, subtracts Form 8959 line 22 and adds one-half of Form 8959 line 13. What remains uncovered is the Schedule 2 lines 5/6/13 legs of line 22 — disclosed on /socialSecurityOverEitc, not here. Do not read this fact alone as the §24(d)(2) total.
ROUNDING : the box-4 and box-6 amounts are summed WITH CENTS and this combined total is rounded ONCE, here. Before this fix each per-W-2 box was rounded first and the rounded items were summed — the sum-of-rounded-addends defect fixed on the Form 8959 box-5/box-6 totals and fixed on Form 1040 lines 1a/1z. This fact was the last named OPEN row of its audit that still summed rounded W-2 items. The per-W-2 facts /formW2s/*/oasdiWithholding and /formW2s/*/medicareWithholding are UNCHANGED in value — both are MeF exports standing for one document's printed box — so the blast radius is exactly this total and its one reader, ctcOdc:/sched8812Line21, which is NOT repointed and simply consumes the corrected value.
⚠ THIS FACT BREAKS its "single-W-2 returns are provably unchanged" RULE, and the audit's blanket statement of it is WRONG here. That rule holds for a total whose addends are one CollectionSum — with a single item Round(x) = Round(Σx). This total is NOT that shape: it draws on TWO boxes per W-2, and the pre-fix formula rounded each of those 2N box amounts separately. A return with exactly ONE W-2 therefore still presented TWO rounded addends — its own box 4 and its own box 6 — and can still move by $1. Two of the three corpus cases this fix moves carry a single W-2: box 4 = 10,918.20 and box 6 = 8,213.37 gives 10,918 + 8,213 = 19,131 before and Round(19,131.57) = 19,132 after. The number of documents is the wrong test for this fact; the number of separately-rounded addends is.

Fact.Name: Primary Filer W2s
Fact.Description: The W2s that belong to the primary filer

Fact.Name: Primary Filter W2s Count
Fact.Description: How many W2s does the primary filer have?

Fact.Name: Primary Filer Total Social Security Wages
Fact.Description: Sum of Social Security Wages across Primary Filer W2s. Each addend (/formW2s/*/oasdiWagesForKnockoutCalculation) already sums the unrounded box 3 + box 7 twins per W-2, so this CollectionSum rounds once, after the total, rather than summing pre-rounded per-employer addends.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's total social security tax withheld (Form(s) W-2 box 4)
Fact.Description:
Sum of box 4 (social security tax withheld) across the PRIMARY filer's W-2s. The withholding twin of /primaryFilerTotalOasdiWagesForKnockout, and built to that fact's shape deliberately: a bare CollectionSum over the same /primaryFilerW2s filtered collection.
WHY PER FILER AND NOT A GRAPH-WIDE SUM, which is the only way to get this fact wrong: OASDI is capped PER PERSON, and the Schedule 3 line 11 test the aggregate exists for reads "If you, or your spouse if filing a joint return, had more than one employer". A single Sum over every W-2 on a joint return would let one spouse's under-cap position mask the other's over-cap one, or invent an excess where neither filer exceeded the base. The node test formW2s/w2-per-filer-oasdi-withholding-split-mfj pins that divergence: 9,300 and 4,650 to two different filers, where the graph-wide 13,950 matches neither.
COMPLETE-SAFE WITHOUT A WRAPPER, and that is a property of the inputs rather than an omission. /formW2s/*/oasdiWithholding is /formW2s/*/oasdiWithholdingUnrounded rounded, and that fact already carries the IsComplete/Switch that resolves an unanswered box 4 to $0 — so every addend is Complete and a CollectionSum over an empty filtered collection is $0. Adding an IsComplete/Switch here would be divergence from the wage twin for no gain; formW2s/w2-per-filer-oasdi-withholding-unanswered-complete-safe pins it instead of asserting it.
CONSUMED BY NOTHING TODAY — exported, not wired. THE PURPOSE THIS PARAGRAPH USED TO CLAIM IS RETIRED, because the consuming unit landed and declined it. It read that this pair is "the additive first half of the Schedule 3 line 11 excess-OASDI credit"; schedule3: /primaryFilerTotalOasdiWithholdingForExcess then shipped as that addend instead, and its Description states the reason plainly — this pair sums UNCAPPED box 4, so it could not have been the input to a correct line 11 under ANY rounding decision (the per-employer section 3101 ceiling is applied by /formW2s/*/oasdiWithholdingForExcessCalculation before the sum). What survives is the per-FILER framing below, which is still correct and still the only way to get a box-4 aggregate right; what does not survive is the claim to be line 11's input.
THE ROUNDING CHOICE THIS FACT DISCLOSED IS NOW DECIDED, CENTS-PRESERVING. It previously summed the WHOLE-DOLLAR item fact /formW2s/*/oasdiWithholding, so N W-2s contributed N separately rounded addends — the sum-of-rounded-addends shape i1040gi page 23 forbids for any amount built by adding ("include cents when adding the amounts and round off only the total"), and the same shape fixed on Form 8959 lines 1/19, on Form 1040 line 25a and the boxes-4+6 total /socialSecurityTaxesWithheld, and on Form 1040 lines 1a/1z. It now sums /formW2s/*/oasdiWithholdingUnrounded.
NO ROUND BELONGS ON THIS TOTAL, and that is a decision inherited rather than invented: schedule3:/primaryFilerTotalOasdiWithholdingForExcess adjudicated exactly this call for the line-11 addend — "THE DECISION IS CENTS-PRESERVING, ROUND ONCE AT LINE 11" — and this fact is the same quantity one cap short of that one. It is an ADDEND, not a printed line, so it takes the /primaryFilerWages shape: bare CollectionSum over the cents-bearing sibling, rounding deferred to whichever line consumes it. The per-W-2 item fact /formW2s/*/oasdiWithholding keeps its own Round and its exported value is unchanged.
WHAT MOVED, STATED PRECISELY BECAUSE THE USUAL BOUND DOES NOT APPLY HERE. For a total that rounds, Round(x) = Round(Sigma x) makes a single-W-2 return provably unchanged. THIS TOTAL CARRIES NO ROUND, so it moves on EVERY return with cents in box 4, including single-W-2 ones: 10,918.20 previously resolved 10,918 and now resolves 10,918.20. Nothing reads this fact, so no computed tax moves anywhere on any return; what moves is this fact's own resolved value. formW2s/w2-per-filer-oasdi-withholding-primary-two-employers carries the flipped pin (13,950.80 now, against the 13,950 the rounded shape reported) and keeps the rejected shape as a named step.

Fact.Name: Secondary Filer W2s
Fact.Description: The W2s that belong to the secondary filer

Fact.Name: Secondary Filter W2s Count
Fact.Description: How many W2s does the secondary filer have?

Fact.Name: Secondary Filer Total Social Security Wages
Fact.Description: Sum of Social Security Wages across Secondary Filer W2s. Exact twin of /primaryFilerTotalOasdiWagesForKnockout — each addend already sums the unrounded box 3 + box 7 twins per W-2, so this CollectionSum rounds once, after the total.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's total social security tax withheld (Form(s) W-2 box 4)
Fact.Description:
Sum of box 4 (social security tax withheld) across the SECONDARY filer's W-2s. Exact twin of /primaryFilerTotalOasdiWithholding — see that fact for the per-filer rationale, the complete-safe argument, the consumed-by-nothing status, the retired claim to be Schedule 3 line 11's addend, and the rounding decision; all of them apply here unchanged, and the two facts must stay the same shape. On a non-MFJ return /secondaryFilerW2s is empty and this resolves $0, Complete.
REPOINTED at /formW2s/*/oasdiWithholdingUnrounded in the same commit as the primary twin, because "the two facts must stay the same shape" is load-bearing rather than decorative: leaving this one summing rounded items would make an MFJ return's two per-filer subtotals answer the same question by two different rules. No Round here either, for the reason stated in full on the primary twin.

Fact.Name: Some filer has combat pay
Fact.Description: Either the primary filer or their MFJ spouse has combat pay on at least one of their W2s.

Fact.Name: Only one filer has combat pay
Fact.Description: Either the primary filer or their MFJ spouse (if MFJ) has combat pay on one of their W2s.

Fact.Name: MFJ Spouse has combat pay
Fact.Description: Whether a TP has an MFJ spouse and that MFJ spouse has combat pay on at least one of their W2s

Fact.Name: MFJ spouse combat pay, cents preserved
Fact.Description: The MFJ spouse's combat pay summed across their W-2s WITH CENTS, zero if the filing status is not MFJ. The spouse twin of /primaryFilerCombatPayUnrounded — the ADDEND that /bothFilersCombatPay and /combatPayAmount (Form 1040 line 1i) sum before rounding once at the line. Do NOT use it as a stand-in for a printed line; it deliberately carries cents. Read /MFJSpouseCombatPay for the whole-dollar per-filer figure.

Fact.Name: MFJ Spouse Combat Pay
Fact.Description:
The amount of combat pay an MFJ spouse has on all of their W2s combined. Returns zero if filing status is not MFJ.
The spouse twin of /primaryFilerCombatPay, and whole at the filer for the same printed-line reason stated there in full. Was a bare CollectionSum over the Round-wrapped item (sum-of-rounded-addends); now rounds the cents-preserving /MFJSpouseCombatPayUnrounded once. Under useSpouseCombatPay and useSpouseNotPrimaryCombatPay this figure IS Form 1040 line 1i, and under every election it is the amount entered on the EIC Step 5 worksheet line 4.

Fact.Name: Only MFJ Spouse has combat pay
Fact.Description: Whether or not ONLY the MFJ Spouse has combat pay on at least one of their W2s and the primary does not

Fact.Name: TP has combat pay
Fact.Description:
Whether a TP has combat pay on at least one of their W2s.
WIDENS THIS GATE, and that is the unit's ONE non-arithmetic consequence, stated here rather than left to be discovered. The threshold is unchanged (still greater than $0 against /primaryFilerCombatPay), but its input stopped being a sum of rounded addends: a filer with TWO W-2s carrying box-12 code Q of $0.30 each used to reach 0 + 0 = 0 and answer FALSE, and now reaches Round(0.60) = 1 and answers TRUE. That propagates to /onlyPrimaryFilerHasCombatPay and /someFilerHasCombatPay, which gate the combat-pay election Switch in eitc, so the election question begins to fire for a population it did not reach before. No committed scenario is affected; the delta store measured 0 changed rows.

Fact.Name: Primary filer combat pay, cents preserved
Fact.Description: The primary filer's combat pay summed across their W-2s WITH CENTS. The ADDEND that /bothFilersCombatPay and /combatPayAmount (Form 1040 line 1i) sum before rounding once at the line. Do NOT use it as a stand-in for a printed line; it deliberately carries cents. Read /primaryFilerCombatPay for the whole-dollar per-filer figure and the reading behind that boundary.

Fact.Name: TP combat pay
Fact.Description:
The amount of combat pay for the primary filer reported on their W2s, whole dollars: /primaryFilerCombatPayUnrounded rounded once.
This was a bare CollectionSum over the Round-wrapped /formW2s/*/combatPay, the sum-of-rounded-addends shape i1040gi page 23 forbids. It now sums the cents-preserving sibling and rounds here, because THIS FACT IS ITSELF A LINE: under usePrimaryCombatPay and usePrimaryNotSpouseCombatPay it is Form 1040 line 1i, and under every election it is the amount entered on the EIC Step 5 worksheet line 4. The rounding boundary sits at the filer here for that printed-line reason and no other; the wages sibling rejected the filer boundary precisely because no per-filer wage line exists, and that distinction is what makes this placement legitimate rather than a repeat of the defect.
THE CDCC READERS ARE DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE. income:/cdccPrimaryFilerCombatPayForCredits and its three siblings read this whole-dollar fact, and that is correct rather than merely convenient: Form 2441 is a PER-SPOUSE earned-income surface (a finding recorded on scheduleSE:/selfEmploymentEarnedIncome), so the per-filer figure is the one its lines want, and it arrives already rounded at its own line. Their VALUES move with this fix, by the same up-to-a-dollar arithmetic as line 1i, but their shape does not.

Fact.Name: Only primary filer has combat pay
Fact.Description: Whether or not ONLY the primary TP has combat pay on at least one of their W2s and the secondary filer does not have combat pay

Fact.Name: Do both filers have combat pay?
Fact.Description: Whether the primary filer and their MFJ spouse has combat pay on at least one of their W2s.

Fact.Name: Both filers combat pay
Fact.Description:
The combined amount of combat pay from both primary filter and MFJ spouse, WITH CENTS.
This is the joint ADDEND, and it is deliberately not a sum of the two whole-dollar per-filer totals. Under useBothCombatPay it is what Form 1040 line 1i rounds, and eitc:/earnedIncomePlusBothTPCombatPay rounds the same figure for the EIC Step 5 worksheet line 4, so the two agree by construction. Adding Round(primary) + Round(spouse) instead rounds twice across one line boundary and can land a dollar above line 1i, which is the footing pathology in its combat pay form. Wired by before that it had no reader at all.

Fact.Name: Combat Pay if Elected
Fact.Description:
The combat pay for line 1i, taking into account whether the user wants to declare it or not.
The Switch arms now read the cents-preserving addends (/primaryFilerCombatPayUnrounded, /MFJSpouseCombatPayUnrounded, /bothFilersCombatPay) so that the Round already sitting on this fact is the ONLY rounding between a W-2's box 12 and the printed line. That is what makes line 1i equal Schedule 8812 line 18b whenever every filer with combat pay elects it; see /primaryFilerCombatPay for the full reading. California TY2025 reads this fact through its stateSystems export (FTB 3514).

Fact.Name: Nontaxable combat pay
Fact.Description:
Nontaxable combat pay. Note: don't go including this on line 1i of the 1040; that box should only be filled in if the taxpayer elects to include combat pay as earned income for purposes of calculating the Earned Income Tax Credit or Child and Dependent Care Credit.
This value is reported on line 18b of schedule 8812, used to calculate ACTC.
Additionally, be careful to appropriately separate spouse and taxpayer combat pay if MFJ. The TP can elect to include neither, either, or both of their combat pay on line 1i.
This was Round(CollectionSum(/formW2s/*/combatPay)) over an item fact that is itself Round-wrapped, the genuine sum-of-rounded-addends defect: Schedule 8812 line 18b is a printed total that adds ("Enter on line 18b the TOTAL amount of nontaxable combat pay that you (and your spouse if filing jointly) received in 2025"), and i1040gi page 23 requires the cents to survive into that sum. It now sums /formW2s/*/combatPayUnrounded and rounds once here.
THE TWO REASONS THE EARLIER ADDEND FIX COULD NOT DO THIS ALONE, and how this fix discharges them:
(1) THE 18b-VS-1i FOOTING TRAP, the same pathology that affects the wages line-1a leg. The same instruction says the amount "will be reported either on line 1i of Form 1040" — line 1i is /combatPayAmount, mef-exported. Repointing THIS total alone would give 18b = Round(Sigma x) while 1i kept Sigma Round(x). This fix therefore moves the per-filer pair with it and routes the useBothCombatPay arm of line 1i through the cents-preserving /bothFilersCombatPay, so both printed lines round the same joint sum exactly once. When every filer with combat pay elects it, 18b = 1i by construction. When only one spouse elects, 18b deliberately EXCEEDS 1i: 18b is all combat pay received, 1i only the elected amount, which is what the instruction says and what the node-test pair pins.
(2) THE EITC TABLE QUESTION, now answered from printed text rather than deferred: the combat pay reaching eitc:/eitcRoundedEarnedIncomeWith*CombatPay stays WHOLE, because the per-filer totals round at the filer (each is itself line 1i under a single-filer election) and the joint arm rounds at the line. The full reading, its rejected alternatives and its honest limits are recorded on /primaryFilerCombatPay.
CORPUS EXPOSURE, MEASURED and RE-MEASURED HERE: zero. Four committed scenarios carry box-12 code Q, none has a filer holding two W-2s, and none carries cents, so the fix is byte-identical on the shipping corpus. The divergence witnesses are the two node tests this unit adds.

Fact.Name: This Form W-2's box 12 code K amount as an addend of the Schedule 2 line 17k total
Fact.Description:
The complete-safe box 12 code K amount of one Form W-2: ../goldenParachuteExciseTax when the filer answered code K, and 0 when they did not. It exists because ../goldenParachuteExciseTax is a bare writable and stays Incomplete on every W-2 with no code K, which is nearly every W-2, so a CollectionSum over the leaf would not resolve on a real return. This module already carries the same shape for the box 12 codes A, B, M and N under the name ../uncollectedBox12TaxAddend, and the naming follows it.
CENTS PRESERVED. This arc became reachable once the code K arm of /formW2s/*/knockoutBox12Code retired. THE OLD BODY read ../goldenParachuteExciseTaxRounded, so every W-2 rounded to whole dollars BEFORE the CollectionSum. That is double rounding, and it is exactly what the i1040gi page-23 rule forbids: "If you have to add two or more" / "amounts to figure the amount to enter on" / "a line, include cents when adding the" / "amounts and round off only the total." (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 23). The named model this fact's own Description points at, ../uncollectedBox12TaxAddend, states the same rule and preserves cents for the same reason; this fact diverged from it. MEASURED, not argued: two W-2s carrying code K amounts of $1,200.50 and $800.50 printed $2,002 at line 17k (1201 + 801) where the printed instruction gives $2,001 (2,001.00 rounded once). NO COMMITTED VALUE MOVES — every committed fixture and scenario answers code K in whole dollars or not at all, where per-W-2 rounding and the single Round agree, so tests/nodes/ty2025/formW2s/s2-r35-line17k-golden-parachute-total stays byte-identical at 1200.00. The single Round still sits on /schedule2Line17kGoldenParachutePaymentsTax. WHY THE DEFECT WAS INVISIBLE UNTIL NOW: until this unit any positive code K knocked the return out, so no filer could reach line 17k at all. ../goldenParachuteExciseTaxRounded is untouched and keeps its MeF export, which is a per-W-2 whole-dollar box 12 statement value and a different question from the line 17k addend.

Fact.Name: Total W-2 code K excise tax before line rounding
Fact.Description: Sum the existing per-W-2 code K tax addends with cents intact. An unanswered or empty W-2 collection contributes zero. This is already tax and no 20% rate applies to it.

Fact.Name: Candidate whole-dollar combined excess-parachute tax
Fact.Description: Round W-2 code K tax plus 20% of total NEC box 3 payments. Dollar multiplication rounds fractional cents, so the printed-line fact checks this candidate against the exact half-dollar threshold before using it.

Fact.Name: Five times the exact combined excess-parachute tax
Fact.Description: Five times W-2 code K tax plus total NEC box 3 payments. This scaled quantity is exact at cent precision and compares the candidate's half-dollar boundary without dividing or rounding the tax. It is an internal comparison amount, not a printed tax or a second intake.

Fact.Name: Schedule 2 line 17k, the 20 percent excise tax on excess golden parachute payments
Fact.Description:
Schedule 2 line 17k: the sum of every Form W-2's box 12 code K amount, the 20 percent excise tax on excess golden parachute payments, summed with cents intact through the complete-safe ../goldenParachuteExciseTaxAddend and rounded ONCE here at the printed entry line, because the bare leaf is Incomplete on a W-2 with no code K. It lives in formW2s because that is the source form module, following /schedule2Line13UncollectedBox12Tax, which is the same shape for the box 12 codes A, B, M and N. The IsComplete guard on /formW2s makes it resolve 0 rather than Incomplete on a return with no W-2.
THE AMOUNT IS THE TAX ITSELF, so nothing on the return applies a rate to it: IRC 4999(a), "There is hereby imposed on any person who receives an excess parachute payment a tax equal to 20 percent of the amount of such payment" (26 U.S.C. 4999, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section4999&num=0&edition=2024), and i1040gi's own line 17k instruction, "Line 17k. If you received an excess" / "parachute payment (EPP), you must pay" / "a 20% tax on it. This tax should be" / "shown in box 12 of Form W-2 with code" / "K." (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 114).
THIS FACT IS THE LINE 17k ADDEND of /line18OfSchedule2, which taxCalculations:/line21OfSchedule2 reads and Form 1040 line 23 prints; the addend preserves cents and the single Round is the one here, per i1040gi page 23 — see ../goldenParachuteExciseTaxAddend's own CENTS PRESERVED paragraph for the measured old-to-new. THE GAP THIS LINE STILL HAS: the same i1040gi passage continues "If you received a Form 1099-NEC," / "the tax is 20% of the EPP shown in" / "box 3. Enter this amount on line 17k." — this sum is Form W-2 only, and there is no 1099-NEC excess-parachute fact anywhere in this dictionary. A filer whose EPP arrived on a Form 1099-NEC is not refused and not charged; that population is a named gap, not a modelled one. The line now combines the W-2 tax with 20% of schedule2:/form1099NecExcessParachutePaymentsTotal. The NEC amount is a payment; the W-2 amount remains tax. Both the Schedule 2 line 18 total and its printed line 17k field consume this fact. Final rounding is half up at the combined line: if cent rounding lifted the candidate across a half-dollar boundary, the exact comparison against five times the tax reduces the candidate by one dollar. All inputs are nonnegative; an unanswered NEC collection contributes zero and preserves the W-2 result.

Fact.Name: Form W-2 box 12 printed codes
Fact.Description: The code letters Form W-2 box 12 prints, A through II, spelled as printed (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/iw2w3--2025.pdf, page 19, "Report in box 12 any items that are listed as codes A through II"; the code list, lines 1332-1533). The option set of the four box 12 slot code writables. It is the PRINTED vocabulary, deliberately distinct from /w2Box12CodeOptions, whose options name this module's per-code fact leaves (a screen picker, a consumer's vocabulary). There is no code I, O, U, X or CC.

Fact.Name: VOID (Form W-2)
Fact.Description: Form W-2 VOID checkbox, printed at the head of Copy A and Copy D only (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/fw2--2025.pdf, page 2, "VOID"; the General Instructions: "VOID. Check this box when an error is made on Form W-2 and you are voiding it because you are going to complete a new Form W-2" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/iw2w3--2025.pdf, page 16)). SCREEN SPEC: a reader transcribes the box as printed; true when checked. An unchecked or unanswered box means the employer did not void this statement. The box is on the employer's SSA and file copies, not on Copies B, C and 2 the employee files with, so a keyed Copy B leaves it unanswered. UNANSWERED POSTURE: complete-safe, nothing reads it. WHAT THE ANSWER FEEDS: nothing federal today; a voided W-2 is one the employer excludes from its Form W-3 totals (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/iw2w3--2025.pdf, page 16), and a reader that sees it checked should tell the person the statement was voided. Intake only.

Fact.Name: Employee's first name and initial
Fact.Description: Form W-2 box e, "Employee's first name and initial" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/fw2--2025.pdf, page 2), the name cell as the employer printed it. SCREEN SPEC: free text, transcribed as printed. The employee is one of this return's filers (../filer), and the return's own name facts stay the name of record; this cell is what the STATEMENT says, which is what an SSA name mismatch is read against (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/iw2w3--2025.pdf, page 16, "Enter the name as shown on your employee's social security card"). Fact.Name: This W-2's printed box 12 slots disagree with its box 12 amounts by code
Fact.Description: True when at least one box 12 entry (../box12Entries, the printed slots 12a-12d and any continuation) has a code answered and, for some code A through II, the entry amounts carrying that code do not add up to the amount recorded for that code (an unanswered amount counts as zero on both sides). The two record the same printed box, so a disagreement is a transcription error that blocks submission through /hasW2ValidationErrors until the filer corrects one side. A W-2 whose slots are not transcribed is not tested.

Fact.Name: This W-2's box 12 entry amounts with code W, complete safe
Fact.Description: The sum of the answered amounts of this W-2's box 12 entries whose answered code is W; $0 when none is or the list is unanswered. Read by ../box12SlotsDisagreeWithCodedAmounts (its code W leg) and the formW2s constraint overlay's code W check against ../employerHsaContributions.

Fact.Name: This W-2's box 12 entry amounts with code D, complete safe

Fact.Name: Form W-2 box 12 entries

RECONCILIATION, not a rewiring: this module already records box 12 BY CODE (one Dollar writable per code letter, picked through ../../writableBox12Code), and those per-code leaves stay the federal consumers; the entries here are the printed box, compared against them by ../../box12SlotsDisagreeWithCodedAmounts.
