Fact.Name: Form W-2AS box 12 entries
Fact.Description: Form W-2AS box 12, the code-and-amount grid printed as slots 12a through 12d (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/fw2as--2025.pdf, page 2): one item per coded entry the statement reports, in the order printed. Item 1 prints in slot 12a, item 2 in 12b, item 3 in 12c and item 4 in 12d; an entry beyond the fourth prints on an attached continuation statement (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/iw2w3--2025.pdf, page 19, right column: Copy A takes no more than four box 12 items, while "you may enter more than four items in box 12 when using an approved substitute" form on the other copies). SCREEN SPEC: a list on each Form W-2AS, "Box 12: add each code and amount shown", one row per printed entry with its code (A through II) and its amount; the slot order means nothing ("the codes do not relate to where they should be entered in boxes 12a through 12d", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/iw2w3--2025.pdf, page 19). UNANSWERED POSTURE: complete-safe; a list never answered reads as no entries. WHAT IT FEEDS: ../blocksForm1040Computation, through each entry's ../box12Entries/*/blocksForm1040Computation: an entry with a printed code other than DD, or a positive amount with no code, refuses the statement (every coded box 12 leg reads /formW2s only; code DD is informational). Otherwise stored for a reader, the territorial return and the state and local returns.

Fact.Name: Box 12 entry code
Fact.Description: The CODE of one Form W-2AS box 12 entry (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/fw2as--2025.pdf, page 2, the "Code" cell of slots 12a-12d): the code letter(s) printed beside the amount, one of A through II (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/iw2w3--2025.pdf, page 19), on the same printed option set as Form W-2 (formW2s:/w2Box12PrintedCodeOptions); transcribed, not classified. Item 1 of the list prints in slot 12a, item 2 in 12b, and so on. SCREEN SPEC: "Code", a picker of the printed codes A through II, asked on each box 12 row. Validation: one of the printed codes. UNANSWERED POSTURE: complete-safe; a row with an amount and no code is read as an uncoded amount. WHAT THE ANSWER FEEDS: this entry's ../blocksForm1040Computation, and through it the statement's refusal test.

Fact.Name: Box 12 entry amount
Fact.Description: The AMOUNT of one Form W-2AS box 12 entry (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/fw2as--2025.pdf, page 2, the amount cell of slots 12a-12d), paired with ../writableCode on the same row. SCREEN SPEC: "Amount", the dollar amount printed beside the code, asked on each box 12 row. Validation: Dollar, Min $0. UNANSWERED POSTURE: complete-safe; an unanswered amount is not an assertion of zero. WHAT THE ANSWER FEEDS: this entry's ../blocksForm1040Computation, and through it the statement's refusal test.

Fact.Name: Statutory employee
Fact.Description: Form W-2AS box 13, "Statutory" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/fw2as--2025.pdf, page 2): the box 13 "Statutory employee" checkbox; true when checked, an unchecked or unanswered box means not checked. SCREEN SPEC: transcribed as printed, one Form W-2AS item per statement received. UNANSWERED POSTURE: complete-safe; nothing reads it. WHAT THE ANSWER FEEDS: nothing federal today. This collection is its own document, not a /formW2s item, because a Form W-2AS does not report wages subject to U.S. income tax withholding (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/iw2w3--2025.pdf, page 4, "Do not use these forms to report wages subject to U.S. income tax withholding"), and whether American Samoa wages reach Form 1040 depends on bona fide residence (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p570.pdf, page 16 (Bona Fide Resident of American Samoa)), a named successor that reads filers:/filers/*/isBonaFidePossessionResident. Stored for a reader, the territorial return and the state and local returns.

Fact.Name: Form W-2AS box 13 "Retirement plan" checked on a statement that is not VOID
Fact.Description: True when this Form W-2AS's box 13 "Retirement plan" box is answered checked and the statement is not VOID; false otherwise, including when box 13 is unanswered. The Form 1040 instructions take the box 13 "Retirement plan" box as the sign that "you were covered by a plan at work" for the IRA deduction (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 96), and the W-2 instructions govern Forms W-2AS, W-2GU and W-2VI too (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/iw2w3--2025.pdf, page 4). Read by /primaryFilerTerritorialFormW2RetirementPlanChecked and its secondary twin for iraDeduction's coverage test.

Fact.Name: Form W-2GUs
Fact.Description: Form W-2GU: Guam Wage and Tax Statement. One item per statement received. Box 1 of every statement not VOID reaches Form 1040 line 1a and line 1z (/territorialFormW2WagesUnrounded); box 2 never reaches line 25a. /knockoutTerritorialFormW2 refuses the return where the statement needs a form, credit or residence answer this dictionary does not carry.

Fact.Name: Employee
Fact.Description: Which filer on this return received this Form W-2GU. SCREEN SPEC: ask "Whose Form W-2GU is this?" (a filer on the return), first, on every item. UNANSWERED: the Placeholder is the primary filer.

Fact.Name: Form W-2GU belongs to primary filer
Fact.Description: Whether this Form W-2GU belongs to the primary filer. IsComplete-first Switch with a literal FALSE default: an UNANSWERED ../filer, or a single-filer return where filers:/primaryFiler resolves to nothing, is complete-safe false.

Fact.Name: Form W-2GU belongs to secondary filer
Fact.Description: Whether this Form W-2GU belongs to the secondary filer. IsComplete-first Switch with a literal FALSE default: an UNANSWERED ../filer, or a single-filer return where filers:/secondaryFiler resolves to nothing, is complete-safe false.

Fact.Name: Forms W-2GU addressed to the primary filer
Fact.Description: The Forms W-2GU that belong to the primary filer (belongsToPrimaryFiler) and are not VOID (isReported). Read by the Schedule 3 line 11 excess social security computation and by case (5) of /knockoutTerritorialFormW2; a VOID statement is not a document the filer submitted and does not count as a statement or an employer.

Fact.Name: Form W-2GU employee's social security number
Fact.Description: Form W-2GU box a, "Employee's social security number" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/fw2gu--2025.pdf, page 2). Fact.Name: VOID (Form W-2GU)

A reader transcribes it; true when checked, and an unchecked or unanswered box means the statement was not voided (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/iw2w3--2025.pdf, page 16). SCREEN SPEC: transcribed as printed, one Form W-2GU item per statement received. UNANSWERED POSTURE: complete-safe; nothing reads it. WHAT THE ANSWER FEEDS: nothing federal today. This collection is its own document, not a /formW2s item, because a Form W-2GU does not report wages subject to U.S. income tax withholding (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/iw2w3--2025.pdf, page 4, "Do not use these forms to report wages subject to U.S. income tax withholding"), and whether Guam wages reach Form 1040 depends on bona fide residence (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p570.pdf, pages 24-25 (a U.S. citizen or resident alien other than a bona fide resident of Guam files with the United States and includes tax withheld by either)), a named successor that reads filers:/filers/*/isBonaFidePossessionResident. Stored for a reader, the territorial return and the state and local returns.

UNANSWERED POSTURE: on a statement that is not VOID, refused by /knockoutTerritorialFormW2. WHAT THE ANSWER FEEDS: no Form 1040 line; a non-zero amount refuses the return through ../blocksForm1040Computation (the credit route is not built). This collection is its own document, not a /formW2s item, because a Form W-2GU does not report wages subject to U.S. income tax withholding (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/iw2w3--2025.pdf, page 4, "Do not use these forms to report wages subject to U.S. income tax withholding"), and whether Guam wages reach Form 1040 depends on bona fide residence (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p570.pdf, pages 24-25 (a U.S. citizen or resident alien other than a bona fide resident of Guam files with the United States and includes tax withheld by either)). Item 1 prints in slot 12a, item 2 in 12b, item 3 in 12c and item 4 in 12d; an entry beyond the fourth prints on an attached continuation statement (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/iw2w3--2025.pdf, page 19, right column: Copy A takes no more than four box 12 items, while "you may enter more than four items in box 12 when using an approved substitute" form on the other copies). SCREEN SPEC: a list on each Form W-2GU, "Box 12: add each code and amount shown", one row per printed entry with its code (A through II) and its amount; the slot order means nothing ("the codes do not relate to where they should be entered in boxes 12a through 12d", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/iw2w3--2025.pdf, page 19). UNANSWERED POSTURE: complete-safe; a list never answered reads as no entries. WHAT IT FEEDS: ../blocksForm1040Computation, through each entry's ../box12Entries/*/blocksForm1040Computation: an entry with a printed code other than DD, or a positive amount with no code, refuses the statement (every coded box 12 leg reads /formW2s only; code DD is informational). Fact.Name: Form W-2VI box 12 entries
Fact.Description: Form W-2VI box 12, the code-and-amount grid printed as slots 12a through 12d (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/fw2vi--2025.pdf, page 2): one item per coded entry the statement reports, in the order printed. Item 1 prints in slot 12a, item 2 in 12b, item 3 in 12c and item 4 in 12d; an entry beyond the fourth prints on an attached continuation statement (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/iw2w3--2025.pdf, page 19, right column: Copy A takes no more than four box 12 items, while "you may enter more than four items in box 12 when using an approved substitute" form on the other copies). SCREEN SPEC: a list on each Form W-2VI, "Box 12: add each code and amount shown", one row per printed entry with its code (A through II) and its amount; the slot order means nothing ("the codes do not relate to where they should be entered in boxes 12a through 12d", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/iw2w3--2025.pdf, page 19). UNANSWERED POSTURE: complete-safe; a list never answered reads as no entries. WHAT IT FEEDS: nothing federal: every Form W-2VI that is not VOID already refuses the return through ../blocksForm1040Computation (Form 8689 not built). Stored for a reader, the territorial return and the state and local returns.

Item 1 of the list prints in slot 12a, item 2 in 12b, and so on. SCREEN SPEC: "Code", a picker of the printed codes A through II, asked on each box 12 row. Validation: one of the printed codes. UNANSWERED POSTURE: complete-safe; a row with an amount and no code is read as an uncoded amount. WHAT THE ANSWER FEEDS: nothing federal; stored for a reader, the territorial return and the state and local returns.

Fact.Name: Form W-2AS is marked VOID
Fact.Description: TRUE when this Form W-2AS's VOID box is answered checked. An unanswered VOID box is an unchecked one (the employer's copies alone print it), so this is complete-safe FALSE when unanswered. A voided statement reports nothing to Form 1040.

Fact.Name: Form W-2AS box 1 reported on Form 1040 line 1a
Fact.Description: This Form W-2AS's box 1, floored at zero with cents kept, as it joins Form 1040 line 1a (/wages) and line 1z. $0 when the statement is VOID. $0 when box 1 is unanswered, and that is NOT a silent zero: an unanswered box 1 on a statement that is not VOID makes ../blocksForm1040Computation TRUE and /knockoutTerritorialFormW2 refuses the return.

Fact.Name: Form W-2AS box 11 of the primary filer, on a statement whose box 1 reaches Form 1040
Fact.Description: This Form W-2AS's box 11 (nonqualified plans) when the statement belongs to the primary filer (../belongsToPrimaryFiler) and is not VOID, floored at $0; $0 otherwise, and $0 when box 11 is unanswered. Box 11 amounts are also in box 1 (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/iw2w3--2025.pdf, page 19), and box 1 of a non-VOID statement joins Form 1040 line 1a (../wagesReportedOnForm1040Unrounded). Pub. 590-A treats as IRA compensation "any amount properly shown in box 1 ... provided that amount is reduced by any amount properly shown in box 11" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p590a.pdf, page 6), and the W-2 instructions govern Forms W-2AS, W-2GU and W-2VI too (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/iw2w3--2025.pdf, page 4). Summed by /primaryFilerTerritorialNonQualifiedPlans for iraDeduction's compensation.

Fact.Name: Form W-2AS box 1 reported for the primary filer
Fact.Description: ../wagesReportedOnForm1040Unrounded when this Form W-2AS belongs to the primary filer (../belongsToPrimaryFiler, complete-safe), else $0. The addend of /primaryFilerTerritorialFormW2WagesUnrounded.

Fact.Name: This Form W-2AS's employer issued another statement to the same filer, complete safe
Fact.Description: True when this statement's employer identification number (box b) is answered and equals box b of another Form W-2AS of the same filer, or box b of one of its filer's Forms W-2. CHECKED: a Form W-2AS sharing an employer within its own collection, or with a Form W-2 (the RRTA-compensation gap that keeps a territorial withholding case off the Medicare leg of /knockoutTerritorialFormW2 can leave a same-employer American Samoa statement unrefused). NOT CHECKED: sharing with a Form W-2GU, Form W-2VI or Form 499R-2/W-2PR (an American Samoa employer issuing one of those to the same filer is not a population this dictionary can source). False when box b is unanswered, when the owner is unanswered, or when a list is not answered.

Fact.Name: This Form W-2AS box 12 entry carries something Form 1040 cannot yet route
Fact.Description: TRUE when this box 12 entry has a printed code other than DD, or a positive amount with no code: every coded box 12 leg of this dictionary reads /formW2s only, and code DD (the cost of employer-sponsored health coverage) is informational. FALSE otherwise, including an entry with neither a code nor a positive amount. Complete-safe: each term is an IsComplete-first All. Read by the statement's ../../blocksForm1040Computation through a Filter over ../box12Entries.

Fact.Name: This Form W-2AS carries something Form 1040 cannot yet route
Fact.Description: TRUE when this Form W-2AS is not VOID and any of: box 1 unanswered (the wages cannot be reported); box 2 unanswered or above $0 (the U.S. return may take a foreign tax credit for American Samoa tax (Form 1116), a leg not built for this statement); box 7 social security tips above $0 (the tip legs read /formW2s only); box 13 Statutory employee or Retirement plan checked (the Schedule C route and the IRA active-participant test read /formW2s only); or a box 12 entry (../box12Entries) with a code other than DD, or a positive amount with no code (every coded box 12 leg reads /formW2s only; code DD is informational). Box 13 Third-party sick pay does not refuse: it is a payer-side indicator and the sick pay is already in box 1. Complete-safe: every term is an IsComplete-first All or a literal. Read by /territorialFormW2ItemBlocksComputation.

Summed by /secondaryFilerTerritorialNonQualifiedPlans for iraDeduction's compensation.

No shares-employer sibling: a shared-employer refusal on a statement that already always refuses would add nothing.

A bona fide USVI resident files with the USVI. Complete-safe: every term is an IsComplete-first All or a literal. Read by /territorialFormW2ItemBlocksComputation.

Fact.Name: The return has a territorial Form W-2 that is not VOID
Fact.Description: TRUE when any answered Form W-2AS, W-2GU or W-2VI collection holds a statement that is not VOID. Complete FALSE on a return whose territorial collections are unanswered (the IsComplete guard heads each All).

Fact.Name: A territorial Form W-2 carries something Form 1040 cannot route
Fact.Description: TRUE when any territorial statement's blocksForm1040Computation is TRUE.

Fact.Name: Every filer answered No to the possession residence question
Fact.Description: TRUE only when filers:/primaryFilerAttestedNotAPossessionResident and filers:/secondaryFilerAttestedNotAPossessionResident are both TRUE: the primary filer was asked and answered No, and the spouse side is cleared (no spouse, or the spouse was asked and answered No). Silence is not a No. Reading BOTH sides also covers the joint-return rule: a joint return is filed with the jurisdiction of the spouse with the greater AGI, so a bona fide resident spouse can move the whole return.

Fact.Name: Guam wages reach the Form 5074 gross income test
Fact.Description: TRUE when /guamWagesOnFormW2GusUnrounded is $5,000 or more. Form 5074 must be attached when AGI is $50,000 or more AND gross income from Guam sources is $5,000 or more; Form 5074 is not built, and the dictionary sources no other income to Guam, so the guard keys on the Guam wages alone. It OVER-refuses the cell with AGI under $50,000, which is named.

Fact.Name: Combined Medicare wages reach the Additional Medicare Tax threshold
Fact.Description:
TRUE when Form W-2 box 5 plus territorial box 5 exceeds /maxMFSMedicareWages (the lowest Form 8959 threshold). Reads /formW2s only, so territorial box 5/6 are safe to leave out only below this threshold; Form 8959 is not built for a territorial statement. Return-level sum, so this is conservative for a per-filer test.
THE MEDICARE LEG IS THE ONLY LEG HERE. An OASDI wage-base leg (Form W-2 box 3 plus territorial box 3 against /maxOasdiWagesOnMultipleW2sForOnePerson) is NOT part of this fact: territorial box 4 and box 3 now join the Schedule 3 line 11 withholding and wage test directly (schedule3: /formW2Ass/*/socialSecurityTaxWithheldForExcess and its Gu/Vi twins, each capped per statement at the one-employer maximum; each statement an employer), and the narrower risk a blanket OASDI leg would have caught — one employer's territorial box 4 across two statements crediting more than the annual maximum — is its own refusal instead, case (5) of /knockoutTerritorialFormW2 (/formW2Ass/*/sharesEmployerWithAnotherStatementOfItsFiler and its Gu twin). The Medicare leg stays because Form 8959 reads /formW2s only; a territorial statement's box 5/6 are not counted toward the Additional Medicare Tax threshold anywhere else.

Fact.Name: Territorial Form W-2 the return cannot yet carry
Fact.Description: Refuses a return with a territorial Form W-2 (W-2AS, W-2GU or W-2VI, not VOID) whose treatment this dictionary cannot compute. SCREEN TEXT: "We can't file your return here because it includes a Form W-2AS, W-2GU or W-2VI that needs forms or questions we don't support yet (for example, Form 8689 for U.S. Virgin Islands wages, Form 5074 for Guam income, a credit for territorial income tax withheld, a bona fide territory residence, or one territorial employer's social security tax withheld split across two statements above the annual maximum). You may need to file with the territory or use other software." TRUE when /territorialFormW2Present and any of: (1) /territorialFormW2FilersCleared is FALSE (a filer did not answer the possession residence question, or answered Yes: a bona fide resident of Guam or the USVI files with the territory, a bona fide American Samoa resident excludes the wages under section 931, and the five-territory question does not name the territory); (2) /territorialFormW2ItemBlocksComputation (every Form W-2VI, territorial tax withheld, and the box 1 / 7 / 12 / 13 entries named on each blocksForm1040Computation); (3) /territorialFormW2GuamForm5074Possible; (4) /territorialFormW2FicaThresholdReached (Medicare wages only); (5) a Form W-2AS or W-2GU with box 4 above zero shares its employer with another of the same filer's statements in that collection or with a Form W-2, and that filer's uncapped box 4 on that collection is above the one-employer maximum: the credit cannot be claimed for one employer's over-collection and this return does not yet group one employer's statements across a territorial collection and Form W-2. What is COMPUTED is everything else: every filer answered No, and each statement is a Form W-2GU or W-2AS with box 2 zero and nothing else to route; its box 1 reaches line 1a and 1z, and its box 3/box 4 join the Schedule 3 line 11 test and withholding. The wages reach /wages whether or not this guard fires, so no population silently omits them.

Fact.Name: Form W-2CM documents
Fact.Description: Source documents received on Form W-2CM, one item per received document. The collection records the printed document without computing or changing federal tax. Its items are available for state returns and document transcription.

Fact.Name: Form W-2CM document owner
Fact.Description: The primary or secondary filer to whom this Form W-2CM is addressed as employee. An unanswered owner is Incomplete; no primary-filer default is assumed. This link supplies ownership for the two attribution facts, not another copy of the printed identifying number.

Fact.Name: Form W-2CM belongs to primary filer
Fact.Description: Whether this Form W-2CM belongs to the primary filer. The owner link and the corresponding filer must both be complete before they are compared. An unanswered owner or an absent primary filer produces false. No federal tax computation reads this attribution; it is exported for document ownership.

Fact.Description: Whether this Form W-2CM belongs to the secondary filer. The owner link and the corresponding filer must both be complete before they are compared. Fact.Name: The employer on this Form 499R-2/W-2PR is the U.S. Government or one of its agencies
Fact.Description: Whether the employer that issued this Form 499R-2/W-2PR (box 1, the employer's name) is the United States Government or one of its agencies. SCREEN SPEC: ask "Is the employer on this Form 499R-2/W-2PR the U.S. Government or a U.S. Government agency?" (yes / no), on every Form 499R-2/W-2PR item that shows wages or other compensation. Help text: the Government of Puerto Rico, its municipalities and public corporations are not the U.S. Government; answer yes only for a federal employer. Validation: Boolean. UNANSWERED: treated as possibly yes, so a bona fide resident of Puerto Rico whose statement shows compensation is refused by /knockoutForm499R2W2PrAmountsNotCarried until it is answered. WHAT IT FEEDS: ../mayReportUsGovernmentCompensation and so /knockoutForm499R2W2PrAmountsNotCarried: a bona fide resident excludes Puerto Rico source income under section 933, but not pay for services as an employee of the United States, and the return does not carry those wages. Stored for the state and local returns.

Fact.Name: Form 499R-2/W-2PR amounts the return cannot carry
Fact.Description: You entered a Form 499R-2/W-2PR that this return cannot carry, so it cannot be filed here. That happens in five cases. (1) The statement shows wages or other compensation and you have not said you were a bona fide resident of Puerto Rico for 2025: a U.S. citizen or resident alien who is not a bona fide resident reports Puerto Rico wages on the U.S. return (with a foreign tax credit for the Puerto Rico tax), and this return does not yet figure the U.S. amount of those wages or the credit. (2) Your Medicare wages and tips, counting box 22 of your Forms 499R-2/W-2PR, are above the Additional Medicare Tax threshold for your filing status: Form 8959 counts box 22 like Form W-2 box 5, and this return does not add it yet. (3) One Form 499R-2/W-2PR shows more than $200,000 in box 22, so the employer may have withheld Additional Medicare Tax that Form 8959 would credit. (4) You were a bona fide resident of Puerto Rico and a statement that shows compensation is from the U.S. Government or one of its agencies, or you have not said whether it is: a bona fide resident does not exclude pay for services as an employee of the United States, so those wages are taxed on the U.S. return (with a foreign tax credit for the Puerto Rico tax on them), and this return does not yet figure them or the credit. (5) A Form 499R-2/W-2PR with social security tax withheld in box 21 comes from an employer that gave you another Form W-2 or Form 499R-2/W-2PR, and your social security tax withheld is above $10,918.20: the credit for excess social security tax cannot be claimed for one employer's over-withholding, and this return does not yet combine one employer's statements across the two forms.
